definition_zh: 变体；变种；变异株；异体；不同的
definition_en: a form or version that differs from the standard one, or differing from a standard
core_image: 同一份说明书的两个版本，页边多了几处不同的批注
scene: 同一份说明书在两个城市印出了两种版式。编辑指着南方版说： The southern edition uses a variant of the same logo.
sceneCN: 这里指「变体／略有不同的版本」（第 1 个义项：与标准形式不同的一个版本）；句意为南方版使用了同一标志的一个变体。

不同的；变异的；替代的

senses.title: A differing version
senses.definition: a version of something that differs in some details from the standard
senses.definitionCN: 在某些细节上与标准不同的一个版本
senses.example: The southern edition uses a variant of the same logo.
senses.exampleCN: 南方版使用了同一标志的一个变体。
senses.why: Variant treats difference as a countable thing: one standard, and beside it another version.
senses.whyCN: variant 把差异当成可数的东西：有一个标准，旁边另有某个版本。

senses.title: A genetic variant
senses.definition: a version of a gene or DNA sequence that differs from the reference
senses.definitionCN: 与参照序列不同的基因或脱氧核糖核酸序列版本
senses.example: This genetic variant lowers the risk of heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 这种遗传变异型降低心脏病风险。
senses.why: Genetics applies the general idea of a differing version to a segment of DNA, counted against a reference genome.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学把「不同版本」的一般观念用到一段脱氧核糖核酸上，以参照基因组为基准来计数。

senses.title: A viral variant
senses.definition: a virus lineage that carries a set of mutations distinguishing it from others
senses.definitionCN: 携带一组突变、因而与其他谱系不同的病毒谱系
senses.example: The new variant spreads faster but causes milder illness.
senses.exampleCN: 新变异株传播更快，但致病较轻。
senses.why: Public health needs a countable label for lineages, so the general word becomes the standard term for a mutated virus.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生需要给谱系一个可数的标签，于是这个一般词成为指变异病毒的标准术语。

senses.title: A spelling variant
senses.definition: an accepted alternative spelling of the same word
senses.definitionCN: 同一个词被接受的另一种拼写
senses.example: The dictionary lists both spellings as variants.
senses.exampleCN: 词典把两种拼写都列为异体。
senses.why: Language tolerates two written forms of one word, and the noun marks them as equal versions rather than errors.
senses.whyCN: 语言容许同一个词有两种书写形式，这个名词把它们标为平等的版本，而非错误。

senses.title: An alternative product version
senses.definition: a model or configuration of a product that differs from the main one
senses.definitionCN: 与主版本不同的产品型号或配置
senses.example: The cheaper variant lacks the heated seats.
senses.exampleCN: 较便宜的版本没有加热座椅。
senses.why: Manufacturers sell one design in several configurations, and each configuration is a variant of the same model.
senses.whyCN: 厂商把同一设计做成多种配置，每种配置都是同一型号的一个变体。

senses.title: A textual variant
senses.definition: a reading in a manuscript or edition that differs from another reading
senses.definitionCN: 手稿或版本中与另一读法不同的文字
senses.example: Editors recorded every variant across the surviving copies.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑记录了现存各本中的每一处异文。
senses.why: Manuscripts of one work drift apart, and scholarship needs a word for each differing reading.
senses.whyCN: 同一作品的手稿会彼此偏离，学术研究需要一个词来指每一种不同的读法。

senses.title: Differing as an adjective
senses.definition: showing variation from a standard form
senses.definitionCN: 表现出与标准形式不同的
senses.example: A variant reading changes the meaning of the line.
senses.exampleCN: 一个不同的读法会改变这一行的意思。
senses.why: As an adjective the word describes the form itself rather than naming a version as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词描述形式本身，而不是把某个版本作为名词命名出来。

senses.title: A nonstandard form
senses.definition: a form used by some speakers but not accepted as the standard
senses.definitionCN: 被部分使用者采用、但未被接受为标准的形式
senses.example: The teacher marked the variant as acceptable but informal.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把这个非标准形式标为可接受但不正式。
senses.why: Once a standard is fixed, everything beside it is called a variant, whether or not it is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 一旦标准被固定，旁边的一切都被称为变体，不论它是否错误。

intro.en: Variant comes from Latin variantem, the present participle of variare 'to change', and entered English through French in the eighteenth century. The genetic and viral senses are modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: variant 来自拉丁 variantem，即 variare「改变」的现在分词，经法语在 18 世纪进入英语。遗传学与病毒学的义项属现代用法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Variare 'to change' has the present participle varians, variant-. English variant is this participle used as adjective and noun.
items.cn: variare「改变」的现在分词是 varians（词干 variant-）。英语 variant 就是这个词形，兼作形容词与名词。

items.en: The verb rests on varius 'varied, various', the same adjective behind variety and various.
items.cn: 这个动词建立在 varius「多样的、不同的」之上，同一形容词也衍生 variety 与 various。

items.en: French variant passed into English in the eighteenth century as a term for a differing form, especially in printing and manuscripts.
items.cn: 法语 variant 在 18 世纪进入英语，指不同的形式，尤用于印刷与手稿。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was adopted for differing gene sequences and, later, for viral lineages.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词被用来指不同的基因序列，后来又指病毒谱系。

items.en: Modern English uses variant as a neutral noun for any alternative version and as an adjective meaning 'differing'.
items.cn: 现代英语中 variant 作中性名词指任何替代版本，也作形容词表示「不同的」。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first dates): the deeper origin of Latin varius is disputed, and the earliest English use of variant is dated only within the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：拉丁 varius 的更深来源有争议；variant 在英语中的最早使用只能定在 18 世纪之内。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same vary family that are easily swapped; group two holds general words for alternative versions.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 vary 词族、容易被混用的词；第二组是表示替代版本的一般词。

entries.definition: The fact or degree of changing; variant is a countable version, while variation may be uncountable.
entries.definitionCN: 指变化的事实或程度；variant 是可数的版本，而 variation 可以不可数。

entries.definition: A range of different kinds, or a cultivated plant kind; it does not mean one alternative version.
entries.definitionCN: 指多种不同种类，或栽培品种；不表示某一个替代版本。

entries.definition: A numerical measure of spread, or a formal disagreement; it is not a physical version.
entries.definitionCN: 指离散程度的数值，或正式分歧；不是具体的版本。

entries.definition: A statistical variable; the spelling differs by one letter but the field is mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 指统计变量；拼写只差一个字母，但所属领域是数学。

entries.definition: Any form of something from a particular point of view; it is broader and needs no standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指从某一角度看某事物的任一形式；范围更广，也不预设标准。

entries.definition: The shape or arrangement of something; it names structure rather than difference from a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指事物的形状或安排；命名结构，而非与标准的差异。

entries.definition: A genetic lineage within a species; in microbiology it is close to variant but usually implies a cultured stock.
entries.definitionCN: 指物种内的一个遗传谱系；在微生物学中接近 variant，但通常暗示培养的品系。

entries.definition: One published form of a text; a variant is a differing reading, while an edition is the whole printing.
entries.definitionCN: 指文本的一个出版形式；variant 是一处不同读法，edition 是整个印本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: vari- 'different' + -ant 'the one being': the one that differs.
normal.cn: vari-「不同」+ -ant「处于某种状态的那一个」：不同的那一个。

normal.en: The family runs vary, variation, variable, variability, various.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 vary、variation、variable、variability、various。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: genetic variant, new variant, spelling variant.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出专业义：遗传变异型、新变异株、拼写异体。

normal.en: A variant is one countable version; variation is the fact or range of difference.
normal.cn: variant 是一个可数的版本；variation 是差异的事实或范围。

normal.en: In manuscripts, editors list variants; in genetics, databases list variants.
normal.cn: 在手稿研究中，编辑列出异文；在遗传学中，数据库列出变异型。

abstract.en: Picture two keys that open the same door but have different notches.
abstract.cn: 想象两把钥匙能开同一扇门，齿形却不同。

abstract.en: Picture one song released in a radio cut and a longer album cut.
abstract.cn: 想象同一首歌发行了电台版和更长的专辑版。

abstract.en: Picture a map reprinted with one road renamed.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图重印时有一条路改了名。

examples.en: The variant differs from the reference sequence at one position.
examples.cn: 该变异型在参照序列的一个位置上不同。

examples.en: Both variants of the software are still supported.
examples.cn: 该软件的两个版本仍在维护。

examples.en: Historians compare variants of the same letter.
examples.cn: 历史学家比较同一封信的不同文本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维瑞恩特」——同一个东西换了个版本，像同款衣服的另一种颜色 → 变体

root: 拉丁 variare「改变」的现在分词 varians（词干 variant-），出自 varius「多样的」；varius 的更深来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: a standard is fixed, and beside it a differing version is counted, whether in genes, viruses, spelling, products or manuscripts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先有标准，旁边再数出一个不同的版本，可用于基因、病毒、拼写、产品或手稿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two printings of one document with small differences in the margin.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一份文件的两个印本，页边有细小差别。

branches.en: VERSION AND NONSTANDARD FORM: a neutral different version, and one accepted only informally.
branches.cn: 版本与非标准形式：一个是中性的不同版本，一个只在非正式场合被接受。

branches.en: GENES AND VIRUSES: the countable version becomes a DNA sequence or a viral lineage.
branches.cn: 基因与病毒：可数的版本变成一段脱氧核糖核酸序列或一个病毒谱系。

branches.en: WORDS AND TEXTS: spelling and manuscript readings are catalogued as variants.
branches.cn: 文字与文本：拼写与手稿读法被编目为异文。

branches.en: PRODUCTS: one design sold in several configurations.
branches.cn: 产品：同一设计以多种配置出售。

branches.en: ADJECTIVE: the word describes the differing form itself.
branches.cn: 形容词：这个词直接描述那个不同的形式。

intro.en: Variant is a Latin present participle in form: vari- supplies the meaning 'different' and -ant marks the thing that differs.
intro.cn: variant 在形式上是拉丁现在分词：vari- 提供「不同」的意思，-ant 标记那个不同的事物。

latinIntro.en: The same Latin verb variare underlies variation, variable and vary; variant is its participial branch.
latinIntro.cn: 同一拉丁动词 variare 支撑 variation、variable 与 vary；variant 是它的分词分支。

items.structure: Latin varius (varied, different) as a root
items.example: The root opens various and variety.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在 various 与 variety 开头。

items.meaning: the one that is or does
items.meaningCN: 处于某状态或做某事的那一个
items.example: Variant marks the version that differs.
items.exampleCN: variant 标记那个不同的版本。

items.example: The two copies vary in one line.
items.exampleCN: 两个本子在一行上不同。

items.example: Variation across the range is wide.
items.exampleCN: 整个范围内的差异很大。

items.example: The variable affects the final score.
items.exampleCN: 这个变量影响最终得分。

items.example: The variance between samples was small.
items.exampleCN: 样本间的方差很小。

items.example: One variant lacks the final paragraph.
items.exampleCN: 有一个版本缺少最后一段。

items.example: Variability makes forecasting hard.
items.exampleCN: 多变性使预测困难。

items.meaning: not changing; a quantity that stays fixed
items.example: The ratio is invariant under rotation.
items.exampleCN: 这个比值在旋转下不变。

latinEntries.structure: variare, vario, variavi, variatum (verb, first conjugation)

senses.title: Of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心智的：发生在头脑里的事
senses.definition: relating to the mind or to thinking, as opposed to the body
senses.definitionCN: 与心智或思维有关的，与身体相对
senses.example: Reading a map is a mental skill, not a physical one.
senses.exampleCN: 看地图是一项心智技能，而不是体力技能。
senses.why: Mental entered English in the early 15th century from Late Latin mentalis, from Latin mens 'mind'. The adjective simply marks what happens inside the head.
senses.whyCN: mental 于 15 世纪初从晚期拉丁语 mentalis 进入英语，源自拉丁语 mens“心智”。这个形容词只标记在头脑内部发生的事。

senses.title: Psychological health
senses.titleCN: 心理的：情绪与心理状态
senses.definition: relating to a person's emotional and psychological condition
senses.definitionCN: 与一个人的情绪与心理状况有关的
senses.example: The clinic offers mental health services for teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为青少年提供心理健康服务。
senses.why: Mental health is recorded from 1803. Once the mind has a health of its own, the adjective moves from describing thought to naming a field of care.
senses.whyCN: mental health 自 1803 年有记录。一旦心智有了自己的健康，这个形容词就从描述思维转为命名一个照护领域。

senses.title: Of the soul
senses.titleCN: 精神的：心灵层面的旧义
senses.definition: in older use, relating to the soul or the inner, spiritual life
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，与灵魂或内在精神生活有关的
senses.example: The old prayer asks for mental peace rather than bodily comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的祷文求的是心灵的安宁，而不是身体的舒适。
senses.why: In Middle English, mental also meant 'of the soul, spiritual'. Before medicine divided mind from body, the word covered the whole inner life.
senses.whyCN: 在中古英语里，mental 也意为“灵魂的、精神的”。在医学把心智与身体分开之前，这个词覆盖的是整个内在生活。

senses.title: Intellectual effort
senses.titleCN: 脑力的：劳动落在头脑上
senses.definition: requiring or involving thought and intellect rather than physical work
senses.definitionCN: 需要或涉及思考与智力，而非体力劳动
senses.example: Mental labour can exhaust a person as surely as lifting does.
senses.exampleCN: 脑力劳动照样能把人累垮，就像搬运一样。
senses.why: From the 1520s the word meant 'done or performed in the mind'. Effort shifts from the muscles to the brain, and the adjective follows it.
senses.whyCN: 自 16 世纪 20 年代起，这个词意为“在头脑中完成的”。力气从肌肉转到大脑，形容词也跟着转了过去。

senses.title: Done inside the head
senses.titleCN: 默算默想：不外化的过程
senses.definition: performed silently in the mind, without writing or speaking
senses.definitionCN: 不写出来也不说出来，在脑中默默完成
senses.example: She did the sum mentally and wrote only the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她心算了那道题，只写下答案。
senses.why: Mental arithmetic keeps the whole operation invisible. The adjective marks work that leaves no trace until the result appears.
senses.whyCN: 心算把整个运算过程藏了起来。这个形容词标记的是那种直到结果出现才留下痕迹的劳动。

senses.title: Psychiatric illness
senses.definition: relating to psychiatric illness, its institutions and its patients
senses.definitionCN: 与精神疾病、其机构及病人有关的
senses.example: He was admitted to a mental hospital after the second episode.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次发作后，他被送进了精神病院。
senses.why: Mental patient is recorded from 1859 and mental hospital from 1891. Once institutions exist, the adjective becomes a clinical address.
senses.whyCN: mental patient 自 1859 年有记录，mental hospital 自 1891 年有记录。一旦机构存在，这个形容词就变成了一个临床门牌号。

senses.title: Slang: crazy
senses.titleCN: 口语：发疯的、脑子有毛病的
senses.definition: in informal British English, crazy or wildly unreasonable
senses.definitionCN: 在英式口语中，指发疯的或极不合理的
senses.example: You are mental if you think that jump is safe.
senses.exampleCN: 你要是觉得那样跳下去没事，那你真是疯了。
senses.why: The slang sense 'crazy, deranged' is recorded from 1927, probably from combinations such as mental patient. A clinical label leaks into the playground.
senses.whyCN: “发疯的、精神错乱的”这一俚语义自 1927 年有记录，很可能来自 mental patient 一类的组合。临床标签漏进了操场。

senses.title: Slang noun: a mad person
senses.definition: in informal British English, a person who is mentally ill or behaves wildly
senses.definitionCN: 在英式口语中，指精神失常或行为失控的人
senses.example: The driver was a complete mental and should never have been on the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那个司机完全是个疯子，根本就不该上路。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun for a person who has the quality. Here the medical label becomes an insult.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词直接变成指人的名词。在这里，医学标签变成了骂人的话。

senses.title: Legal and clinical capacity
senses.definition: in law and medicine, used of a person's ability to understand, decide and be responsible
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与医学中，指一个人理解、决定与承担责任的能力
senses.example: The court asked whether the accused had the mental capacity to understand the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 法院问的是被告是否有心智能力理解这项指控。
senses.why: Law needs the mind as a measurable fact, not a metaphor. Mental capacity turns the inner life into something a form can record.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要把心智当成可测量的事实，而不是比喻。mental capacity 把内在生活变成表格上可以填写的东西。

intro.en: Mental comes from Latin mens (genitive mentis) 'mind' through Late Latin mentalis. Its root is PIE *men- 'to think'. The medical and middle senses of the letters 'ment' belong to other roots entirely. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mental 经由晚期拉丁语 mentalis 来自拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”。它的词根是原始印欧语 *men-“思考”。字母 ment 所对应的“医疗”与“中间”两族词，属于完全另外的词根。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded as 'in, of, or pertaining to the mind; characteristic of the intellect'. It came from Late Latin mentalis 'of the mind', an adjective built on Latin mens.
items.cn: 最早记录为“在心智之中的、属于心智的；智力特征的”。它来自晚期拉丁语 mentalis“心智的”，是建立在拉丁语 mens 之上的形容词。

items.en: Latin mens (genitive mentis) means 'mind, intellect, thought, intention'. The stem ment- is what English borrows in mental, mentality and dementia.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）意为“心智、智力、思想、意图”。英语在 mental、mentality、dementia 中借入的正是词干 ment-。

items.en: The root *men- (1) means 'to think'. It also lies behind English mind, a native Germanic cousin of Latin mens rather than a borrowing from it.
items.cn: 词根 *men-（第一支）意为“思考”。它也是英语 mind 的来源——mind 是拉丁语 mens 在日耳曼语里的本族表亲，而不是从拉丁语借来的。

items.en: Mental also meant 'of the soul, spiritual' in Middle English. The word covered the inner life before medicine separated mind from body.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，mental 也意为“灵魂的、精神的”。在医学把心智与身体分开之前，这个词覆盖的是整个内在生活。

items.en: The sense 'done or performed in the mind' is recorded, the sense behind mental arithmetic and mental rehearsal.
items.cn: 记录到“在头脑中完成的”这一义项，它正是 mental arithmetic 与 mental rehearsal 背后的意思。

items.en: Mental health is recorded from 1803, mental illness from 1819, mental patient from 1859 and mental hospital from 1891. The slang sense 'crazy, deranged' follows in 1927, probably from those combinations.
items.cn: mental health 自 1803 年有记录，mental illness 自 1819 年，mental patient 自 1859 年，mental hospital 自 1891 年。俚语义“发疯的、精神错乱的”在 1927 年出现，很可能来自这些组合。

note.en: The first group separates the native noun mind, the derived noun mentality, the adverb and the person word. The second group places mental against the adjectives it is most often confused with, including its usual opposite.
note.cn: 第一组区分本族名词 mind、派生名词 mentality、副词与指人的词。第二组把 mental 与最常混淆的几个形容词放在一起，包括它通常的对立面。

entries.definition: the faculty of thinking, or a person's thoughts and attention. It is the native English cousin of Latin mens, while mental is the borrowed adjective built on mens.
entries.definitionCN: 思维的能力，或一个人的想法与注意力。它是拉丁语 mens 在英语里的本族表亲，而 mental 是建立在 mens 上的借入形容词。

entries.definition: a typical way of thinking, or the level of a person's intellectual power. It is a countable pattern of mind, not a synonym of mental.
entries.definitionCN: 典型的思维方式，或一个人的智力水平。它是可数的思维模式，不是 mental 的同义词。

entries.definition: in the mind, or with respect to the mind. It modifies a verb ('mentally rehearsed') where mental would modify a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在脑中，或就心智而言。它修饰动词（如 mentally rehearsed），而 mental 修饰名词。

entries.definition: a performer who appears to read minds, or a believer in mentalism. It never means 'a mental person'.
entries.definitionCN: 看似能读心的表演者，或心灵主义的信奉者。它从不表示“精神失常的人”。

entries.definition: relating to the study of the mind and behaviour, or to a person's inner emotional state. It is more technical than mental and often replaces it in careful writing.
entries.definitionCN: 与心理学研究或一个人的内在情绪状态有关的。它比 mental 更技术化，在严谨写作中常替代 mental。

entries.definition: relating to the medical treatment of mental illness. It names the clinic, while mental can still be a neutral word for the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 与精神疾病的医学治疗有关的。它命名的是临床，而 mental 仍可中性地指心智。

entries.definition: relating to the intellect and its exercise, especially in learning and analysis. It praises the work of the mind; mental merely locates it.
entries.definitionCN: 与智力及其运用有关的，尤其在学习与分析中。它赞赏头脑的工作；mental 只标明位置。

entries.definition: relating to the body rather than the mind. The pair mental and physical organises everyday talk about health, training and fatigue.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体而非心智有关的。mental 与 physical 这一对词组织起了日常关于健康、训练与疲劳的说法。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin mens (genitive mentis) 'mind', PIE *men- 'to think', the English cousin mind, and the family mentality, mentally, dementia.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”、原始印欧语 *men-“思考”、英语表亲 mind，以及 mentality、mentally、dementia 词族。

normal.en: mens, mentis means 'mind'. Mental is the adjective of that noun: whatever belongs to the mind.
normal.cn: mens、mentis 意为“心智”。mental 就是这个名词的形容词：一切属于心智的东西。

normal.en: The root *men- means 'to think', and it also gives the native English word mind. Mental is the borrowed twin of mind.
normal.cn: 词根 *men- 意为“思考”，它也给出英语本族词 mind。mental 是 mind 的借入版双胞胎。

normal.en: mentality is mental plus -ity: not the mind itself but its habitual shape, a way of thinking.
normal.cn: mentality 是 mental 加 -ity：不是心智本身，而是它习惯性的形状，即一种思维方式。

normal.en: mentally is the adverb: it tells you where the work happens, as in mentally rehearsed.
normal.cn: mentally 是副词：它告诉你工作发生在哪里，如 mentally rehearsed（在脑中排练）。

normal.en: Keep the fixed phrases straight: mental health, mental illness, mental hospital. These are clinical and neutral, not insults.
normal.cn: 把固定搭配记准：mental health、mental illness、mental hospital。这些是临床且中性的说法，不是骂人。

abstract.en: Picture a lit lamp inside a skull. Nobody outside can see the flame, only its light falling on what the person does next.
abstract.cn: 想象颅骨里点着一盏灯。外面的人看不见火焰，只看见火光落在这个人接下来的动作上。

abstract.en: The same lamp can be described in three registers: mental is everyday, psychological is scientific, psychiatric is clinical. One flame, three vocabularies.
abstract.cn: 同一盏灯可以用三种语域描述：mental 是日常的，psychological 是科学的，psychiatric 是临床的。一团火焰，三套词汇。

abstract.en: Because the light is invisible, the word is easily abused: it can name care, or it can become an insult. The phrase tells you which.
abstract.cn: 正因为光看不见，这个词容易被滥用：它可以命名照护，也可以变成侮辱。是哪个，要看它所在的短语。

examples.en: The injury healed in weeks, but the mental scars took years.
examples.cn: 伤在几周内就愈合了，但心理上的伤痕花了好几年。

examples.en: He ran the whole interview in his head, mentally correcting every answer.
examples.cn: 他在脑子里把整场面试过了一遍，逐条修正每个回答。

examples.en: The report calls for better mental health care in rural schools.
examples.cn: 报告呼吁改善乡村学校的心理健康照护。

dict_mnemonic.text: “门头儿”——门头儿里面亮着一盏灯，那是脑子里转个不停的念头 → mental 心理的、心智的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”，词根 *men- 意为“思考”，核心是“在头脑内部进行的活动”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mental, all lit by one lamp inside the skull: first it simply marks where thought happens, then it names health, effort, silence, illness, insult and finally a legal fact.
sensesIntro.cn: mental 的九个义项都被颅骨里的同一盏灯照亮：它先只标记思考发生的位置，继而命名健康、劳动、沉默、疾病、辱骂，最后成为一种法律事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp burning inside a skull, visible only through what the person does.
core.cn: 核心意象：颅骨里燃着的一盏灯，只能通过这个人的举动被看见。

branches.en: THE INNER LIFE: the oldest sense marks the mind, and once also the soul, as a region distinct from the body.
branches.cn: 内在生活：最老的义项标记心智——也曾标记灵魂——作为区别于身体的一个区域。

branches.en: HEALTH: mental health gives the inner life a condition that can be cared for.
branches.cn: 健康：mental health 给内在生活一个可以被照护的状态。

branches.en: EFFORT: thought becomes labour, and labour can be done with no visible trace.
branches.cn: 劳动：思考变成劳作，而这种劳作可以不留可见痕迹。

branches.en: ILLNESS: the clinical label builds hospitals and patients, and then turns into a playground insult.
branches.cn: 疾病：临床标签建起了医院与病人，随后又变成操场上的骂人话。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: slang decides who is crazy; law decides who can understand and be responsible.
branches.cn: 判断：俚语义断定谁疯了；法律则断定谁能理解、谁能负责。

intro.en: Mental is Latin ment- 'mind' plus the adjective ending -al. The suffix is productive in English; the stem ment- is not a free word, but it recurs in mentality, dementia and mentalize.
intro.cn: mental 是拉丁语 ment-“心智”加形容词词尾 -al。这个后缀在英语里能产；词干 ment- 不能单独成词，却在 mentality、dementia、mentalize 中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin mentalis was built on Latin mens (genitive mentis) 'mind', from PIE *men- 'to think'. The same root supplies dementia (de- 'away' + mens) and the native English mind.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 mentalis 建立在拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”之上，源自原始印欧语 *men-“思考”。同一词根也给出 dementia（de-“离开”+ mens）以及英语本族词 mind。

items.meaning: of or relating to the mind
items.meaningCN: 心理的；心智的（ment- 心智 + -al 形容词词尾）
items.example: The test measures mental rather than manual speed.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测的是思维速度，而不是手的速度。

items.meaning: a way of thinking; mental character
items.meaningCN: 心态；思维方式（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The team's mentality changed after the first win.
items.exampleCN: 首胜之后，球队的心态变了。

items.meaning: in the mind; with respect to the mind
items.meaningCN: 心理上；在脑中（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She counted the steps mentally before jumping.
items.exampleCN: 起跳前她在心里数了步子。

items.meaning: a mind-reading performer; a believer in mentalism
items.meaningCN: 读心术表演者；心灵主义者（-ist 指人）
items.example: The mentalist guessed the card without touching it.
items.exampleCN: 那位读心术表演者没碰牌就猜中了。

items.meaning: the view that mind or consciousness is fundamental
items.meaningCN: 心灵主义；唯心论（-ism 表学说）
items.example: Mentalism treats consciousness as the basic stuff of reality.
items.exampleCN: 心灵主义把意识当作现实的基本材料。

items.meaning: relating to mentalism or to explanations in mental terms
items.meaningCN: 心灵主义的；用心理术语解释的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: Behaviourists rejected mentalistic explanations.
items.exampleCN: 行为主义者拒斥用心理术语所作的解释。

items.meaning: to understand behaviour as arising from mental states
items.meaningCN: 心智化；把行为理解为心理状态的产物（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: Children learn to mentalize through play.
items.exampleCN: 儿童在游戏中学着理解他人的心理。

items.meaning: a condition in which the mind has gone away
items.meaningCN: 痴呆；认知功能衰退（de- 离开 + ment- 心智 + -ia 状态）
items.example: The early signs of dementia were mistaken for tiredness.
items.exampleCN: 痴呆的早期迹象被误认为是疲劳。

items.meaning: out of one's mind; wildly foolish
items.meaningCN: 精神错乱的；荒唐的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The plan was demented from the first page.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划从第一页起就荒唐透顶。

items.meaning: an object kept as a reminder
items.meaningCN: 纪念物；使人想起某事的物件（源自拉丁语祈使式“记得”）
items.example: He kept the ticket as a memento of the trip.
items.exampleCN: 他把那张票留着，作为那次旅行的纪念。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 失去理智的；精神错乱的

definition_zh: 收获；收割；收成；（努力得到的）成果；采集（数据、细胞、野生资源）
definition_en: the act or season of gathering ripe crops, the crop gathered, the result of effort, or the act of collecting resources
core_image: 一片成熟麦田在短时间内被割倒、捆扎、装车，田里只剩整齐的茬
scene: 麦穗低下头，镰刀从田边推进，捆好的束子一列列码在车上，天色已近黄昏。 The harvest must be brought in before the first storm.
sceneCN: 这里指「把成熟作物收回来」（第 1 个义项：收割庄稼）；句意为必须在第一场暴风雨前完成收获。

pos.zh: 收获；收割；收成；（努力的）成果
收割；采集（数据、细胞、野生资源）

derivatives.zh: harvest + -er（施动者或工具）→ 收割的人；收割机
harvest + -ing（动作名词）→ 收割作业；采集
harvest + -ed（过去分词作形容词）→ 已收割的
harvest + -able（能……的）→ 可收割的；可采集的
post-（之后）+ harvest → 收获后的（语义偏移：指采收之后的处理与储藏）
pre-（之前）+ harvest → 收获前的（语义偏移：指采收之前的田间管理）
harvest + man（人）→ 收割者；盲蛛（语义偏移：一种外形像长腿收割者的蛛形动物）

senses.title: Cut and gather ripe crops
senses.definition: to cut, pick or dig up ripe crops and bring them in
senses.definitionCN: 把成熟作物割下、摘下或挖出并运回
senses.example: They harvest the wheat before the rain breaks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在雨来之前收割小麦。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the decisive act of the farming year: what has grown is finally taken.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是农事年里决定性的动作：长成的东西终于被取走。

senses.title: The act or season of gathering
senses.definition: the work or the time of gathering crops, as in a late harvest
senses.definitionCN: 收集作物的劳作或时段，如晚收
senses.example: The harvest lasted three weeks that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年的收获持续了三个星期。
senses.why: English often turns a season and its main activity into one noun, and harvest names both at once.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一个季节与其主要活动合成一个名词，harvest 同时指两者。

senses.title: The crop that is gathered
senses.definition: the amount of crop produced and gathered in one season
senses.definitionCN: 一季中产出并收上来的作物总量
senses.example: A dry summer cut the harvest by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱的夏天使收成减少了三分之一。
senses.why: By metonymy the act becomes the thing it produces, so people speak of a good or bad harvest.
senses.whyCN: 以转喻方式，行为变成它的产物，于是人们说收成好或坏。

senses.title: The fruit of long effort
senses.definition: the result or reward that comes from sustained work, as in the harvest of years of research
senses.definitionCN: 持续工作带来的结果或回报，如多年研究的成果
senses.example: The book was the harvest of ten quiet years.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是十年静默工作的成果。
senses.why: The agricultural image generalizes: any long investment eventually has a gathering time.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象被一般化：任何长期投入最终都有采收的时候。

senses.title: Collect data in bulk
senses.definition: to gather large amounts of data or information, often automatically
senses.definitionCN: 大量收集数据或信息，常为自动进行
senses.example: The app harvests location data from every user.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用从每位用户那里采集位置数据。
senses.why: Data is treated as a crop: it is already there, and the work is to gather it efficiently.
senses.whyCN: 数据被当作作物：它已经在那里，工作就是高效地把它收上来。

senses.title: Take cells or organs for use
senses.titleCN: 摘取细胞或器官供使用
senses.definition: to remove cells, tissue or organs from a body for medical treatment or research
senses.definitionCN: 从身体中取出细胞、组织或器官，用于治疗或研究
senses.example: Surgeons harvested a nerve from the patient's leg.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生从病人腿部取出一段神经。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the image of taking a living supply from where it grew.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了「从生长处取走活材料」的意象。

senses.title: Gather wild resources
senses.definition: to gather wild plants, shellfish or timber from their natural setting
senses.definitionCN: 从自然环境中采集野生植物、贝类或木材
senses.example: Villagers harvest shellfish at the low tide.
senses.exampleCN: 村民在退潮时采拾贝类。
senses.why: Not everything gathered is planted; the word also covers taking what the wild has produced.
senses.whyCN: 被收走的不都是种下的；这个词也涵盖取走野生环境产出之物。

senses.title: Autumn as the old season word
senses.definition: the season of autumn, the original meaning of the word in Old English
senses.definitionCN: 秋天这一季节，即该词在古英语中的本义
senses.example: In older texts harvest names the season, not only its work.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的文本里，这个词指季节本身，而不只是季节里的活。
senses.why: Old English hærfest meant autumn; the modern crop sense narrowed out of the season when crops were cut.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hærfest 意为秋天；现代作物义是从「收割作物的季节」中收窄出来的。

intro.en: Harvest goes back to Old English hærfest, autumn, from Proto-Germanic harbitas. The same word family survives as German Herbst, autumn. The crop sense narrowed out of the season sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: harvest 可上溯到古英语 hærfest「秋天」，源自原始日耳曼语 harbitas。同族词在德语中保留为 Herbst「秋天」。作物义是从季节义中收窄出来的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hærfest named autumn and also the gathering of crops that filled that season; the two readings were not separated.
items.cn: hærfest 指秋天，也指填满这个季节的收作物；两种读法尚未分开。

items.en: The Germanic form harbitas is reconstructed from the older English and German evidence; it is not directly recorded.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 harbitas 是由较早的英语与德语证据重构出来的，并未被直接记录。

items.en: The word is generally connected with a root meaning to gather or pluck, but the exact Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 这个词一般认为与表示「收集、采摘」的词根有关，但确切的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Middle English kept both autumn and crop readings, while the season sense slowly passed to the Latin-derived word autumn.
items.cn: 中古英语同时保留「秋天」与「作物」两种读法，而季节义慢慢转给拉丁来源的 autumn。

items.en: The verb harvest appears later than the noun and extends the gathering image to data, organs and wild resources.
items.cn: 动词 harvest 比名词出现得晚，并把采集意象扩展到数据、器官与野生资源。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Germanic origin is reconstructed only, and no single Indo-European source is agreed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：日耳曼语之前的来源只有重构形式，学界并未达成单一印欧来源。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to harvest but name different things; group two holds words for taking in what has grown.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近 harvest、却指不同事物的词；第二组是表示「把长成之物收进来」的词。

entries.definition: The modern season word, borrowed from Latin autumnus; it replaced the season sense of harvest but is not related to it.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的季节词，借自拉丁 autumnus；它取代了 harvest 的季节义，但与之并非同源。

entries.definition: One who harvests or a machine that cuts and threshes grain; it is the doer, not the crop or the season.
entries.definitionCN: 收割的人或收割脱粒的机器；它是施动者，不是作物或季节。

entries.definition: A long-legged arachnid, named for its resemblance to a reaper; it is not a person who works in the fields.
entries.definitionCN: 一种长腿蛛形动物，因形似收割者而得名；并不是在田里劳作的人。

entries.definition: A celebration held after the crop is in; it marks the end of harvesting rather than the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 庄稼收完后举行的庆祝；它标记收割结束，而非收割本身。

entries.definition: A plant or plant product grown in quantity; the harvest is the act of taking it in, or its total yield.
entries.definitionCN: 大量种植的植物或植物产品；harvest 是把它收进来的动作，或总产量。

entries.definition: The amount produced by land or by an effort; it is a quantity, while harvest can be the work, the season or the crop.
entries.definitionCN: 土地或努力产出的数量；它是量，而 harvest 可以是工作、季节或作物。

entries.definition: To cut grain by hand or machine; it is the first step of harvesting and does not cover data or organs.
entries.definitionCN: 用手或机器割谷；是收获的第一步，不涵盖数据或器官。

entries.definition: The general verb for bringing scattered things together; harvest is more specific and implies a crop ready to be taken.
entries.definitionCN: 把散落之物聚拢的普通动词；harvest 更具体，暗示作物已到可收之时。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English hærfest meant autumn: the season and its work were one word.
normal.cn: 古英语 hærfest 意为秋天：季节与季节里的活曾是同一个词。

normal.en: The family runs harvest, harvesting, harvester, harvested, harvestable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 harvest、harvesting、harvester、harvested、harvestable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: bring in the harvest, harvest season, harvest festival.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出田间义：把庄稼收回来、收获季节、丰收节。

normal.en: The modern verb extends to data, organs, rainwater and shellfish.
normal.cn: 现代动词扩展到数据、器官、雨水与贝类。

normal.en: German Herbst still means autumn, the lost sense of the English word.
normal.cn: 德语 Herbst 仍指秋天，正是英语这个词丢失的义项。

abstract.en: Picture a field that disappears into stacks and sacks in a single afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田在一个下午里消失，变成一堆堆捆束与一袋袋粮食。

abstract.en: Picture a decade of notes finally tied into one bundle.
abstract.cn: 想象十年的笔记终于被扎成一捆。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pool emptied at low water, every shellfish taken before the sea returns.
abstract.cn: 想象退潮后的潮池被掏空，海水回来之前每一只贝都被取走。

examples.en: The combine harvested the field in two days.
examples.cn: 联合收割机两天就收完了这块田。

examples.en: This year's harvest was the smallest in a decade.
examples.cn: 今年的收成是十年来最少的。

examples.en: Researchers harvest tissue samples from consenting patients.
examples.cn: 研究人员从知情同意的病人身上采集组织样本。

dict_mnemonic.text: harvest 本指秋天，后来专指秋天里最要紧的活——把长熟的东西收回来；于是作物、收成、成果、数据都能「收」。

root: 古英语 hærfest「秋天」，源自原始日耳曼 harbitas；一般认为与表示「收集、采摘」的词根有关，但更早的印欧形式属重构。德语 Herbst「秋天」为同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one moment: ripe growth is cut and carried in, and that moment then becomes a season, a yield, a reward and a way of collecting anything useful.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个时刻展开：成熟之物被割下并运回，这个时刻随后变成季节、产量、回报，以及收集任何有用之物的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ripe field is emptied in a short, decisive burst of work, and the year's growth becomes a store.
core.cn: 核心意象：成熟的田在一阵短促而决定性的劳作中被收空，一年的生长变成一座粮仓。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS TIME: cutting the crop and the weeks in which it is done.
branches.cn: 动作与其时间：割下作物，以及做这件事的那几周。

branches.en: THE SEASON AND ITS STORE: autumn and the amount it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 季节与其储藏：秋天，以及它留下的数量。

branches.en: THE REWARD: any long effort has a gathering day.
branches.cn: 回报：任何长期投入都有采收的一天。

branches.en: THE DATA FIELD: information is gathered like grain.
branches.cn: 数据之田：信息像谷物一样被收走。

branches.en: THE LIVING SUPPLY: cells, organs, shellfish and timber are taken from where they grew.
branches.cn: 活的供应：细胞、器官、贝类与木材都从生长处取走。

intro.en: Harvest is a native Germanic word, not a Latin derivative; its English family is built with ordinary suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: harvest 是日耳曼本族词，并非拉丁派生词；它的英语词族由普通后缀与复合方式构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for this word, so the Latin side is left empty; the family is entirely Germanic and English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁部分留空；其词族完全属于日耳曼语与英语。

items.example: The noun once named the whole season.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词曾命名整个季节。

items.meaning: one who does, or a tool that does
items.example: The suffix builds harvester from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由动词构成 harvester。

items.meaning: a reaper or a harvesting machine
items.example: The harvester cleared the last row at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 收割机在黄昏清完了最后一行。

items.example: Harvesting began before sunrise.
items.exampleCN: 收割在天亮前开始。

items.example: The harvested grain was dried on racks.
items.exampleCN: 收下的谷子在架子上晾干。

items.meaning: ready or able to be gathered
items.example: Only half the stand was harvestable.
items.exampleCN: 只有一半的林分可采伐。

items.example: Postharvest losses were cut by better storage.
items.exampleCN: 更好的储藏减少了收获后的损失。

items.example: Preharvest checks look for mould.
items.exampleCN: 收获前检查寻找霉变。

items.meaning: a reaper; also a long-legged arachnid
items.example: A harvestman crossed the stubble.
items.exampleCN: 一只盲蛛爬过茬地。

definition_zh: 按次序的；依次的；逐步依赖前一步的；顺序存取的；时序的；连续编号的
definition_en: arranged or happening in a fixed order, with each step coming after and depending on the one before
core_image: 装配台上一排螺栓从左到右排开，前一颗拧到位，手才移到下一颗
scene: 装配台上，工人按说明书一步接一步拧紧螺栓，前一颗没到位就不动下一颗。 The assembly steps are sequential, so no bolt is tightened before the one beside it.
sceneCN: 这里指按固定次序、后一步依赖前一步（第 1 个义项：按固定次序排列的）；句意为装配步骤是依次进行的，旁边那颗没拧好之前不会去拧这一颗。图中可辨识物件：成排螺栓、装配说明书、拧紧扳手、到位标记。

pos.zh: 按次序的；依次的；逐步的
（计算机）顺序存取的；（电子）时序的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「依次地；按顺序地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「顺序性」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「顺序；一连串」
由「顺序」一词加动名词尾构成，义为「排序；测序」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「接着发生的」，较少用

senses.title: Arranged in a fixed order
senses.definition: placed or happening in an order where position matters
senses.definitionCN: 按位置有意义的固定次序放置或发生
senses.example: The manual lists five sequential steps, and skipping one breaks the seal.
senses.exampleCN: 说明书列出五个依次进行的步骤，跳过任何一步都会弄坏密封。
senses.why: The Latin stem simply means to follow, so anything that follows in line is called by this word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁词干本义就是「跟随」，凡是在队列里跟着来的都可用它形容。

senses.title: Each step depends on the last
senses.definition: built so that a later step cannot start before the earlier one finishes
senses.definitionCN: 构造上后一步必须等前一步完成才能开始
senses.example: The process is sequential, which is why a delay at the first stage stops everything.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流程环环相扣，所以第一环节一拖，全线都停。
senses.why: Following in time hardens into depending in time: order becomes a condition, not a preference.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的跟随硬化成条件上的依赖：次序从偏好变成了前提。

senses.title: Sequential access in computing
senses.definition: reading stored data in the order it was written rather than jumping to any point
senses.definitionCN: 按写入顺序读取存储数据，而不是直接跳到任意位置
senses.example: A tape drive is a sequential access device, so finding the last file takes the longest.
senses.exampleCN: 磁带机是顺序存取设备，所以找最后一个文件最费时间。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word because the machine must walk through every earlier item to reach the next one.
senses.whyCN: 计算机借用了这个词，因为机器必须走过前面每一项才能到达下一项。

senses.title: Sequential logic in electronics
senses.definition: circuits whose output depends on earlier inputs as well as the present one
senses.definitionCN: 输出不仅取决于当前输入、还取决于先前输入的电路
senses.example: A traffic light controller is built from sequential logic, since its next state depends on the last one.
senses.exampleCN: 交通灯控制器由时序逻辑构成，因为它下一个状态取决于上一个状态。
senses.why: Here the earlier state is remembered inside the circuit, so sequence is stored rather than merely observed.
senses.whyCN: 这里先前状态被电路记住，于是「先后」是被存下来的，而不只是被观察到的。

senses.title: Sequential decision making
senses.definition: choosing step by step, each choice made after seeing the result of the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 一步一步地做选择，每一步都在看到前一步结果之后才定
senses.example: The company used sequential decision making, approving each site only after the previous one opened.
senses.exampleCN: 公司采用序贯决策，前一个门店开业后才批下一个。
senses.why: The sense treats a string of choices as one procedure, which is the point of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把一串选择当成一个程序来看，这正是这个形容词的着力处。

senses.title: Issued one after another
senses.definition: published or released in separate parts rather than all at once
senses.definitionCN: 分几次发布而不是一次性全部放出
senses.example: The journal published the findings in sequential parts over three months.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊用三个月分几次陆续发表这些发现。
senses.why: Release can be ordered in time too, and then the word describes the schedule rather than the content.
senses.whyCN: 发布也能按时间排序，这时词描述的是日程而不是内容。

senses.title: Sequential bilingualism
senses.definition: learning a second language after the first is already established
senses.definitionCN: 在第一种语言已经稳固之后才学第二种语言
senses.example: Sequential bilingualism describes a child who adds English after mastering another home language.
senses.exampleCN: 「先后习得」指孩子先掌握家中另一种语言，之后才加上英语。
senses.why: In language study the order of acquisition is the whole distinction, so the same word does precise work.
senses.whyCN: 在语言研究里，习得的先后就是全部区别，于是同一个词承担了精确的区分。

senses.title: Numbered without gaps
senses.definition: carrying numbers that run on without a break
senses.definitionCN: 号码一个接一个、中间不断开
senses.example: Each sample received a sequential number so the lab could prove none was lost.
senses.exampleCN: 每份样本都得到一个连续编号，实验室据此证明没有丢失任何一份。
senses.why: Numbering is the plainest visible form of order, and the word marks it as unbroken.
senses.whyCN: 编号是最直观可见的次序形式，这个词标出它是不断开的。

intro.en: Sequential comes from Latin sequi, to follow, through sequentia, a following or a sequence. English built the adjective on that stem, and the same root also gives sequence, subsequent and consequence, each taking a different prefix or ending to say what kind of following is meant.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「跟随」，经「跟随、连续」这一名词进入英语。形容词是在该词干上构成的；同一词根还给出「顺序」「随后的」「后果」等词，各自用不同的前缀或词尾说明是哪种跟随。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow, and it stands behind a whole family of words about coming after something.
items.cn: 这个词意为「跟随」，一整族表示「在……之后」的词都由它而来。

items.en: The noun named a following, hence a series of things one after another.
items.cn: 该名词表示「跟随」，因此也指一件接一件的一串事物。

items.en: Church music used the same word for verses appended after the alleluia, an early example of following in order.
items.cn: 教会音乐用同一个词指附加在欢呼词之后的诗节，是「按序接在后面」的早期例子。

items.en: French passed the noun to English, where it named an order of events or of items in a series.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词传给英语，用来指事件或一系列项目的次序。

items.en: English added the adjective ending to the Latin stem in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪给这个拉丁词干加上形容词词尾。

items.en: Computing and electronics took the word for data read in order and for circuits that remember earlier states; the first recorded year of each technical use is uncertain.
items.cn: 计算机与电子学分别用它指按顺序读出的数据与记住先前状态的电路；这两种技术用法各自首见的年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for following; the second group names other ways of coming one after another, and the note separates sequential from subsequent.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「跟随」动词；第二组指其他「一个接一个」的说法，并借以分清「依次」与「随后」。

entries.definition: An order of items or events; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指项目或事件的次序，是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: Coming after something else in time; it adds a prefix meaning under or after, so it points to one later item rather than to an internal order.
entries.definitionCN: 指在时间上紧随某事之后；它加了表示「在下、在后」的前缀，指向某一个较晚的项目而不是内部次序。

entries.definition: A result that follows from an action, with a prefix meaning together with.
entries.definitionCN: 指由某一行动引出的结果，前缀意为「连同」。

entries.definition: Following without a break; it comes from another verb meaning to follow closely, not from the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指连续不断的；出于另一表示「紧跟」的动词，并非同一名词。

entries.definition: Following on; the rare adjective form without the extra ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指接着发生的；不带附加词尾的少用形容词形式。

entries.definition: Following one after another, often with the sense of a series of similar items.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个接一个，常指同类项目构成的系列。

entries.definition: Arranged in a series, one at a time, as with numbers or ports.
entries.definitionCN: 指排成系列的、逐个进行的，如编号或接口。

entries.definition: Arranged according to a rule or plan.
entries.definitionCN: 指按某种规则或计划排好。

entries.definition: Done in stages, with each stage explained or completed before the next.
entries.definitionCN: 指分阶段进行，每阶段完成后再进下一阶段。

entries.definition: Proceeding in a straight line of steps without branching.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿着一条不回头的步骤线推进。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the bolt row, the manual's steps, the tape drive and the unbroken numbering.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用成排螺栓、说明书的步骤、磁带机与不间断的编号。

normal.en: A sequential process is a queue, not a crowd: nobody moves out of turn.
normal.cn: 依次的流程是队列而不是人群：没人能插队。

normal.en: If the first step stalls, every later step waits, because order is also dependence.
normal.cn: 第一步卡住，后面的每一步都等着，因为次序同时是依赖。

normal.en: A tape must walk past every earlier file to reach yours.
normal.cn: 磁带必须走过前面每个文件，才够到你那一个。

normal.en: Sequential numbering leaves no gap, so a missing number is proof of a lost item.
normal.cn: 连续编号不留空档，跳号就证明丢了东西。

normal.en: Sequential is about the order inside a line; subsequent is about one thing landing after another.
normal.cn: 「依次」说的是队列内部的次序，「随后」说的是某物落在另一物之后。

abstract.en: Order is a promise that the next thing will not arrive before the last one has finished.
abstract.cn: 次序是一个承诺：下一件事不会在上件事结束前到来。

abstract.en: A society runs on sequential rules it never notices, until two things try to happen at once.
abstract.cn: 社会靠无数不被注意的先后规则运转，直到两件事试图同时发生。

abstract.en: Following is neutral; the prefix decides whether you follow behind, follow with, or follow on.
abstract.cn: 「跟随」本身是中性的，前缀决定你是跟在后面、跟着一起，还是接着往下。

examples.en: Please follow the sequential steps in the order given, not in the order you prefer.
examples.cn: 请按给出的次序完成这些步骤，而不是按你喜欢的次序。

examples.en: The interview moved through sequential stages, and each stage was scored before the next began.
examples.cn: 面试按阶段依次进行，每一阶段先打分，再进入下一阶段。

examples.en: Files on the old tape are stored in sequential order, so a search can take several minutes.
examples.cn: 旧磁带上的文件按顺序存放，因此检索可能要花好几分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「西宽小」：事情得按「先来后到」排成一列，一步「宽」出格，后面的全乱

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「跟随」的动词，其名词义为「跟随、连续」，形容词即在此词干上构成。同一词根还给出表示「顺序」「随后」「后果」的词；其中表示「随后」的那个加了「在后」的前缀，只指某一个较晚的项目，而这个词指队列内部的先后。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from plain order to technical order: fixed arrangement, step-by-step dependence, sequential access, sequential logic, sequential decisions, staged release, sequential bilingualism, and unbroken numbering.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从普通次序走到技术次序：固定排列、环环相扣、顺序存取、时序逻辑、序贯决策、分期发布、先后习得语言，以及连续编号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bolts sit in a row, and the hand may only move after the previous bolt is tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：螺栓排成一列，前一颗拧紧之后，手才允许移动。

branches.en: THE QUEUE AND ITS LOCK: position in line, then dependence on the previous step.
branches.cn: 队列与锁：先有队列中的位置，再有对前一步的依赖。

branches.en: THE MACHINE'S MEMORY: data read in stored order, and circuits that keep an earlier state.
branches.cn: 机器的记忆：按存储次序读取数据，电路记住先前状态。

branches.en: THE STAGGERED SCHEDULE: choices and releases that come out one at a time.
branches.cn: 错开的日程：选择与发布都一个一个出来。

branches.en: THE SECOND LANGUAGE AFTER THE FIRST: acquisition ordered in time.
branches.cn: 先母语后第二语言：习得按时间排序。

branches.en: THE NUMBER WITHOUT A GAP: order made visible.
branches.cn: 不断号的数字：被看得见的次序。

intro.en: Sequential is a Latin following stem with three English endings around it; the same stem supplies the nouns and verbs of ordering.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「跟随」词干套上英语词尾；同一词干还提供表示「排序」的名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies sequi and sequentia, and the prefix family shows how many kinds of following the root can name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「跟随」动词与名词；前缀家族则显示这个词根能命名多少种「跟随」。

items.example: The root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族的词根。

items.example: It gave English sequence.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语的「顺序」。

items.example: The stem seen in sequent and consequent.
items.exampleCN: 见于「接着的」与「随之而来的」两词。

items.example: It marks the adjective as relating to order.
items.exampleCN: 它标明该形容词与次序有关。

items.example: The everyday adverb of procedure.
items.exampleCN: 这是描述流程时最常用的副词。

items.example: It makes subsequent mean coming later.
items.exampleCN: 它使「随后的」表示较晚发生。

items.example: It makes consequence a result that comes along.
items.exampleCN: 它使「后果」成为随之而来的结果。

items.example: It closes the noun of consequence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结果的「后果」名词。

definition_zh: 顾客满意；顾客满意度（顾客对产品或服务体验的总体评价）
definition_en: the degree to which customers are pleased with a product, service or transaction
core_image: 餐厅门口的意见卡上打满勾，用餐的客人带着笑离开，店员把卡片收进透明盒子
scene: 服务台前，几位顾客离店前填写评价卡，店员把卡片收进透明的收集箱。 Customer satisfaction drives repeat visits more reliably than advertising.
sceneCN: 这里 customer satisfaction 指「顾客对整体体验的满意程度」（第 1 个义项：顾客对产品、服务与交易的整体评价）；句意为顾客满意比广告更能稳定地带来回头客。图中可辨识物件：评价卡、勾选栏、透明收集箱、离店顾客。

（作定语）用于衡量顾客满意的，如满意度调查、满意度评分等搭配
