senses.title: Overall approval of an experience
senses.definition: the overall judgement that a product or service has met the buyer's expectations
senses.definitionCN: 顾客对产品或服务是否达到预期的总体判断
senses.example: Customer satisfaction rose after the hotel added late check-out.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店增加延迟退房服务后，顾客满意度上升。
senses.why: satisfaction is built from satis 'enough' plus facere 'to do', so the word asks whether enough has been done for the buyer.
senses.whyCN: satisfaction 由 satis「足够」加 facere「做」构成，因此这个词问的是卖方是否「做得够」。

senses.title: A score produced by a survey
senses.titleCN: 调查量出的满意度得分
senses.definition: a number reported after buyers rate their experience on a scale
senses.definitionCN: 顾客按量表打分后得出的数值
senses.example: The chain reports customer satisfaction every quarter as a percentage.
senses.exampleCN: 该连锁企业每季度以百分比形式公布顾客满意度。
senses.why: once satisfaction became a target, it needed a number, and the phrase took on the sense of a measured index.
senses.whyCN: 当满意成为管理目标，就需要一个数字，这个短语便有了「可测量的指数」义。

senses.title: Reaction to a single transaction
senses.definition: the immediate judgement formed during one purchase, visit or service encounter
senses.definitionCN: 在某一次购买、到访或服务接触中当场形成的判断
senses.example: Customer satisfaction at the counter depends heavily on the wait.
senses.exampleCN: 柜台前的顾客满意度在很大程度上取决于等候时间。
senses.why: customer marks the person at the point of sale, so the phrase can be read narrowly as what one buyer feels at that moment.
senses.whyCN: customer 指交易现场的那个人，所以这个短语也可窄读为一个买主在那一刻的感受。

senses.title: Satisfaction accumulated over years
senses.titleCN: 长期关系中累积的满意
senses.definition: the sum of many experiences with one supplier over months or years
senses.definitionCN: 数月或数年间与同一供应商多次打交道后累积下来的评价
senses.example: Customer satisfaction built over a decade can survive one bad delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 十年累积的顾客满意度能经受住一次糟糕的配送。
senses.why: firms speak of the phrase across a whole relationship because memory outlasts a single receipt.
senses.whyCN: 企业谈这个短语时覆盖整段关系，因为记忆比一张小票活得更久。

senses.title: Satisfaction as a driver of repeat business
senses.definition: the level of contentment that makes a buyer return instead of switching to a rival
senses.definitionCN: 使买主回头而不转投对手的满意程度
senses.example: Customer satisfaction predicts repurchase better than a discount does.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客满意度比折扣更能预测复购。
senses.why: marketers read satisfaction as a cause rather than a result once repeat purchase becomes the goal.
senses.whyCN: 一旦复购成为目标，营销者就把满意看作原因而非结果。

senses.title: A figure tracked as a management target
senses.titleCN: 作为考核指标跟踪的数字
senses.definition: a figure that managers set, track and reward as part of performance review
senses.definitionCN: 管理者设定、跟踪并据此考核的绩效数字
senses.example: Customer satisfaction is one of the three targets in the manager's bonus plan.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客满意度是经理奖金方案中的三项指标之一。
senses.why: the phrase becomes countable when it names a dashboard figure rather than a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当这个短语指仪表盘上的数字而非一种感受时，它变得可数。

senses.title: Satisfaction after a complaint is handled
senses.definition: the judgement a buyer makes after a problem has been acknowledged and repaired
senses.definitionCN: 问题被承认并解决之后买主作出的评价
senses.example: Customer satisfaction recovered only after the airline refunded the ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 直到航空公司退还票款，顾客满意度才恢复。
senses.why: service research splits the phrase because a failure and its repair are judged separately from routine service.
senses.whyCN: 服务研究把这个短语单独切出，因为失误与修复是和日常服务分开评价的。

senses.title: Residents' approval of a public service
senses.titleCN: 居民对公共服务的满意
senses.definition: the same judgement applied by residents to a government service rather than a shop
senses.definitionCN: 居民对政府服务而非商店作出的同类判断
senses.example: Customer satisfaction with the water utility is now surveyed by the city.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府如今会调查居民对供水服务的满意度。
senses.why: the word customer widened to cover anyone served, even when no money changes hands.
senses.whyCN: customer 的词义扩大为任何被服务的人，即使没有金钱交易。

intro.en: Customer enters English through Anglo-French custumer, from custume 'habit, customary payment', itself from Latin consuetudo. Satisfaction is Latin satisfactio, from satis 'enough' and facere 'to do'. The two-word phrase is twentieth-century marketing vocabulary. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: customer 经盎格鲁-法语 custumer 进入英语，其源为 custume「习惯、惯常缴纳」，再上溯拉丁 consuetudo。satisfaction 来自拉丁 satisfactio，由 satis「足够」与 facere「做」构成。整个短语是 20 世纪营销词汇。年代均为约数。

items.en: Consuetudo 'custom, habit' was built from con- 'together' and suescere 'to become accustomed'. Its stem reached Old French as custume, the source of custom.
items.cn: consuetudo「习惯、惯例」由 con-「共同」与 suescere「变得习惯」构成；其词干进入古法语作 custume，即 custom 的来源。

items.en: Custumer named a person who had habitual dealings with a place, and in trade it came to mean one who buys regularly. The suffix -er marks the person, as in baker and buyer.
items.cn: custumer 指与某地常有往来的人，在商业中转而指经常购买的人；后缀 -er 标记人，如 baker、buyer。

items.en: Satis 'enough' plus facere 'to do, make' produced satisfacere 'to do enough, to discharge a claim'. The noun satisfactio first meant the settlement of a debt or an offence.
items.cn: satis「足够」加 facere「做、造」构成 satisfacere「做得够、清偿要求」；名词 satisfactio 最初指清偿债务或赎罪。

items.en: In English satisfaction kept its legal sense of settling a claim through the fourteenth century and only later, in the sixteenth, took the modern sense of contentment.
items.cn: 英语 satisfaction 在 14 世纪仍保留「清偿要求」的法律义，到 16 世纪才出现现代「满意」义。

items.en: Customer satisfaction became a fixed term with the growth of market research in the mid twentieth century, and later acquired the abbreviation CSAT in service management.
items.cn: 随着 20 世纪中期市场研究的兴起，customer satisfaction 成为固定术语，后来在服务管理中又得到缩写 CSAT。

items.en: No exact first citation for the full phrase is recorded; the earliest uses belong to mid twentieth-century marketing writing. The pre-Latin origin of suescere is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated form.
items.cn: 完整短语的最早书证没有确切记录，早期用例属 20 世纪中期的营销写作；suescere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，并非已证形式。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring forms from the same Latin stock that are constantly swapped; group two holds words that describe a related state without measuring it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词源、常被混用的邻近词形；第二组是描述相关状态却不作测量的词。

entries.definition: A blend of satisfy and suffice, coined in decision theory for accepting an adequate option instead of the best one; its second half is Latin sufficere, not facere.
entries.definitionCN: satisfy 与 suffice 的混成词，在决策理论中指接受「够用」的方案而非最优方案；它的后半来自拉丁 sufficere，而非 facere。

entries.definition: Built on the same satisfac- stem, it judges a thing as good enough rather than describing the buyer's feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 satisfac- 词干，但它评价事物「够好」，而非描述买主的感受。

entries.definition: From Latin satietas, also from satis 'enough', but it names physical fullness, especially after eating, not commercial approval.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 satietas，同样出自 satis「足够」，但指生理上的饱足，尤指吃饱，而非商业上的认可。

entries.definition: The plural of custom means duties charged on imported goods; it comes from the same habit-and-payment line but is not the buyer.
entries.definitionCN: custom 的复数指对进口货物征收的关税；它同出「习惯与缴纳」这条线，但并不指买主。

entries.definition: A quiet inner state of being satisfied with what one has; it is not measured, scored or tied to a purchase.
entries.definitionCN: 对现状感到满足的安静内心状态，不被测量、打分，也不与某次购买绑定。

entries.definition: The satisfaction of completing a promise or duty; it stresses delivery of an obligation, while customer satisfaction stresses the buyer's verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 完成承诺或职责后的满足，强调义务的兑现；顾客满意则强调买主的评判。

entries.definition: A formal or informal judgement that something is acceptable; it can be given without any feeling of pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事可否接受的正式或非正式判定；它可以不含任何愉悦感受。

entries.definition: Continued support for a person or brand; satisfaction may cause it, but loyalty is behaviour over time rather than a rating.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某品牌的持续支持；满意可能促成忠诚，但忠诚是长期行为而非一个评分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: satis 'enough' + facere 'do': satisfaction is the sense that enough has been done.
normal.cn: satis「足够」+ facere「做」：满意就是觉得对方做得够。

normal.en: customer is the person who comes back by custom, so the phrase already carries the idea of repeat buying.
normal.cn: customer 是按惯例回来的那个人，因此这个短语本身已含重复购买之意。

normal.en: The family runs customer, custom, satisfy, satisfaction, satisfactory, satisfied, satisfying.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 customer、custom、satisfy、satisfaction、satisfactory、satisfied、satisfying。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the measured sense: satisfaction survey, satisfaction score, satisfaction rating.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出测量义：满意度调查、满意度评分、满意度评级。

normal.en: Service writing shortens it to CSAT, a three-letter index on a dashboard.
normal.cn: 服务管理写作把它缩写成 CSAT，即仪表盘上的三字母指标。

abstract.en: Picture a card with five boxes, four ticked and one left empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一张有五个方框的卡片，四个打了勾，一个空着。

abstract.en: Picture the same shopper returning to the same counter on the same weekday.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个顾客在同一个星期几回到同一个柜台。

abstract.en: Picture a glass box slowly filling with identical cards.
abstract.cn: 想象一个透明箱子慢慢被相同的卡片填满。

examples.en: The airline measures customer satisfaction after every long-haul flight.
examples.cn: 该航空公司在每次长途航班后测量顾客满意度。

examples.en: Customer satisfaction fell when the return window was cut to seven days.
examples.cn: 退货期限缩短到七天后，顾客满意度下降。

examples.en: A polite reply to a complaint can restore customer satisfaction within a day.
examples.cn: 对投诉作出礼貌回应，可以在一天内恢复顾客满意度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「customer（顾客）+ satisfaction（满足）」——顾客的要求被做得够，心里就满足 → 顾客满意度

root: customer 经古法语 custumer 上溯拉丁 consuetudo「习惯」（con- + suescere「变得习惯」）；satisfaction 来自拉丁 satisfactio（satis「足够」+ facere「做」）。整个短语是 20 世纪市场研究的产物。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one judgement: a buyer decides that enough has been done, and that judgement is then counted, timed, summed over years, turned into a target, applied to a repair, and finally extended to public services.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个判断展开：买主认定对方做得够，这个判断再被计数、被限定在单次、被多年累加、变成考核指标、用于补救，最后延伸到公共服务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a comment card full of ticks, dropped into a clear box by a customer on the way out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张打满勾的意见卡，被离店的顾客投进透明箱子。

branches.en: MET EXPECTATION: the plain state, and the same state summed over a long relationship.
branches.cn: 预期被满足：朴素状态，以及长期关系中被累加起来的同一状态。

branches.en: MEASURED AND MOMENTARY: a survey turns the feeling into a number, while a single counter visit keeps it momentary.
branches.cn: 被测量与即时的：调查把感受变成数字，单次柜台经历则让它停留在当下。

branches.en: CAUSE OF RETURN: satisfaction is read forward as a reason a buyer comes back.
branches.cn: 回头的原因：满意被向前读作买主回来的理由。

branches.en: TARGET AND WIDER SERVE: a dashboard figure, then the same figure applied to residents served by a city.
branches.cn: 指标与更广的服务：先是仪表盘数字，再是用于城市居民的同一种数字。

branches.en: AFTER FAILURE: a complaint and its repair are judged on their own.
branches.cn: 失误之后：投诉与补救被单独评价。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived noun for the buyer to a Latin noun for contentment; both halves carry suffixes that also build other common words.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「买主」名词接在拉丁来源的「满足」名词上；两部分所带的后缀还构成其他常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin consuetudo supplies custom and customer, while satis and facere supply satisfy, satisfaction and satisfactory; satis also feeds satiety and satiate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 consuetudo 提供 custom 与 customer，satis 与 facere 提供 satisfy、satisfaction 与 satisfactory；satis 还衍生 satiety 与 satiate。

items.structure: Latin consuetudo via Old French custume
items.example: Custom decides which side of the road traffic uses.
items.exampleCN: 习惯决定车辆靠道路哪一侧行驶。

items.example: The customer asked for the same brand again.
items.exampleCN: 这位顾客又要了同一个品牌。

items.meaning: to meet a need or expectation
items.example: One small change satisfied most complaints.
items.exampleCN: 一处小改动就满足了大部分投诉。

items.example: Her satisfaction showed in a short nod.
items.exampleCN: 她轻轻点头，显出满意。

items.example: The repair was satisfactory but not elegant.
items.exampleCN: 修理结果合格，但算不上漂亮。

items.example: The diners left satisfied.
items.exampleCN: 食客们满意地离开。

items.example: It was a slow but satisfying meal.
items.exampleCN: 这顿饭上得慢，却令人满足。

items.example: Simon argued that managers satisfice rather than maximise.
items.exampleCN: 西蒙认为管理者会选择「够用」而非「最优」。

items.example: Rich food brings satiety quickly.
items.exampleCN: 油腻的食物很快带来饱足感。

items.example: The market showed an insatiable appetite for the device.
items.exampleCN: 市场对这款设备表现出无法满足的需求。

definition_zh: 暴露于；接触到；受到……作用；面临……风险；置身于……之下
definition_en: to be placed in contact with something that can act on a person, a material or an organisation, whether harmfully or instructively
core_image: 一扇仓门被拉开，外面的风、尘与光一齐涌进来，站在门口的人无处遮挡，只能让这些东西落在身上
scene: 老厂房的切割车间里，除尘罩一直没有装好，工人站在飞溅的碎屑中间作业。 Workers in the older plant may be exposed to fine silica dust during the cutting process.
sceneCN: 这里指工人置身于有害粉尘之中（第 1 个义项：人体接触可能造成伤害的物质）；句意为在老厂区，工人在切割过程中可能接触到细小的硅尘。图中可辨识物件：切割机、悬浮粉尘、未装的除尘罩、口罩。

pos.zh: 暴露于；接触到（系表结构，后接名词或动名词，时态由系动词承担）
受到……作用；面临……风险（用于材料、组织与抽象事物）

derivatives.zh: 去掉系动词与介词后的核心动词，义为「使暴露；揭露」
由动词加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「暴露；曝光；接触量」
由动词的过去分词转作形容词，义为「暴露的；无遮蔽的」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可暴露的；可揭开的」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「说明性的」

senses.title: In contact with a hazard
senses.definition: to be in contact with a substance or condition that may damage health
senses.definitionCN: 接触可能损害健康的物质或环境
senses.example: Workers who may be exposed to asbestos must wear sealed suits.
senses.exampleCN: 可能接触石棉的工人必须穿密闭防护服。
senses.why: The core verb meant to put something outside, and being outside is exactly how a hazard reaches the body.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「把某物放到外面」，而「在外面」正是危险物触及身体的途径。

senses.title: Learning a language by contact
senses.definition: to hear and use a language in daily surroundings rather than through formal study
senses.definitionCN: 在日常环境中听到并使用某种语言，而非只靠正式学习
senses.example: Children can be exposed to two languages from the first year without confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童从第一年起就可以接触两种语言，而不会混淆。
senses.why: A child put outside the home's single language meets a second one, and contact is the whole method.
senses.whyCN: 孩子被放到家庭单一语言之外，遇上第二种语言，接触本身就是全部方法。

senses.title: Meeting a new practice
senses.definition: to come into contact with unfamiliar methods, tools or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 接触到不熟悉的方法、工具或观念
senses.example: Villagers may be exposed to new farming methods through the extension officer.
senses.exampleCN: 村民可能通过推广员接触到新的耕作方法。
senses.why: A villager brought outside the usual routine meets a method that was not available indoors.
senses.whyCN: 村民被带到惯常做法之外，遇上一种在屋里得不到的方法。

senses.title: Acted on by heat, light or radiation
senses.definition: to be subjected to energy that changes the material
senses.definitionCN: 受到会改变材料性质的能量的作用
senses.example: Film of this kind should not be exposed to direct sunlight for more than an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这类胶片受阳光直射不应超过一小时。
senses.why: Photography gave this sense its sharp edge: a sensitive surface left outside is changed by light itself.
senses.whyCN: 摄影给了这一义项锋利的边界：感光面留在外面，就会被光本身改变。

senses.title: Carrying financial risk
senses.definition: to hold assets or obligations whose value can move against one
senses.definitionCN: 持有价值可能朝不利方向变动的资产或负债
senses.example: Firms that may be exposed to currency swings usually hedge their contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 可能受到汇率波动冲击的公司，通常会为合同作对冲。
senses.why: Assets held in the open move with a market one does not control, exactly as a surface left outside moves with the weather.
senses.whyCN: 暴露在外的资产随自己无法控制的市场起落，正如留在外面的表面随天气变化。

senses.title: Laid open to public view
senses.definition: to be made visible or known to people who had no right to see it
senses.definitionCN: 被本无权看到的人看见或知道
senses.example: The private letters should never be exposed to public view without the family's consent.
senses.exampleCN: 未经家属同意，这些私人信件绝不应暴露在公众眼前。
senses.why: Letters carried out of a private drawer are seen by eyes that were never meant to read them.
senses.whyCN: 信件被从私人抽屉里拿出来，被本不该读它们的人看见。

senses.title: Given small amounts to build immunity
senses.definition: to be brought into controlled contact with an antigen so the body learns to resist it
senses.definitionCN: 与抗原发生受控接触，使身体学会抵抗
senses.example: Infants can be exposed to harmless proteins that train the immune system.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿可以接触无害的蛋白，以训练免疫系统。
senses.why: A small dose put into the body teaches it to meet the full dose later.
senses.whyCN: 少量被放进身体，教它日后应对足量的侵袭。

senses.title: Opened to criticism or testing
senses.definition: to be placed where others may examine and challenge one's claims
senses.definitionCN: 被置于他人可以审查和质疑其主张的位置
senses.example: Every claim in the paper must be exposed to independent scrutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 论文中的每一项主张都必须接受独立审查。
senses.why: A claim brought into the open can be challenged by anyone who can reach it.
senses.whyCN: 主张被带到明处，任何够得着它的人都能质疑。

senses.title: Damaged by an external condition
senses.definition: to suffer slow damage from the surrounding air, water or salt
senses.definitionCN: 因周围空气、水或盐分而缓慢受损
senses.example: The bronze plaques may be exposed to salt air and lose their polish.
senses.exampleCN: 那些铜牌可能受含盐海风侵蚀而失去光泽。
senses.why: Metal left in salt air is slowly eaten by the very air it stands in.
senses.whyCN: 留在含盐空气中的金属，被它身处其中的空气慢慢吃掉。

intro.en: The phrase is built on the verb meaning to put out, which Latin formed from ex- 'out' and ponere 'to place'. To expose is literally to put something out, and the phrase names what the thing is put out into.
intro.cn: 这个短语的核心是表示「放到外面」的动词，拉丁语用表示「向外」的前缀加表示「放置」的动词构成。所谓使暴露，字面就是「把某物放到外面」，短语则补出「放到什么之中」。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or to place, and it stands behind position, compose, deposit and expose alike.
items.cn: 这个词意为「放置」，位置、组成、沉积与暴露诸词都出自它。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ponere produced exponere, to put out, to set forth, and also to abandon an infant to the elements.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的前缀加「放置」，构成「放出、摆出」的动词，也曾指把婴儿弃于户外。

items.en: Old French reshaped the verb as exposer, to set out, to display, to leave unprotected.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词改写为「摆出、展示、任其无遮」的意思。

items.en: English took the verb for laying something open to view or to danger; the passive frame followed naturally.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入这个动词，指让某物敞开于视野或危险之中；被动框架随之自然形成。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the frame covered radiation dose, chemical contact and market risk. The exact first citation of the passive frame is uncertain.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个框架覆盖辐射剂量、化学接触与市场风险。该被动框架最早的书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin placing verb and is constantly confused with it; the second group holds other ways of saying that something is acted on.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「放置」动词，常被与之混淆；第二组是其他表示「受到作用」的说法。

entries.definition: The active verb names an agent who lays something open; the passive phrase removes the agent and keeps only the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 主动动词点出「把某物敞开」的施事者；被动短语去掉施事者，只留下那种处境。

entries.definition: The noun measures the contact as a quantity, as in a radiation exposure; the phrase describes the state, not the dose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词把接触量化为数值，如辐射暴露量；短语描述状态，而不是剂量。

entries.definition: Im- 'on' plus ponere means to place a burden on someone; it shares the root but has nothing to do with being laid open.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「在上」的前缀加「放置」，意为把负担压在某人身上；词根相同，但与「敞开」无关。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus ponere means to put parts together; the shared root is placing, not exposing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「一起」的前缀加「放置」，意为把各部分放在一起；共享的只是「放置」这一动作。

entries.definition: A formal phrase for being made to undergo a treatment or rule; it often implies an authority doing the subjecting.
entries.definitionCN: 正式地表示「使遭受某种处理或规则」，常暗示有权威在施加。

entries.definition: Neutral about harm: two things touch, and nothing is said about damage or learning.
entries.definitionCN: 对是否有害保持中立：两物接触，不涉及损害或学习。

entries.definition: To meet something unexpectedly, often used of difficulties; it lacks the sense of prolonged contact.
entries.definitionCN: 意外遇到某物，常用于困难；不含长时间接触之意。

entries.definition: To have a risk or a problem ahead; it stresses what one must deal with rather than what acts on one.
entries.definitionCN: 面前存在风险或问题；强调必须应对，而不是受到作用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the open warehouse door, the bilingual household, the film canister and the bronze plaque.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用敞开的仓门、双语家庭、胶片暗盒与铜牌四个场景。

normal.en: A warehouse door pulled open: dust, wind and light all enter at once.
normal.cn: 仓门一拉开，尘、风与光同时涌进来。

normal.en: A child hears one language at the table and another at the door.
normal.cn: 孩子在饭桌边听一种语言，在门口听另一种语言。

normal.en: A film canister left on the sill turns milky by noon.
normal.cn: 胶片暗盒放在窗台上，到中午就发白了。

normal.en: A bronze plaque near the sea grows a green skin.
normal.cn: 靠海的铜牌长出一层绿皮。

normal.en: A paper read at a seminar before it is published.
normal.cn: 论文先拿到研讨会上读，然后才发表。

abstract.en: To be exposed is to lose the wall between oneself and the world.
abstract.cn: 被暴露，就是失去自己与世界之间的那堵墙。

abstract.en: Not all exposure harms: small doses can teach a body or a mind what to resist.
abstract.cn: 并非所有暴露都有害：小剂量能教身体或心智学会抵抗。

abstract.en: A claim kept indoors is safe; a claim exposed is either strengthened or broken.
abstract.cn: 主张关在屋里最安全；一旦暴露，不是变强就是被击碎。

examples.en: Samples left on the bench may be exposed to dust and should be capped at once.
examples.cn: 留在实验台上的样品可能沾染灰尘，应立即加盖。

examples.en: Students can be exposed to primary sources only after the archive grants permission.
examples.cn: 学生只有在档案馆许可之后，才能接触原始文献。

examples.en: A fund that may be exposed to sudden withdrawals needs a cash reserve.
examples.cn: 可能遭遇突然赎回的基金，需要留有一笔现金储备。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 伊克斯波兹德 图」：把「放到外面」记成仓门大开，风尘一起落在身上——这就是暴露于

root: 核心动词出自拉丁语，由表示「向外」的前缀加表示「放置」的动词构成，本义是「把某物放到外面、摆出来」，引申为「使无遮蔽、使遭受」。该短语为被动框架，由系动词、过去分词与介词构成，后面补出所暴露的对象。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from harm to instruction: a hazard, a language, a new method, radiant energy, market risk, public view, a vaccine dose, criticism, and slow corrosion.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从伤害走到教益：有害物、语言、新方法、辐射能量、市场风险、公众视野、疫苗剂量、批评与缓慢侵蚀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opened onto a room with no wall, letting whatever is outside act on whoever stands within.
core.cn: 核心意象：门一开，房间没有墙，外面的东西直接作用在站在里面的人身上。

branches.en: THE OPENING: a body or a metal face meets dust, salt or weather and pays for it.
branches.cn: 敞口：身体或金属面遇到粉尘、盐分或天气，并为此付出代价。

branches.en: THE WIDE WORLD: a learner meets a language or a method that was not in the room before.
branches.cn: 广阔世界：学习者遇到原本不在屋里的语言或方法。

branches.en: THE SENSITIVE SURFACE: energy itself changes the material left in the open.
branches.cn: 感光面：能量本身改变了留在外面的材料。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: value held in the open moves with a market one does not control.
branches.cn: 账簿：暴露在外的价值，随自己无法控制的市场起落。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC EYE: words, antigens and claims are all brought out where others may act on them.
branches.cn: 公众之眼：言辞、抗原与主张都被带到别人可以作用的地方。

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin verb for placing, with a prefix that points outward; the endings cover the act, the state and the thing placed.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语「放置」动词上，前缀指向外；词尾覆盖动作、状态与被放置之物。

latinIntro.en: Latin exponere and its participle expositus reached English through French, which supplied the modern spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「放出」动词及其分词经法语进入英语，现代拼写由法语提供。

items.example: It marks the thing as put outside.
items.exampleCN: 它标出某物被放到外面。

items.example: The placing verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族背后的「放置」动词。

items.example: The direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The participle that became the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词后来成为英语的形容词。

items.example: It turns the participle into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 它把分词变成描述词。

items.example: It forms the noun of the state of being laid open.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「敞开状态」的名词。

items.example: It forms the adjective for what can be exposed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「可被暴露」的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective of a setting-forth style.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「说明性」的形容词。

derivatives.zh: 核心动词，义为「使暴露；揭露」
由动词加状态名词尾构成，义为「暴露；曝光」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「无遮蔽的」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可暴露的」

definition_zh: 朝向；方位；方向感；迎新介绍；取向；定位；定向能力；（材料的）取向
definition_en: the direction in which something faces, the ability to know where you are, an introduction to a new place or role, or the aim toward which a person or policy is turned
core_image: 指南针的针在罗盘上找到自己的北，随后所有方向都从这一指算起
scene: 新生报到第一天，老师带大家绕校园走一圈，把食堂、图书馆和宿舍一一指出来。 The campus tour on the first day is the orientation for new students.
sceneCN: 这里 orientation 是「迎新介绍」（第 3 个义项：帮助刚到新环境的人熟悉地方与流程的介绍活动）；句意：第一天的校园参观就是给新生的迎新介绍。

pos.zh: 朝向；方位；方向感；迎新介绍；取向；定向

collocations.zh: 迎新项目；入职培训计划

derivatives.zh: 使朝向；使适应；东方
以……为导向的；面向……的
东方的；东方人（旧称，今多含争议）
重新定向；方向调整
迷失方向；定向障碍

senses.title: The direction a thing faces
senses.definition: the direction in which a building, object, or structure is placed or turned relative to its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物、物体或结构相对于周围环境被放置或转向的方向
senses.example: The orientation of the chapel windows lets the morning sun fall on the altar.
senses.exampleCN: 小教堂窗户的朝向让晨光正好落在祭坛上。
senses.why: Latin oriens is the rising sun, the east. The first orientation was literally a turning toward the east; any facing direction is that same needle settling on a point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 oriens 是“升起的太阳”，也就是东方。最早的 orientation 字面上就是“朝东”；任何朝向都是同一根指针停在某个点上。

senses.title: Knowing where you are
senses.titleCN: 知道自己在哪的方向感
senses.definition: the ability to judge your position and the direction you are facing, especially after a change of place
senses.definitionCN: 判断自己所在位置与所面方向的能力，尤其是在换了地方之后
senses.example: He lost his orientation in the unlit stairwell and climbed the wrong way.
senses.exampleCN: 他在没有灯的楼梯井里失去了方向感，爬错了方向。
senses.why: The compass needle inside you has to find north before the body can move. When that inner needle fails, the word names the missing skill rather than the direction of any object.
senses.whyCN: 身体移动之前，你心里那根罗盘针必须先找到北。当这根内心的针失灵时，这个词命名的是缺失的能力，而不是某个物体所朝的方向。

senses.title: An introduction to a new place
senses.definition: an organized introduction that helps new students, employees, or members learn where things are and how they work
senses.definitionCN: 帮助新学生、新员工或新成员了解地方与流程的有组织介绍活动
senses.example: Orientation week ends with a tour of the library and the health center.
senses.exampleCN: 迎新周以参观图书馆和医疗中心结束。
senses.why: A newcomer has no needle yet. Orientation hands them one: a map, a schedule, and the names of the rooms, so that they can face the right way on their first Monday.
senses.whyCN: 新来的人还没有自己的针。迎新介绍递给他们一根：一张地图、一份日程、各个房间的名字，好让他们在第一个周一就朝向正确的方向。

senses.title: The set of beliefs that directs a person
senses.titleCN: 指导一个人的那套信念
senses.definition: the beliefs, values, or interests that set the direction of a person's thinking, politics, or desire
senses.definitionCN: 决定一个人思想、政治立场或情感指向的信念、价值观或兴趣
senses.example: The survey asked about religious orientation but not about party affiliation.
senses.exampleCN: 调查询问了宗教取向，却没有询问党派归属。
senses.why: The needle no longer points north but toward a value. Orientation here means the direction a mind has settled on, which explains why the word works for politics, religion, and sexuality alike.
senses.whyCN: 指针不再指向北，而是指向某种价值。这里的 orientation 指思想已经落定的方向，这解释了为什么它同时适用于政治、宗教与性取向。

senses.title: Turning something toward a purpose
senses.definition: the act of aiming a policy, institution, or product toward a particular purpose, audience, or market
senses.definitionCN: 把政策、机构或产品对准某个目的、受众或市场的行动
senses.example: The new funding rules mark a clear orientation toward basic research.
senses.exampleCN: 新的资助规则明显转向了基础研究。
senses.why: This is orientation as an action: someone physically turns the object so that its face is toward the goal. Policy language borrows the gesture and calls the resulting aim an orientation.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 orientation 是一个动作：有人把物体实际转过来，让它的正面朝向目标。政策语言借用了这个动作，并把由此形成的目标称为“导向”。

senses.title: Aligning a map or instrument
senses.titleCN: 把地图或仪器对齐方位
senses.definition: the act of turning a map, instrument, or device so that its markings agree with the points of the compass
senses.definitionCN: 转动地图、仪器或装置，使其标记与罗盘方位一致的动作
senses.example: Check the orientation of the map before you trust the trail markers.
senses.exampleCN: 在相信路标之前，先检查地图有没有定向。
senses.why: The original technical sense survives here in its purest form: the paper must be turned until its north matches the world's north. Orientation is that turning, not the direction that results.
senses.whyCN: 最初的技术义在这里以最纯粹的形式保留下来：必须转动纸面，直到图上的北与世界的北对上。orientation 指的是这个转动动作，而不是转出来的方向。

senses.title: How animals find their way
senses.definition: the way animals determine and maintain a direction during migration, homing, or daily movement
senses.definitionCN: 动物在迁徙、归巢或日常移动中判断并保持方向的方式
senses.example: Sea turtles rely on magnetic orientation to cross open water.
senses.exampleCN: 海龟依靠磁定向穿越开阔海域。
senses.why: Biology applies the compass to a living body. The animal carries its own needle — magnetic, solar, or chemical — and orientation names the process by which that needle is read.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这根罗盘用到了活的躯体上。动物自带一根针——磁的、太阳的或化学的——orientation 命名的是读取这根针的过程。

senses.title: The alignment of molecules or fibres
senses.titleCN: 分子或纤维的排列取向
senses.definition: the arrangement of molecules, fibres, or crystals along a common axis, which changes the strength or behaviour of a material
senses.definitionCN: 分子、纤维或晶体沿同一轴线排列的方式，这种排列会改变材料的强度或性能
senses.example: Pulling the polymer through a die increases the orientation of its chains.
senses.exampleCN: 把聚合物拉过模口会增加其分子链的取向程度。
senses.why: At the micro-scale the needle is a long molecule. When all of them lie the same way, the material gains strength, so orientation moves from 'which way it faces' to 'how its parts are lined up'.
senses.whyCN: 在微观尺度上，指针就是一根长分子。当所有分子都朝同一方向躺下时，材料就获得强度，于是 orientation 从“朝哪边”转成“内部如何排列”。

senses.title: Finding a vocational direction
senses.definition: the process of helping a person identify the kind of study or work that suits their interests and abilities
senses.definitionCN: 帮助一个人找出适合其兴趣与能力的学习或工作方向的过程
senses.example: The careers service offers vocational orientation in the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 就业服务中心在二年级提供职业定向辅导。
senses.why: A young person without a direction is like a traveller without a compass. The counsellor supplies readings — interests, aptitudes, values — until one bearing feels like north.
senses.whyCN: 没有方向的年轻人就像没有罗盘的旅人。辅导员提供各种读数——兴趣、性向、价值观——直到某个方位读起来像“北”。

intro.en: Orientation is English orient plus the Latin action suffix -ation (-ationem). Orient goes back to Latin oriens, orientem, 'the east, the rising sun', the present participle of oriri 'to rise'. The word first named the act of turning a church or building toward the east, then any facing, then a map's alignment, and only in the 20th century an introduction for newcomers. The same oriri underlies origin, original, and originality.
intro.cn: orientation 是英语 orient 加拉丁动作后缀 -ation（-ationem）。orient 上溯拉丁语 oriens、orientem“东方、升起的太阳”，即 oriri“升起”的现在分词。这个词最早指把教堂或建筑朝东，之后指任何朝向，再指地图定向，直到 20 世纪才指对新来者的介绍。同一个 oriri 也是 origin、original、originality 的源头。

items.en: Oriens, orientem is 'the east' and literally 'the rising one', from oriri 'to come up, rise', used of the sun. The noun orient entered English in the 14th century as the east.
items.cn: oriens、orientem 意为“东方”，字面是“升起者”，出自 oriri“升起”，专用于太阳。名词 orient 在 14 世纪以“东方”进入英语。

items.en: Orientation first appears in English in the 17th century for the action of turning toward the east, especially the ritual placement of a church altar, and for the arrangement of a building relative to the compass.
items.cn: orientation 在 17 世纪首次出现在英语中，指“转向东方”的动作，尤指教堂祭坛的仪式性朝向，也指建筑物相对罗盘的布置。

items.en: The sense widens from east to any direction, and then to the act of aligning a map or instrument with the compass. The figurative sense of a person's political or intellectual bearing follows.
items.cn: 词义从“东”扩大到任何方向，再扩大到把地图或仪器与罗盘对齐的动作。随后出现比喻义，指一个人的政治或思想方位。

items.en: American colleges and employers begin to call the introduction for newcomers an orientation, because it teaches them which way everything faces. The usage spreads to vocational and psychological guidance.
items.cn: 20 世纪 40 年代，美国高校与雇主开始把对新来者的介绍称为 orientation，因为它教人认清一切事物的朝向。这一用法随后扩展到职业与心理辅导。

items.en: The -ation ending is Latin -ationem, an action noun. It makes orientation name the act of turning and, by transference, the resulting direction — which is why one word covers both 'the turning' and 'the bearing'.
items.cn: -ation 词尾是拉丁 -ationem，构成动作名词。它让 orientation 既命名“转”的动作，又转指转出来的方向——所以一个词同时覆盖“转向”与“方位”。

items.en: Ornament comes from Latin ornare 'to adorn' and shares nothing with oriri. Orientation, origin, original, and abortive's oriri branch form one family; ornament's orn- is decoration, not rising.
items.cn: ornament 来自拉丁语 ornare“装饰”，与 oriri 毫无关系。orientation、origin、original 属同一词族；ornament 的 orn- 表示装饰，与“升起”无关。

note.en: The first group follows the family from the verb orient through the noun origin and one spelling trap. The second group separates the words used for direction, for a sense of place, for an induction, and for a line-up.
note.cn: 第一组沿着词族从动词 orient 走到名词 origin，并区分一个拼写陷阱。第二组分辨用于“方向”“方位感”“入职引导”“对齐”的几个词。

entries.definition: to turn or place something so that it faces a particular direction, or the east as a noun. Orientation is the action noun built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物转向或置于某个方向；作名词时指东方。orientation 是在它之上构成的动作名词。

entries.definition: the point where something begins or comes from. It shares oriri 'to rise' with orientation, but its image is the source of a river, not the needle of a compass.
entries.definitionCN: 事物开始或来源的那一点。它与 orientation 共享 oriri“升起”，但意象是河流的源头，而不是罗盘的指针。

entries.definition: a decorative object or addition. Its root is ornare 'to adorn'; the shared or- is a coincidence of spelling, not of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰物或装饰性的添加。它的词根是 ornare“装饰”；相同的 or- 只是拼写巧合，意义无关。

entries.definition: a sport in which runners find their way across unknown ground with a map and compass. It is built on orient plus -eer and -ing, and keeps the literal compass sense.
entries.definitionCN: 参赛者凭地图和罗盘在陌生地形中找路的运动。它由 orient 加 -eer 与 -ing 构成，保留了字面的罗盘义。

entries.definition: the line along which something moves or faces. It is the bare geometric word, with no image of a needle finding north.
entries.definitionCN: 事物移动或朝向的那条线。它是纯几何词，没有“指针找到北”的画面。

entries.definition: your position relative to surrounding places, chiefly in the phrase to get your bearings. It is the personal sense of orientation, not the formal act of aligning.
entries.definitionCN: 你相对于周围地点的位置，主要用于短语 to get your bearings。它偏指个人的方位感，而非正式的定向动作。

entries.definition: the formal process of introducing a new employee or member to rules and duties. It stresses procedure, while orientation stresses learning where things are.
entries.definitionCN: 把新员工或新成员正式引入规则与职责的过程。它强调程序，而 orientation 强调了解事物在何处。

entries.definition: the state of being arranged in a straight line or in agreement. It is the physical or strategic lining-up, not the compass-facing that orientation names.
entries.definitionCN: 排成直线或达成一致的状态。它指物理或战略上的对齐，而不是 orientation 所指的朝向罗盘。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: oriri 'to rise', oriens 'east', the 17th-century church use, the 1940s campus use, and the ornare trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：oriri“升起”、oriens“东方”、17 世纪的教堂用法、20 世纪 40 年代的校园用法，以及 ornare 陷阱。

normal.en: Oriens is the rising sun: orientation began as turning a church toward the east, so every later 'facing' keeps the sunrise in it.
normal.cn: oriens 是升起的太阳：orientation 最初指把教堂转向东方，所以后来每一种“朝向”里都留着那个日出。

normal.en: Oriri 'to rise' also gives origin and original: the place where the sun comes up and the place where a thing begins are one idea.
normal.cn: oriri“升起”也产生 origin 与 original：太阳升起的地方和事物开始的地方，是同一个想法。

normal.en: A map is oriented when its north matches the world's north; the word names the turning, and the direction is what the turning produces.
normal.cn: 地图定向，就是让图上的北与世界上的北对齐；这个词命名的是转的动作，方向是转出来的结果。

normal.en: In the 1940s American campuses gave newcomers an orientation: a tour that points their inner compass at the right buildings.
normal.cn: 20 世纪 40 年代的美国校园给新生安排 orientation：一趟把内心罗盘指到正确楼房的参观。

normal.en: Ornament is from ornare 'to adorn'; decoration changes how a thing looks, orientation changes which way it faces.
normal.cn: ornament 出自 ornare“装饰”；装饰改变事物的外观，orientation 改变事物的朝向。

abstract.en: A needle does not know north; it only refuses to rest anywhere else. Orientation is the refusal that becomes a direction.
abstract.cn: 指针并不认识北；它只是拒绝停在别处。orientation 就是这种拒绝变成的方向。

abstract.en: Standing in a new city at dusk, you turn your body until the map and the streets agree; that small turn is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 黄昏站在陌生城市里，你转动身体，直到地图与街道对上；这个小小的转动就是这个词的全部。

abstract.en: A molecule lying the same way as its neighbours is a compass needle at the scale of the invisible.
abstract.cn: 一个与邻居躺向相同的分子，就是一根存在于不可见尺度上的罗盘针。

examples.en: The orientation of the solar panels was adjusted for the winter sun.
examples.cn: 太阳能板的朝向按冬季日照做了调整。

examples.en: New employees spend their first morning in orientation.
examples.cn: 新员工第一个上午参加入职介绍。

examples.en: The fibres show strong orientation along the direction of the draw.
examples.cn: 纤维沿拉伸方向表现出很强的取向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥瑞恩泰申」——奥瑞恩（太阳神）一升起来，罗盘就知道哪边是东，所有方向都从这一点算 → orientation 朝向；方位；迎新介绍（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 oriens/orientem「东方、升起的太阳」，出自 oriri「升起」；后缀 -ation 为拉丁动作名词词尾。核心是「让一根针找到北，其他方向都由它算起」。同族含 orient、origin、original，均出自 oriri；ornament（ornare「装饰」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of orientation all begin with a needle finding north. What changes is what is being turned — a building, a map, a mind, a policy, a molecule, or a newcomer — and whether we name the turning or the bearing it produces.
sensesIntro.cn: orientation 的九个义项都从“一根针找到北”开始。变化的是被转的是什么——建筑、地图、思想、政策、分子或新来的人——以及我们命名的是转的动作，还是转出来的方位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a compass needle finding its north, with every other direction measured from that one point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根罗盘针找到自己的北，其他所有方向都从这一点量起。

chain: THE BODY TURNS TO MATCH IT
THE MIND CAN HOLD A BEARING
AND A NEWCOMER CAN BE GIVEN ONE

branches.en: PHYSICAL FACING: a building's placement, a map turned to the compass, and molecules lined along one axis.
branches.cn: 物理朝向：建筑的布置、地图与罗盘对齐，以及分子沿同一轴线排列。

branches.en: LIVING DIRECTION-FINDING: a person's sense of place and an animal's magnetic or solar navigation.
branches.cn: 生命体的定向：人的方位感，以及动物依靠磁场或太阳导航。

branches.en: THE GIVEN COMPASS: an introduction that hands a newcomer a map, a schedule, and room names.
branches.cn: 被递来的罗盘：一份把地图、日程与房间名交给新来者的介绍。

branches.en: THE INWARD NEEDLE: beliefs and values that direct a person, and the act of aiming a policy or product at a purpose.
branches.cn: 内心的针：指导一个人的信念与价值观，以及把政策或产品对准某个目的的行动。

branches.en: VOCATIONAL BEARING: guidance that helps a young person read their interests as a direction.
branches.cn: 职业方位：帮助年轻人把兴趣读成一个方向的辅导。

intro.en: Orientation is orient plus -ation, a Latin action-noun suffix. Orient is not a suffix-built word: it comes whole from Latin oriens, the rising sun. English then added -al for the adjective and -ation for the noun, and re- and dis- for the two reversals.
intro.cn: orientation 是 orient 加 -ation（拉丁动作名词后缀）。orient 不是靠后缀造出来的：它整体来自拉丁语 oriens“升起的太阳”。英语随后加 -al 构成形容词、加 -ation 构成名词，并用 re- 与 dis- 表示两种反向。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is oriri 'to rise', oriens/orientem 'the east', and the derived noun ortus 'a rising'. The compass sense is English, not Latin: Latin had no orientation in the modern sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 oriri“升起”、oriens/orientem“东方”，以及派生名词 ortus“升起”。罗盘义是英语自己发展出来的，拉丁语并没有现代意义上的 orientation。

items.meaning: the act of turning toward a point, and the bearing that results
items.meaningCN: 转向某一点的动作，以及由此形成的方位（-ation 动作名词）
items.example: The orientation of the antenna must match the transmitter.
items.exampleCN: 天线的朝向必须与发射机一致。

items.structure: Latin oriens, orientem 'east, rising sun' (from oriri)
items.meaning: to turn toward a direction; the east
items.example: Orient the map before you read the trail.
items.exampleCN: 读路标之前先把地图定向。

items.meaning: turned toward, or built around, a particular aim
items.meaningCN: 朝向某物的，或以某个目标为核心的（-ed 分词形容词）
items.example: The course is oriented toward laboratory work.
items.exampleCN: 这门课以实验室工作为导向。

items.meaning: of the east; now often avoided as a label for people
items.meaningCN: 东方的；今用于指人时常被视为不当标签
items.example: The museum's oriental collection is being renamed.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆的东方藏品正在被重新命名。

items.meaning: relating to orientation as a property
items.meaningCN: 与取向或朝向这一属性有关的
items.example: The study measured orientational order in the crystal.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究测量了晶体中的取向有序度。

items.meaning: a turning to a new direction
items.meaningCN: 转向新的方向；重新定向（re- 再次）
items.example: The firm announced a reorientation toward services.
items.exampleCN: 公司宣布向服务业重新定位。

items.meaning: loss of one's sense of direction or place
items.meaningCN: 失去方向感或位置感；定向障碍（dis- 去除）
items.example: Jet lag left her with a mild disorientation.
items.exampleCN: 时差让她有点失去方向感。

items.meaning: the sport of finding one's way with map and compass
items.meaningCN: 凭地图和罗盘找路的运动（-eer 人 + -ing 活动名词）
items.example: Orienteering requires both speed and map reading.
items.exampleCN: 定向越野既需要速度，也需要读图能力。

items.meaning: the British variant of orient as a verb
items.meaningCN: 英式英语中 orient 作动词的变体
items.example: New staff are orientated to the building layout.
items.exampleCN: 新员工会被告知楼内布局。

latinEntries.meaning: to rise, come up, be born

latinEntries.structure: present participle of oriri, genitive orientis

definition_zh: 工程；工程学；把科学原理用于设计、建造与改进的行业与活动
definition_en: the profession and activity of applying scientific and mathematical principles to design, build and improve things
core_image: 一张铺满图纸的长桌，桌边摆着模型桥、齿轮和计算尺，几个人围着它争论尺寸
scene: 长桌上铺满图纸，模型桥旁散着齿轮与计算尺，几个人围着争论一处尺寸。 The bridge stood because careful engineering had anticipated the river's spring floods.
sceneCN: 这里 engineering 指把科学原理用于设计与建造的行业与活动（第 1 个义项：工程这一行业）；句意：那座桥能立住，是因为细致的工程工作早已预判了河流的春汛。

pos.zh: 工程；工程学；工程设计工作

forms.label: 复数（罕用，指多种工程实践）

derivatives.zh: 工程师；设计建造
经工程设计的
生物工程
地球工程

senses.title: The profession as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为一个整体的工程行业
senses.definition: the organised occupation of designing and building reliable structures, machines and systems
senses.definitionCN: 设计并建造可靠结构、机器与系统的有组织职业
senses.example: Engineering attracts people who like a problem with a measurable answer.
senses.exampleCN: 工程行业吸引那些喜欢有可测量答案的问题的人。
senses.why: the -ing noun names the occupation, not one act, so it first means the trade as a body of practitioners.
senses.whyCN: 这个 -ing 名词指职业，而不是单次动作，因此首先指由从业者构成的行业。

senses.title: The application of science to practical ends
senses.definition: the activity of turning physical knowledge into working designs under real constraints
senses.definitionCN: 在真实约束下把物理知识变成可用设计的活动
senses.example: Engineering begins where the equation has to survive mud and weather.
senses.exampleCN: 当方程式必须经受泥泞与天气时，工程就开始了。
senses.why: the word marks the meeting point of theory and matter, which is why it is often defined against pure science.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记理论与物质的交会点，因此常被拿来与纯科学对照定义。

senses.title: A named branch of the profession
senses.definition: one specialised division such as civil, mechanical or electrical work
senses.definitionCN: 如土木、机械或电气这样的专门分支
senses.example: She moved from chemical engineering to safety inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 她从化学工程转到安全检验。
senses.why: large trades divide by material and method, and each division takes the head word as its family name.
senses.whyCN: 大型行业会按材料与方法分科，每个分支都以这个词作姓氏般的类名。

senses.title: The design work behind a structure
senses.titleCN: 支撑一项结构的设计工作
senses.definition: the calculations and choices that make a particular bridge, building or device work
senses.definitionCN: 使某座桥、某栋楼或某台设备成立的计算与选择
senses.example: The elegance of the hall is engineering you cannot see.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大厅的优雅是看不见的工程工作。
senses.why: a finished object hides its design, and the word names that hidden labour.
senses.whyCN: 成品把设计藏在内部，这个词就指那份看不见的劳动。

senses.title: Analysis of forces and materials
senses.definition: the technical calculation of loads, stresses and safety margins
senses.definitionCN: 对荷载、应力与安全裕度的技术计算
senses.example: Good engineering predicted the crack two winters before it opened.
senses.exampleCN: 优秀的工程分析在裂缝张开前两个冬天就预测到了它。
senses.why: the intellectual core of the trade is predicting behaviour before anything is built.
senses.whyCN: 这门行业最核心的智力工作，是在建造之前预测行为。

senses.title: Manipulation of people or systems
senses.definition: the arranging of social or financial affairs to produce a desired result
senses.definitionCN: 安排社会或财务事务以产生预期结果
senses.example: The scheme was social engineering dressed as charity.
senses.exampleCN: 那套方案是披着慈善外衣的社会操纵。
senses.why: the word's core is planned control of a system, and people can be treated as one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是对系统的有计划的控制，而人也可以被当作系统。

senses.title: Deliberate alteration of living things
senses.definition: the planned modification of genes or organisms for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某种目的对基因或生物体进行有计划的改造
senses.example: Genetic engineering of the crop reduced its water needs.
senses.exampleCN: 对那种作物的基因工程降低了它的用水需求。
senses.why: once heredity was understood as a mechanism, it could be designed like any other.
senses.whyCN: 一旦遗传被理解为一种机制，它就能像别的机制一样被设计。

senses.title: Financial or business structuring
senses.titleCN: 金融与业务结构的设计
senses.definition: the construction of financial arrangements to fit a defined aim
senses.definitionCN: 为实现特定目标而搭建的金融安排
senses.example: The tax result came from financial engineering, not from luck.
senses.exampleCN: 那个税务结果来自金融设计，而不是运气。
senses.why: money, like steel, can be arranged into structures, and the trade word extends to it.
senses.whyCN: 钱和钢一样可以被搭成结构，行业词就延伸到这里。

senses.title: The academic subject
senses.definition: the taught discipline of analysis, materials and design in a university
senses.definitionCN: 大学里讲授的分析、材料与设计学科
senses.example: He teaches engineering to students who have never held a tool.
senses.exampleCN: 他教那些从没拿过工具的学生学工程。
senses.why: a trade codified in textbooks becomes a degree subject with the same name.
senses.whyCN: 被写进教科书的行业会成为同名学位科目。

senses.title: The industrial sector
senses.definition: the firms and jobs that make up the trade in an economy
senses.definitionCN: 在经济中构成该行业的公司与岗位
senses.example: Engineering employs more people here than farming does.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，工程产业雇用的人比农业多。
senses.why: a profession counted in statistics becomes a sector, and the name travels with it.
senses.whyCN: 被统计的职业会变成一个产业部门，名称也随之而去。

intro.en: Engineering grows from engine, and engine goes back through French to Latin ingenium, inborn cleverness. The modern sense shifts from a clever device to the organised design of devices.
intro.cn: engineering 由 engine 生长而来，而 engine 经法语可追到拉丁语 ingenium「天生的才智」。现代含义从「巧妙的装置」转向「有组织地设计装置」。

items.en: Latin ingenium meant inborn character or natural talent, built from in- and gignere, to beget. A device born of talent was also called an ingenium.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ingenium 指天生的性情或才能，由 in- 与 gignere「生育」构成。由才能所生之物也被称为 ingenium。

items.en: Old French engin meant cleverness and also a contrivance, especially a military engine for a siege.
items.cn: 古法语 engin 指聪明，也指巧妙的装置，尤指攻城用的军用器械。

items.en: English engine first named any machine or device, and only with steam did it narrow to a power-producing motor.
items.cn: 英语 engine 最初指任何机器或装置，直到蒸汽时代才收窄为产生动力的发动机。

items.en: An engineer was first the person who built and worked military engines; the title later covered civil works as well.
items.cn: engineer 最初指建造与操作军用器械的人；这个称号后来也涵盖民用工程。

items.en: Engineering named the activity of such builders in the eighteenth century, when roads, canals and machines became a profession.
items.cn: 十八世纪，道路、运河与机器成为一门职业，engineering 才用来指这些建造者的活动。

items.en: The word then multiplied into branches and into figurative uses such as social and genetic engineering, all keeping the sense of planned construction.
items.cn: 此后这个词繁殖出许多分支，也进入社会工程、基因工程等比喻用法，全都保留「有计划的建造」这一含义。

note.en: The first group shares the engine root and the professional family; the second group is the neighbouring ideas of technology and design.
note.cn: 第一组共享 engine 词根与职业词族；第二组是技术与设计这些相邻观念。

entries.definition: The practitioner; engineering is the field and the activity that the practitioner carries out.
entries.definitionCN: 指从业者；engineering 是从业者所从事的领域与活动。

entries.definition: A machine that converts energy into motion; the older and wider sense was any contrivance.
entries.definitionCN: 把能量转成运动的机器；更早更广的含义是任何巧妙装置。

entries.definition: Designed with deliberate technical care, as in an engineered joint.
entries.definitionCN: 指经过有意的技术设计，如「工程设计的接缝」。

entries.definition: The body of scientific knowledge that supports engineering practice.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑工程实践的那部分科学知识。

entries.definition: The tools and techniques a society uses; engineering is the work of creating them.
entries.definitionCN: 一个社会使用的工具与技术；engineering 是创造它们的工作。

entries.definition: Science directed at practical problems; engineering adds design decisions under cost and safety limits.
entries.definitionCN: 面向实际问题的科学；engineering 另加成本与安全限制下的设计决策。

entries.definition: The act of building on site; engineering is the wider work that plans and justifies it.
entries.definitionCN: 指在现场施工；engineering 是包含规划与论证的更广工作。

entries.definition: The arrangement of a form to meet a purpose; engineering is the profession that applies it to physical systems.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成目的而安排形态；engineering 是把它施于实体系统的职业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Latin root and the real branch names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实拉丁词根与真实分支名称。

normal.en: Ingenium meant inborn talent; an engine was a thing born of talent.
normal.cn: ingenium 指天生的才能；engine 就是才能所生之物。

normal.en: The title started with military engines and then moved to roads and machines.
normal.cn: 这个称号从军用器械开始，后来转向道路与机器。

normal.en: Branch names all end in the same word: civil, mechanical, electrical, software.
normal.cn: 各分支名都以同一个词收尾：土木、机械、电气、软件。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show its reach: engineering degree, engineering team, reverse engineering.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示它的范围：工程学位、工程团队、逆向工程。

normal.en: The word is uncountable as a field, so one says a career in engineering, not an engineering.
normal.cn: 作为领域它不可数，所以说「从事工程行业」，而不是「一个工程」。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing table whose lines hold up a bridge that does not exist yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张绘图桌，纸上的线条撑起一座还不存在的桥。

abstract.en: Picture a gear that turns a river into a schedule.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚齿轮把一条河变成一张时间表。

abstract.en: Picture a safety margin drawn as a thin margin on paper and standing as a thick wall in the world.
abstract.cn: 想象纸上薄薄一道安全裕度，在现实里站成厚厚一堵墙。

examples.en: Engineering is judged by what happens after ten winters, not on opening day.
examples.cn: 工程的好坏要看十个冬天之后，而不是落成那天。

examples.en: She studied engineering because she wanted to see her drawings become heavy things.
examples.cn: 她学工程，是因为想让自己的图纸变成有重量的东西。

examples.en: The company treats engineering and maintenance as one budget line.
examples.cn: 公司把工程与维护放在同一条预算线上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩（en）机（gi）捏（neer）ring」——承恩于机器，又亲手去捏去造的那一行，就是工程

root: 拉丁 ingenium「天生才能」← in- + gignere「生育」→ 古法语 engin「巧器」→ 英语 engine；engineer 先指造军用器械者，十八世纪起 engineering 指这一职业与活动。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses move from the profession to applied science, branches, hidden design work, force analysis, social and genetic manipulation, finance, teaching and the sector.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从行业出发，经过应用科学、分支、隐藏的设计工作、受力分析、社会与基因改造、金融、教学，最后到产业部门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table of drawings, a model bridge and a slide rule, with people arguing over one dimension.
core.cn: 核心意象：一桌图纸、一座模型桥与一把计算尺，人们围着某个尺寸争论。

branches.en: PROFESSION AND SUBJECT: the trade as a body of workers, and the same trade taught as a degree.
branches.cn: 行业与学科：由从业者构成的行业，以及被当作学位教授的同一行业。

branches.en: THEORY MEETS MATTER: applying science, and calculating loads and margins before building.
branches.cn: 理论与物质相接：应用科学，并在建造前计算荷载与裕度。

branches.en: DIVISIONS AND SCALE: named branches on one side, the whole sector counted in an economy on the other.
branches.cn: 分支与规模：一边是有名目的分支，一边是经济统计中的整个产业。

branches.en: HIDDEN STRUCTURING: the design behind a built thing, and the arrangement of financial affairs.
branches.cn: 隐形的搭建：建成物背后的设计，以及金融事务的安排。

branches.en: TREATING SYSTEMS AS BUILDABLE: social manipulation, and the deliberate alteration of living things.
branches.cn: 把系统当作可建造物：社会操纵，以及对生物的有意改造。

intro.en: Engineering is an English -ing noun on the base engineer, which itself carries a French and Latin history; the ending makes a trade out of a person.
intro.cn: engineering 是以 engineer 为词基的英语 -ing 名词，而 engineer 本身带有法语与拉丁语的历史；这个词尾把人变成一门行业。

latinIntro.en: Latin ingenium is the deep source; French engin and engineer are the middle steps; English then added -ing to name the occupation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ingenium 是深远源头；法语 engin 与 engineer 是中间环节；英语再加 -ing 来指这门职业。

items.example: The prefix is part of the Latin noun for inborn quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀是拉丁语「天生品质」名词的一部分。

items.example: The verb explains why a device could be called a born thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词解释了为何装置可被称为「被生出之物」。

items.example: The noun already joins talent with contrivance.

dict_mnemonic.text: duet ＝ 意大利语 duetto ＝ duo（二）＋ 指小后缀 -etto ＝「给两个人的小曲」。所以 duet 的关键永远是「二」：两个声部是二重唱，两件乐器是二重奏。同源的 duo 指「二人组合」，dual 指「双重的」，而 duel（决斗）也是两个人——只是他们对着干而不是合着唱。记画面：舞台两侧各一支话筒，声音在中央汇成一条线。

definition_zh: 核糖体的；与核糖体有关的；由核糖体 RNA 或核糖体蛋白构成的
definition_en: relating to a ribosome, or made of the RNA and proteins that form a ribosome
core_image: 一个颗粒被透明罩子罩住，罩内的 RNA 骨架与蛋白颗粒各自贴上同一种颜色的标签
scene: 这里指「核糖体的」。 Ribosomal RNA folds into the core of the particle, while the proteins sit on its surface.
sceneCN: 这里 ribosomal 指「核糖体的、由核糖体组分构成的」（第 2 个义项：指 rRNA 与核糖体蛋白这些组分本身）；RNA 折叠成核心，蛋白贴在外围。图中可辨识物件：透明罩、RNA 骨架、表面蛋白颗粒、标签。

senses.title: Of the particle as a whole
senses.definition: relating to a ribosome as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 与整个核糖体相关的
senses.example: Ribosomal structure is strikingly similar across all three domains of life.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体结构在生命的三个域之间惊人地相似。
senses.why: the -al suffix turns the particle's name into a label of relation, so the adjective starts as 'of the ribosome'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把颗粒的名字变成表示关系的标签，因此这个形容词的起点是「核糖体的」。

senses.title: Of its RNA and protein components
senses.titleCN: 核糖体组分的：rRNA 与核糖体蛋白
senses.definition: made of or relating to the RNA and proteins that constitute the particle
senses.definitionCN: 由构成该颗粒的 RNA 与蛋白质组成，或与之相关
senses.example: Ribosomal proteins are imported into the nucleus before assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体蛋白在组装前被输入细胞核。
senses.why: the adjective shifts from the whole to its ingredients, naming the parts by the name of the thing they build.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从整体转向配料，用其所构成之物的名字来命名这些部件。

senses.title: Of the two subunits
senses.definition: relating to the small or large subunit of the particle
senses.definitionCN: 与核糖体的小亚基或大亚基相关
senses.example: A ribosomal subunit must fold correctly before it can join the other.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体亚基必须正确折叠才能与另一半结合。
senses.why: because the particle is built of two halves, the adjective also marks either half.
senses.whyCN: 由于该颗粒由两半构成，这个形容词也标记其中任一半。

senses.title: Of the docking sequence
senses.definition: relating to the site where a ribosome attaches to a messenger RNA
senses.definitionCN: 与核糖体附着到信使 RNA 的位点相关
senses.example: The ribosomal binding site lies just upstream of the start codon.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体结合位点就在起始密码子上游。
senses.why: the adjective follows the particle to its landing place and names that sequence as ribosomal.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词随颗粒走到它的落点，并把那段序列称为核糖体的。

senses.title: Of the genes that encode the parts
senses.titleCN: 核糖体基因的：编码组分的基因
senses.definition: relating to the genes that code for ribosomal RNA or ribosomal proteins
senses.definitionCN: 与编码核糖体 RNA 或核糖体蛋白的基因相关
senses.example: Ribosomal DNA is repeated hundreds of times in the human genome.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体 DNA 在人类基因组中重复数百次。
senses.why: since the parts are made from genes, the adjective extends to the instructions behind them.
senses.whyCN: 既然这些部件由基因制造，这个形容词便延伸到背后的指令。

senses.title: Of the act of translation
senses.titleCN: 核糖体翻译的：与翻译过程相关
senses.definition: describing protein synthesis carried out on the particle, as opposed to other routes
senses.definitionCN: 描述在该颗粒上完成的蛋白合成，以区别于其他途径
senses.example: Ribosomal translation accounts for almost all protein made in the cell.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体翻译承担了细胞内几乎全部蛋白质的制造。
senses.why: the adjective marks the route as well as the machine, so 'ribosomal translation' names a pathway.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既标记机器也标记路径，因此 ribosomal translation 命名一条通路。

senses.title: Of the conserved core
senses.titleCN: 核糖体保守核心的：进化上稳定的部分
senses.definition: relating to the parts of the particle that are nearly unchanged across species
senses.definitionCN: 与在各物种间几乎不变的部分相关
senses.example: The ribosomal core is the most conserved sequence in the cell.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体核心是细胞内最保守的序列。
senses.why: comparison across species shows a frozen core, so the adjective can point to what evolution refused to alter.
senses.whyCN: 跨物种比较显示出一个被冻结的核心，因此这个形容词可以指向演化拒绝改动的那部分。

senses.title: Of a drug target
senses.titleCN: 核糖体靶点的：药理学用法
senses.definition: describing the particle as a site where drugs can act selectively
senses.definitionCN: 把该颗粒描述为药物可选择性作用的位置
senses.example: Many antibiotics are ribosomal inhibitors with narrow spectra.
senses.exampleCN: 许多抗生素是核糖体抑制剂，作用谱窄。
senses.why: medicine uses the adjective to name a class of targets, turning the particle into a pharmacological address.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个形容词命名一类靶点，把这个颗粒变成一个药理学地址。

intro.en: Ribosomal is the English adjective on ribosome, with Latin -alis; the base is a twentieth-century blend of a chemical stem and Greek soma.
intro.cn: ribosomal 是以 ribosome 为词干、加拉丁 -alis 构成的英语形容词；词干是 20 世纪把化学词干与希腊 soma 混合的产物。

items.en: ribosome was coined in the 1950s from ribo- (RNA) and -some (Greek soma 'body'); the adjective adds only a suffix.
items.cn: ribosome 于 1950 年代由 ribo-（RNA）与 -some（希腊 soma「身体」）合成；形容词只增加一个后缀。

items.en: Latin -alis formed relational adjectives such as naturalis and structurals; English keeps -al, giving ribosomal.
items.cn: 拉丁 -alis 构成关系形容词，如 naturalis；英语保留为 -al，得 ribosomal。

items.en: New Latin ribosoma and ribosomalis are Latinized spellings, not inherited words; no classical Latin root can be claimed.
items.cn: 新拉丁语 ribosoma 与 ribosomalis 是拉丁化拼写，不是传承词；不应主张古典拉丁词根。

items.en: The adjective spread with electron microscopy and biochemistry in the 1950s and 1960s; its first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 该形容词随电镜与生物化学在 1950 至 60 年代传播；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Once ribosomal RNA was distinguished from transfer RNA, the adjective became a standard qualifier for RNA, protein, subunit and gene.
items.cn: 当核糖体 RNA 与转运 RNA 被区分后，这个形容词成为修饰 RNA、蛋白、亚基与基因的标准限定语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and coiner): neither the coiner nor the exact date of ribosome is firmly recorded, so the starting point of the derived adjective can only be given approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与首创者）：ribosome 的首创者与确切年代均无坚实记录，因此派生形容词的起点也只能给出约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes with a shared piece but a different referent; group two holds adjectives used in the same laboratory sentences.
note.cn: 第一组是共享构件但所指不同的形近词；第二组是出现在同一类实验句子里的形容词。

entries.definition: The particle itself. Ribosomal is only the qualifier; the noun is needed when a countable thing is meant.
entries.definitionCN: 指颗粒本身；ribosomal 只是限定语，指可数事物时须用名词。

entries.definition: An RNA molecule with enzymatic power. It shares ribo- but names a molecule class, not a ribosomal part.
entries.definitionCN: 具酶活性的 RNA 分子；共享 ribo-，但指一类分子，不是核糖体部件。

entries.definition: A five-carbon sugar found in RNA; the shared stem refers to a chemical, not to the particle.
entries.definitionCN: RNA 中的五碳糖；共享词干指一种化学物，不指颗粒。

entries.definition: The adjective of lysosome, built with the same -some. It marks a digestive compartment, not translation.
entries.definitionCN: 溶酶体的形容词，用同一个 -some 构成；标记消化区室，与翻译无关。

entries.definition: Relating to a polysome, a cluster of particles on one message; the unit is the ribosome, the cluster is the polysome.
entries.definitionCN: 与多聚核糖体相关；单位是核糖体，簇是多聚核糖体。

entries.definition: Relating to the nucleolus, where ribosomal RNA is transcribed and subunits begin assembly.
entries.definitionCN: 与核仁相关，那里转录 rRNA 并开始组装亚基。

entries.definition: Relating to translation as a process, including its control; ribosomal names the place, translational the stage.
entries.definitionCN: 与翻译这一过程及其调控相关；ribosomal 指场所，translational 指阶段。

entries.definition: Located in the cytoplasm, where free ribosomes work; it describes location rather than identity.
entries.definitionCN: 位于细胞质，游离核糖体在此工作；描述位置而非身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ribosome + -al: the same relational suffix as in natural and structural.
normal.cn: ribosome + -al：与 natural、structural 中的关系后缀相同。

normal.en: The family runs ribosome, ribosomal, rRNA, rDNA, polysome, ribozyme.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ribosome、ribosomal、rRNA、rDNA、polysome、ribozyme。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: ribosomal RNA, ribosomal protein, ribosomal subunit, ribosomal binding site.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：核糖体 RNA、核糖体蛋白、核糖体亚基、核糖体结合位点。

normal.en: Lab shorthand: rRNA is the RNA of the ribosome, tRNA is the carrier, mRNA is the message.
normal.cn: 实验室简称：rRNA 是核糖体的 RNA，tRNA 是搬运者，mRNA 是信使。

normal.en: The adjective also carries the '-al' words for other organelles: lysosomal, mitochondrial, nuclear.
normal.cn: 这个形容词也与其他细胞器的 -al 形容词并列：lysosomal、mitochondrial、nuclear。

abstract.en: Picture a machine whose parts are all stamped with the machine's own name.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器，其每个零件都打上这台机器的名字。

abstract.en: Picture two unequal halves that must click together before the work begins.
abstract.cn: 想象大小不等的两半必须先扣合才能开工。

abstract.en: Picture a core so old that every descendant still carries the same groove.
abstract.cn: 想象一个核心古老到每个后代都仍带着同一道槽。

examples.en: Ribosomal RNA is transcribed in the nucleolus and assembled with proteins.
examples.cn: 核糖体 RNA 在核仁中转录，并与蛋白质组装。

examples.en: A ribosomal mutation can make a bacterium resistant to one antibiotic class.
examples.cn: 核糖体突变可使细菌对某一类抗生素耐药。

examples.en: Ribosomal profiling showed that translation slowed within minutes of starvation.
examples.cn: 核糖体印迹显示饥饿数分钟内翻译就减慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「核糖体（ribosome）的 -al 尾巴」——凡修饰 rRNA、核糖体蛋白、亚基 → 核糖体的

root: ribo-（ribonucleic acid 缩略）+ 希腊 soma「身体」→ 英语 ribosome + 拉丁关系后缀 -alis → ribosomal。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one relational suffix: the particle as a whole, its ingredients, its two halves, its docking site, the genes behind it, the pathway it runs, the core it never changed, and the address drugs aim at.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个表关系的后缀散开：整个颗粒、其配料、两个亚基、停靠位点、背后的基因、所走的通路、从未改动的核心，以及药物瞄准的地址。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a translucent hood over the particle, tagging each RNA and protein part with the particle's own colour.
core.cn: 核心意象：颗粒外罩一层透明罩，把每个 RNA 与蛋白部件都染上颗粒自身的颜色。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: the simplest relational reading, 'of the ribosome'.
branches.cn: 整体：最简单的关系读法，「核糖体的」。

branches.en: PARTS: ingredients and subunits are named after the thing they compose.
branches.cn: 部件：配料与亚基用其所构成之物的名字命名。

branches.en: ADDRESSES: the docking sequence and the genes that encode the parts.
branches.cn: 地址：停靠序列与编码这些部件的基因。

branches.en: PATHWAY AND CORE: what the particle does, and the part evolution kept unchanged.
branches.cn: 通路与核心：颗粒所做的工作，以及演化未改动的部分。

branches.en: TARGET: pharmacology reads the same particle as a selective address.
branches.cn: 靶点：药理学把同一颗粒读成一个可选择性作用的地址。

intro.en: The word is English ribosome plus the Latin relational suffix -alis, kept in English as -al.
intro.cn: 该词是英语 ribosome 加拉丁关系后缀 -alis，在英语中保留为 -al。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix is Latin; the base is a modern blend of a chemical clipping and Greek soma. New Latin ribosomalis is a re-spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀是拉丁语；词干是现代把化学缩略与希腊 soma 混合的产物。新拉丁语 ribosomalis 只是改写拼法。

items.example: Ribosomal subunits assemble in the nucleolus.
items.exampleCN: 核糖体亚基在核仁中组装。

items.example: The peptide is ribosomally synthesized.
items.exampleCN: 该肽由核糖体合成。

items.example: Ribosomes are numerous in growing cells.
items.exampleCN: 生长中的细胞核糖体很多。

items.example: rRNA forms the scaffold of the subunit.
items.exampleCN: rRNA 构成亚基的支架。

items.example: rDNA repeats cluster on several chromosomes.
items.exampleCN: rDNA 重复序列聚集在数条染色体上。

items.example: Polysomal fractions were collected for sequencing.
items.exampleCN: 收集多聚核糖体组分用于测序。

items.example: Ribosomal proteins stabilise the RNA core.
items.exampleCN: 核糖体蛋白稳定 RNA 核心。

items.example: The binding site controls translation start.
items.exampleCN: 结合位点控制翻译起始。

latinEntries.structure: Greek soma (neuter noun, borrowed into New Latin)

definition_zh: 阻碍；妨碍；拖慢；阻挠
definition_en: to make progress, movement or an effort slower or more difficult
core_image: 一条窄路中间横着一块落石，后面的人只能一点点侧身挪过去
scene: 材料迟迟不到，工人只能在半成品旁边等，工期一天天往后推。 Late deliveries hindered progress on the upper floors.
sceneCN: 这里指拖慢工程的推进（第 1 个义项：阻碍进展）；句意为到货太晚妨碍了上层的施工进度。图中可辨识物件：横在路中的落石、侧身通过的人、堆着的半成品。

pos.zh: 阻碍；妨碍；拖慢

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示性质或结果的名词尾构成，义为「阻碍；障碍物」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「受妨碍的」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「起妨碍作用的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「阻碍者」（少用）
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以妨碍的方式」（少用）

senses.title: To slow a project
senses.definition: to make a project or task take longer by creating obstacles
senses.definitionCN: 通过制造障碍，让项目或任务花更长时间
senses.example: Missing permits hindered work on the site for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 缺少许可使工地施工拖了好几周。
senses.why: The core sense is being placed behind, and a delay puts a task behind schedule.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是「被放在后面」，而延误就是把任务放到进度后面。

senses.title: To block movement
senses.definition: to make it hard for someone or something to move forward
senses.definitionCN: 使人或物难以前进
senses.example: Fallen trees hindered the rescue teams in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树妨碍了山谷里的救援队。
senses.why: This is the physical picture at its simplest: something in the way, a body moving around it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的物理画面：有东西挡路，身体绕着走。

senses.title: To restrain growth
senses.definition: to keep an economy, market or organism from expanding at its potential rate
senses.definitionCN: 使经济、市场或生物体无法按潜在速度扩张
senses.example: Uncertain rules hindered investment in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 规则不明朗抑制了该地区的投资。
senses.why: Growth is a forward motion, and hindering puts weight on it.
senses.whyCN: 增长是向前运动，阻碍就是给它加上重量。

senses.title: To disrupt work or study
senses.definition: to interrupt concentration or routine so that output falls
senses.definitionCN: 打断专注或日常节奏，使产出下降
senses.example: Constant noise hindered her revision for the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 持续的噪声干扰了她的备考复习。
senses.why: Attention is a narrow path, and any obstruction on it costs time.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是一条窄路，路上任何阻碍都要花时间。

senses.title: To obstruct a plan
senses.definition: to act so that a proposal or decision cannot proceed as intended
senses.definitionCN: 采取行动，使提案或决定无法按计划推进
senses.example: Two members hindered the vote by raising procedural objections.
senses.exampleCN: 两名成员提出程序异议，阻挠了表决。
senses.why: Institutions run on procedure, so blocking a step is enough to hold the whole thing back.
senses.whyCN: 机构靠程序运转，卡住一步就足以拖住整件事。

senses.title: To stunt growth or recovery
senses.definition: to prevent a living thing or a recovery from reaching full development
senses.definitionCN: 使生物体或恢复过程无法充分发展
senses.example: Poor light hindered the seedlings after transplanting.
senses.exampleCN: 光照不足抑制了移栽后的幼苗生长。
senses.why: Biology uses the verb for anything that keeps a process below its natural curve.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用这个动词指任何让过程低于其自然曲线的因素。

senses.title: To make a task harder
senses.definition: to raise the effort or cost needed to complete something
senses.definitionCN: 提高完成某事所需的努力或成本
senses.example: The outdated software hindered every update.
senses.exampleCN: 过时的软件让每次更新都更难。
senses.why: Difficulty is friction, and the verb names the extra friction added.
senses.whyCN: 难度就是摩擦，这个词指被加上去的那份额外摩擦。

senses.title: To impair communication
senses.definition: to make exchange of information or cooperation less effective
senses.definitionCN: 使信息交换或合作效果变差
senses.example: Different reporting formats hindered coordination between teams.
senses.exampleCN: 不同的报表格式妨碍了各团队之间的协调。
senses.why: Coordination needs a clear channel, and hinder narrows it.
senses.whyCN: 协调需要畅通的通道，而这个词把它收窄。

intro.en: Hinder comes from Old English hindrian, to hold back, from hinder, meaning behind. The word is Germanic and has always kept the picture of being placed at the back.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古英语 hindrian「拦在后面」，出自 hinder「在后面」；属日耳曼语，始终保留「被放到后面」的画面。

items.en: The adverb meant behind or in the rear, and it is the same element seen in behind.
items.cn: 这个副词意为「在后面、在后部」，与 behind 中的成分相同。

items.en: The verb meant to keep back or delay, and it was used of people, animals and journeys.
items.cn: 这个动词意为拦阻、耽搁，用于人、牲畜与行程。

items.en: The spelling settled as hinder, and the noun hindrance grew beside it with the same vowel pattern.
items.cn: 拼写后来固定为 hinder，名词 hindrance 以相同的元音模式在旁边长成。

items.en: German hinter and English behind belong to the same Germanic background of rear position.
items.cn: 德语 hinter 与英语 behind 属同一日耳曼语「后位」背景。

items.en: The noun hind, a female deer, is a different word and must not be read into the verb.
items.cn: 名词 hind 指雌鹿，是另一个词，不能读进这个动词里。

items.en: The verb now takes abstract objects such as progress, growth and coordination more often than physical ones.
items.cn: 今天这个动词更多接进展、增长、协调这类抽象宾语，而非具体物。

note.en: The first group looks close or shares the behind root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of obstruction.
note.cn: 第一组与「hinder」形近或共享「在后」词根；第二组是与「阻挡」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for an obstacle or the act of holding something back.
entries.definitionCN: 指障碍物或拦截行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that has been held back.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指被拖住的。

entries.definition: At the back of something, the spatial core of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某物后面，正是这个动词的空间内核。

entries.definition: A female deer, especially of red deer; a different word despite the spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 指雌鹿，尤指红鹿；拼写近似但属另一个词。

entries.definition: The land behind a coast or a settled area, from German hinter.
entries.definitionCN: 指海岸或定居区后方的腹地，来自德语 hinter。

entries.definition: To slow or block progress, often by an obstacle in the way.
entries.definitionCN: 指拖慢或阻碍进展，常指路上有障碍。

entries.definition: To block a passage or a process deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 指故意堵塞通道或流程。

entries.definition: To make movement or work awkward, as if by loose equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 指使行动或工作别扭，像是被松散装备缠住。

entries.definition: To limit by rule rather than by obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 指用规则加以限制，而非用障碍。

entries.definition: To make something happen later than planned.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事比计划更晚发生。

entries.definition: To reduce speed without necessarily blocking the route.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低速度，未必堵住路线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the behind root, the old spelling pair behind and hinder, and the false friend hind.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「在后」词根、behind 与 hinder 这对古老拼写伙伴，以及易混的 hind。

normal.en: Hinder begins with the idea of behind, so it is to push something to the back of the queue.
normal.cn: 这个词从「在后面」起步，也就是把某事推到队尾。

normal.en: Behind and hinder share the same Germanic element of rear position.
normal.cn: behind 与 hinder 共享同一日耳曼语「后位」成分。

normal.en: The noun is hindrance, not hinderance, and the vowel changes.
normal.cn: 名词是 hindrance，不是 hinderance，元音有变化。

normal.en: Projects are hindered by missing permits, not by enemies.
normal.cn: 项目是被缺失的许可拖住的，而不是被敌人。

normal.en: Hind, the female deer, is a different word and a common trap.
normal.cn: hind 指雌鹿，是另一个词，也是常见的陷阱。

abstract.en: To hinder is to add distance between a person and the thing they were moving towards.
abstract.cn: 阻碍，就是在人和他要去的地方之间加上距离。

abstract.en: Most obstruction is not a wall but a small stone that makes every step cost more.
abstract.cn: 多数阻碍不是一堵墙，而是一块让每一步都更贵的小石头。

abstract.en: Whatever is put behind schedule was never stopped, only made late.
abstract.cn: 被放到进度后面的东西从未停止，只是被弄晚了。

examples.en: Heavy rain hindered the repair crews for two days.
examples.cn: 大雨使维修队受阻两天。

examples.en: Unclear ownership hindered the transfer of the land.
examples.cn: 权属不清妨碍了这块土地的转让。

examples.en: Lack of sleep hindered his concentration during the test.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足妨碍了他在测试中的专注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「辛德」——路中一块落石，后面的人侧身挪：阻碍、拖慢

root: 古英语 hinder「在后面」→ hindrian「拦阻、耽搁」；属日耳曼语，与 behind 同出「后位」义。名词 hindrance 为同族派生。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all put an obstacle in a path: a project, movement, growth, attention, a plan, a living thing, a task and coordination.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在一条路径上放置障碍：项目、移动、增长、注意力、计划、生物体、任务与协调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone sits in a narrow path and everyone behind it must edge past sideways.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块落石横在窄路上，后面的人只能侧身挪过去。

branches.en: THE SCHEDULE SLIPS: a project or an economy loses its forward pace.
branches.cn: 进度滑落：项目或经济失去向前的速度。

branches.en: THE PATH IS BLOCKED: a body or a vehicle cannot move freely.
branches.cn: 路径被堵：人或车辆无法自由移动。

branches.en: THE ATTENTION IS CUT: noise or interruption breaks the narrow channel of focus.
branches.cn: 注意力被截断：噪声或打断切断专注这条窄通道。

branches.en: THE DECISION IS STALLED: procedure is used to hold a proposal where it stands.
branches.cn: 决定被卡住：程序被用来把提案按在原处。

branches.en: THE PROCESS UNDERPERFORMS: growth, a task or coordination finishes below its natural level.
branches.cn: 过程发挥不足：生长、任务或协调低于其自然水平。

intro.en: Hinder is a Germanic verb, so its affixes are English endings rather than Latin ones.
intro.cn: 这是一个日耳曼语动词，其词缀是英语词尾而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this verb; the Latin column stays empty instead of borrowing unrelated forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词没有拉丁语来源，拉丁部分留空，不借无关形式来填。

items.example: The adverb is the spatial seed of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词是动词的空间种子。

items.example: It formed hindrian from the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它由副词构成 hindrian。

items.example: It keeps the same rear picture in modern English.
items.exampleCN: 它在现代英语里保留同一个「后位」画面。

items.example: It forms hindrance, the standard noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成标准名词 hindrance。

items.example: It forms hindered.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 hindered。

items.example: It forms hindering.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 hindering。

items.example: It forms the rare hinderer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成少用的 hinderer。

items.example: It forms the rare hinderingly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成少用的 hinderingly。
