definition_zh: 怀疑的；不轻信的；对某事持保留态度的；怀疑论的；显出怀疑的
definition_en: inclined to doubt a claim until evidence supports it, or showing that doubt openly
core_image: 一张递过来的宣传单摆在桌上，一只手按住它，另一只手先去翻背面密密麻麻的小字
scene: 听证会开始前，一位委员把厚厚的报告推到一边，要求先看原始数据再表态。 The committee remained skeptical of the summary until the raw records were released.
sceneCN: 这里指对某一说法持保留态度（第 1 个义项：不轻易相信的）；句意为委员会对那份摘要一直存疑，直到原始记录公布才松口。图中可辨识物件：厚报告、被推到一边的摘要、原始数据表、听证席。

pos.zh: 怀疑的；不轻信的；怀疑论的
（表情、语气）显出怀疑的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示主义、态度的名词尾构成，义为「怀疑态度；怀疑论」
由同一希腊词干构成，义为「持怀疑态度的人；怀疑论者」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「怀疑地」
英式拼写变体，义同「怀疑的」
英式拼写变体，义同「怀疑态度」

senses.title: Not easily convinced
senses.definition: refusing to accept a claim before evidence appears
senses.definitionCN: 在证据出现之前拒绝接受某个说法
senses.example: Investors were skeptical of the forecast until the third quarter numbers came out.
senses.exampleCN: 在第三季度数据公布之前，投资者对那份预测一直持怀疑态度。
senses.why: The Greek word behind it meant fond of looking closely, and looking closely is exactly what this sense asks for.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的希腊词意为「爱细看」，而这一义项要求的正是先细看再表态。

senses.title: Doubting one particular claim
senses.definition: doubting that a specific statement is true
senses.definitionCN: 怀疑某个具体陈述为真
senses.example: She was skeptical of his explanation that the delay was caused by weather.
senses.exampleCN: 他解释说延误是天气造成的，她对此表示怀疑。
senses.why: Here the doubt has an object: one named statement is held back from belief.
senses.whyCN: 这里的怀疑有明确对象：某个被点名的说法被暂时挡在信任之外。

senses.title: The habit of testing instead of accepting
senses.titleCN: 以检验代替接受的习惯
senses.definition: the working habit in research of testing claims rather than trusting them
senses.definitionCN: 研究中以检验主张代替直接相信的工作习惯
senses.example: A skeptical reviewer asked for the raw measurements behind the graph.
senses.exampleCN: 一位持怀疑态度的审稿人要求提供图表背后的原始测量数据。
senses.why: This sense names a method rather than a mood: doubt becomes a routine step in the work.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项指的不是情绪而是方法：怀疑成了工作流程里的固定一步。

senses.title: A doubtful expression
senses.definition: a look or tone that openly shows disbelief
senses.definitionCN: 公开显出不相信的神情或语气
senses.example: He raised one eyebrow and gave the salesman a skeptical look.
senses.exampleCN: 他挑起一边眉毛，用怀疑的神色看了推销员一眼。
senses.why: The feeling moves to the face, and the word can then describe the face itself.
senses.whyCN: 这种感受移到脸上，于是这个词也能直接描述那张脸。

senses.title: Doubtful about an outcome
senses.definition: doubting that something will actually happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 怀疑某事是否真会发生或成功
senses.example: Analysts are skeptical about a recovery before the end of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士对年底前出现复苏持怀疑态度。
senses.why: The object here is a future event, so the doubt is about likelihood rather than truth.
senses.whyCN: 这里怀疑的对象是未来的事件，所以怀疑的是可能性而不是真假。

senses.title: Unwilling to trust rank
senses.definition: unwilling to accept a person's word simply because of their position
senses.definitionCN: 不愿仅因某人的地位就接受其说法
senses.example: The young engineers were skeptical of the senior consultant's rule of thumb.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻工程师对那位资深顾问的经验法则并不买账。
senses.why: Doubt aimed at authority is a political as well as a mental act, and the word carries that edge.
senses.whyCN: 把怀疑对准权威，既是心理动作也是社会动作，这个词带着这股锋芒。

senses.title: The philosophical position
senses.definition: belonging to the philosophical view that certainty cannot be reached
senses.definitionCN: 属于「人无法获得确定知识」这一哲学立场
senses.example: The seminar compared skeptical and dogmatic answers to the same question.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课就同一个问题比较了怀疑论与独断论的两种回答。
senses.why: Ancient skepticism suspended judgment on purpose; this sense keeps that technical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 古代怀疑论是刻意悬置判断，这一义项保留的就是那个术语含义。

senses.title: Hard to move once convinced otherwise
senses.definition: needing strong evidence before giving up an existing view
senses.definitionCN: 要有强证据才肯放弃原有看法
senses.example: He stayed skeptical of the new method long after his colleagues had switched.
senses.exampleCN: 同事早就换了方法，他仍对新方法持怀疑态度，久久不肯改口。
senses.why: Doubt can harden into a position, and then the word describes a person who will not shift easily.
senses.whyCN: 怀疑也会硬化成立场，这时词就形容一个不容易松动的人。

senses.title: Trained professional doubt
senses.definition: a disciplined habit of checking claims that comes with a profession
senses.definitionCN: 随职业训练而来的、核查主张的审慎习惯
senses.example: Auditors are professionally skeptical, so a friendly email proves nothing to them.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师出于职业习惯而存疑，所以一封热情洋溢的邮件对他们毫无说服力。
senses.why: In fields where mistakes are costly, doubt is taught as a skill rather than felt as an emotion.
senses.whyCN: 在错误代价高昂的领域，怀疑是被训练出来的技能，而不是被感受到的情绪。

intro.en: Skeptical goes back to Greek skeptikos, fond of examining, from skeptesthai, to look at or consider. The name belonged to the ancient school that suspended judgment, passed through Latin and French, and entered English as a word for both a temperament and a method. The choice between the k and c spellings is a modern habit rather than an old distinction.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到希腊语「爱考察的」，出自动词「细看、考虑」。古代把判断悬置起来的学派以此得名，词经拉丁语与法语进入英语，既指一种性情也指一种方法。现代英语里美式与英式的拼写各走一路，这是后来的习惯，并非古已有之的分野。

items.en: Skepsis meant a careful looking at something, the act of a person who examines before speaking.
items.cn: 本义是对某物的一番细看，即先看过再开口的人所做的动作。

items.en: The adjective described someone fond of examining, and it named the philosophical school that refused to settle every question.
items.cn: 这个形容词形容爱考察的人，并成为那个拒绝为一切问题下结论的学派之名。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as a label for the school, keeping the idea of deliberate suspension of judgment.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借用为学派标签，保留了「有意悬置判断」的意思。

items.en: French carried the word into early modern debate, where it described both thinkers and a general temper.
items.cn: 法语把这个词带入近代早期的论争，既指思想家，也指一种普遍性情。

items.en: English adopted it as skeptical, first for the ancient school and soon for ordinary unwillingness to believe.
items.cn: 英语以这个形式吸收它，最初指古代学派，很快也指日常里的不肯轻信。

items.en: American usage settled on k while British usage kept c; the date at which the two spellings parted is uncertain.
items.cn: 美式用法自行定了一种拼法，英式用法保留了另一种；两种拼写分开的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root or looks close; the second group names other ways of withholding belief.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊词根或形近；第二组指其他「不肯相信」的说法。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的英式拼写。

entries.definition: The attitude or doctrine of doubting claims.
entries.definitionCN: 怀疑主张的态度或学说。

entries.definition: A person who doubts claims as a matter of habit.
entries.definitionCN: 习惯性怀疑各种说法的人。

entries.definition: Infected or causing infection; it comes from the Greek word for decay, not from looking.
entries.definitionCN: 指感染的或引起感染的；出自希腊语「腐坏」，与「细看」无关。

entries.definition: A striking public sight; its root means to look at as a spectacle, a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指引人注目的公开景象；其词根是「观看」，属另一动词。

entries.definition: Unsure whether something is true, often with a hint of worry.
entries.definitionCN: 指不确定某事是否为真，常带一丝担忧。

entries.definition: Causing or feeling doubt, often about honesty.
entries.definitionCN: 指令人起疑或自己存疑，常涉及诚信。

entries.definition: Suspecting that something is wrong or hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 指怀疑有错或有隐情。

entries.definition: Unable or unwilling to believe what one hears, often with surprise.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法或不愿相信所听之事，常带惊讶。

entries.definition: Still not persuaded after hearing the case.
entries.definitionCN: 指听完理由后仍未被说服。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the held-down leaflet, the raised eyebrow, the reviewer's raw data and the professional audit.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用按住传单的画面、挑起的眉毛、审稿人要原始数据与职业审计四个场景。

normal.en: A skeptical reader turns the page over before believing the headline.
normal.cn: 怀疑的读者会先把纸翻到背面，再决定信不信标题。

normal.en: One raised eyebrow is the cheapest form of cross-examination.
normal.cn: 挑一下眉毛，是最省力的交叉询问。

normal.en: Skeptical of a claim, not of the person, is the useful version.
normal.cn: 怀疑某个说法而不是某个人，才是有用的版本。

normal.en: A skeptical reviewer asks for the numbers behind the graph.
normal.cn: 持怀疑态度的审稿人，会要图表背后的数字。

normal.en: Professionally skeptical auditors treat a warm email as noise.
normal.cn: 职业性存疑的审计师，把热情邮件当作噪音。

abstract.en: Doubt is a door held ajar: it lets evidence in without letting belief run out.
abstract.cn: 怀疑是一扇虚掩的门：让证据进得来，又不让信念跑光。

abstract.en: Every field that fears error builds a small ritual of skepticism into its day.
abstract.cn: 每个害怕出错的领域，都会在日常里安放一套小小的怀疑仪式。

abstract.en: The same word covers a mood and a method, because a mood repeated becomes a method.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指情绪又指方法，因为情绪重复久了就成了方法。

examples.en: Many scientists remain skeptical of results that no other lab has repeated.
examples.cn: 许多科学家对没有其他实验室复现的结果仍持怀疑态度。

examples.en: She gave the offer a skeptical glance and asked who would pay for the move.
examples.cn: 她怀疑地看了一眼那份报价，问搬迁费由谁出。

examples.en: A skeptical attitude is a requirement of the job, not a personality flaw.
examples.cn: 怀疑的态度是这份工作的要求，而不是性格缺陷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「斯凯普提扣」：事事都要先「细看」一遍的人，别人说得再顺耳也要「扣」一下再信

root: 源于希腊语中表示「细看、考察」的动词，先指爱考察的人，再指把判断悬置起来的古代学派；词经拉丁语与法语进入英语。现代英语用不同字母拼写，是后来的习惯分化，分界年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from a general temper to a trained method: unwillingness to believe, doubt aimed at one claim, the research habit, the doubtful face, doubt about an outcome, distrust of rank, the philosophical school, a hardened position, and professional checking.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一般性情走到训练有素的方法：不肯轻信、针对某个说法的怀疑、研究习惯、怀疑的神情、对结果的怀疑、不信权威、哲学学派、已经硬化的立场，以及职业性的核查。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pins the leaflet to the table and the other hand turns it over to read the small print before nodding.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把传单按在桌上，另一只手先翻到背面读小字，然后才点头。

branches.en: THE HELD-BACK YES: belief is kept back until the evidence arrives.
branches.cn: 按住的「好」：证据到来之前，信任先不给出。

branches.en: THE TRAINED CHECK: the same doubt, repeated as a professional routine.
branches.cn: 训练有素的核查：同一种怀疑，重复成职业惯例。

branches.en: THE FACE AND THE FORECAST: doubt worn openly, whether about a claim or an outcome.
branches.cn: 神情与预测：无论针对说法还是结果，怀疑都写在明处。

branches.en: THE HARD POSITION: refusal to yield to rank, and refusal to yield at all.
branches.cn: 硬化的立场：不向地位让步，也不肯再让步。

branches.en: THE ANCIENT SCHOOL: judgment suspended on principle.
branches.cn: 古代学派：出于原则而悬置判断。

intro.en: Skeptical is a Greek examining word wearing an English adjective ending; its family covers the person, the attitude and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语「考察」之词加上英语形容词尾，词族覆盖「人」「态度」与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin passed the Greek label for the doubting school into French, and English took it in both spellings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把怀疑学派的希腊标签传给法语，英语则把两种拼写都吸收了进来。

items.example: The act that gives the whole family its name.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族由这个动作得名。

items.example: The oldest member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族里最古老的一员。

items.example: It named both a temper and a school.
items.exampleCN: 它既指一种性情，也指一个学派。

items.example: Latin fixed it as a philosophical label.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把它固定为哲学标签。

items.example: It turns the label into an everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个标签变成日常形容词。

items.example: It produces the name of the attitude.
items.exampleCN: 它构成这种态度的名称。

items.meaning: a person or thing of that kind
items.example: It produces the name of the doubting person.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「持怀疑者」的名称。

items.example: It produces the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成副词。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词干加表示学说的名词尾构成，义为「怀疑态度；怀疑论」
由同一希腊词干构成，义为「持怀疑态度的人」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「怀疑地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「怀疑的性质」，较少用

definition_zh: 由于；因为；归因于；应付给；预定于
definition_en: because of, caused by; owed to a person or account; expected or scheduled to do something
core_image: 雾封住跑道，登机屏上一条条航班被划掉，旅客拖着箱子围在柜台前改签
scene: 清晨大雾封住机场，广播通知当天航班全部取消，旅客只能排队改签。 All departures were cancelled due to thick fog.
sceneCN: 这里把结果回指到天气原因（第 1 个义项：由于、因为）；句意为所有出港航班因浓雾取消。图中可辨识物件：跑道灯、雾墙、登机屏、行李箱。

pos.zh: 介词短语：由于；因为（可作表语、后置定语，也可置于句首）

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根直接作形容词，义为「到期的；应支付的；预定的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「按时地；适当地」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「过度的；不当的」
由表示「超过」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「逾期的；早该发生的」
由形容词转作名词并加复数词尾，义为「会费；应缴费用」

senses.title: Because of a stated cause
senses.definition: as a result of a cause that is named after the result
senses.definitionCN: 由于句中已说明的原因而出现某种结果
senses.example: The match was abandoned due to rain.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛因雨取消。
senses.why: The adjective behind the phrase meant owed, so the phrase points from a result back to what it owes its existence to.
senses.whyCN: 短语背后的形容词本义是「被欠的」，因此整条短语从结果回指它所亏欠的原因。

senses.title: After the verb be: attributable to
senses.definition: used after be to say that a result can be attributed to something
senses.definitionCN: 跟在系动词之后，说明结果可归因于某事
senses.example: The delay was due to a fault in the signal system.
senses.exampleCN: 延误是由于信号系统故障造成的。
senses.why: Traditional grammar treats the phrase as adjectival, so it sits after be and explains the subject.
senses.whyCN: 传统语法把它当作形容词性成分，因此跟在系动词后解释主语。

senses.title: Placed after a noun as a modifier
senses.definition: following a noun to identify the cause of that noun
senses.definitionCN: 跟在名词之后，指出该名词的原因
senses.example: Accidents due to fatigue fell sharply after the new rota.
senses.exampleCN: 因疲劳导致的事故在新排班后大幅下降。
senses.why: Modifying a noun directly, the phrase works like a shortened relative clause.
senses.whyCN: 直接修饰名词时，这条短语相当于压缩后的关系从句。

senses.title: Opening a sentence in formal writing
senses.definition: introducing the cause at the start of a clause, common in reports and academic prose
senses.definitionCN: 在句首引出原因，多见于报告与学术文体
senses.example: Due to limited storage, samples were processed within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 由于存储条件有限，样品在一周内处理完毕。
senses.why: Sentence-initial use spread through scientific and administrative writing while the old adjectival rule loosened.
senses.whyCN: 句首用法在科技与行政写作中扩散，同时旧的形容词性规则被放宽。

senses.title: Money owed to someone
senses.definition: in accounting, an amount that is owed and payable to a person or supplier
senses.definitionCN: 会计中应付给个人或供应商的款项
senses.example: The ledger lists amounts due to contractors.
senses.exampleCN: 账簿列出应付给承包商的款项。
senses.why: The older sense of owed survives in finance, where the phrase keeps the creditor as its object.
senses.whyCN: 「应支付」的旧义在财务中保留，短语后面接的正是收款方。

senses.title: Expected at a fixed time
senses.definition: with a verb of arrival or departure, expected or scheduled at a stated time
senses.definitionCN: 与表示到达或出发的动词连用，指预定在某时发生
senses.example: The train is due to arrive at six.
senses.exampleCN: 列车定于六点到达。
senses.why: Here owed refers to an obligation written into a timetable, and the infinitive names the scheduled event.
senses.whyCN: 此处「应」指写进时刻表的义务，后面的不定式说明预定动作。

senses.title: The padded connector due to the fact that
senses.titleCN: 累赘连接语「由于……这一事实」
senses.definition: a wordy way of introducing a clause, often criticised in editing guides
senses.definitionCN: 引出从句的冗长说法，编辑指南常批评其累赘
senses.example: Sales rose due to the fact that the currency weakened.
senses.exampleCN: 销售上升是由于货币走弱这一事实。
senses.why: When the cause is a full clause rather than a noun, writers pad the phrase instead of using because.
senses.whyCN: 当原因是一个完整从句而非名词时，写作者便把这个短语撑长，而不用「因为」。

senses.title: Blame placed on a named factor
senses.definition: used to attribute an unwanted outcome to a single factor, often in official statements
senses.definitionCN: 把不好的结果归到某一因素，常见于官方说明
senses.example: The outage was due to a single misconfigured server.
senses.exampleCN: 这次服务中断是由于一台服务器配置错误。
senses.why: Attribution language lets an institution name a factor without naming the person responsible.
senses.whyCN: 归因说法让机构能点出因素而不点出责任人。

senses.title: Interchangeable with the other causal phrase
senses.titleCN: 与其他因果短语可互换
senses.definition: used as a plain causal preposition in modern speech, where the older placement rule is ignored
senses.definitionCN: 现代口语中当作普通因果介词使用，旧的语法位置规则被忽略
senses.example: Due to a shortage of nurses, the ward closed early.
senses.exampleCN: 由于护士不足，病房提前关闭。
senses.why: Both causal phrases descend from the language of debt, and speakers now treat them alike.
senses.whyCN: 两个因果短语都出自「欠」的说法，说话人如今把它们同样对待。

intro.en: Due to joins the adjective due, meaning owed, with the preposition to. Due entered English through Old French deu, the past participle of devoir, to owe, from Latin debere, to owe, built from de-, away, and habere, to hold. The causal phrase grew out of the idea of something being owed to a cause.
intro.cn: 这个短语由义为「应支付、应归」的形容词与介词合成。形容词经古法语进入英语，是表示「欠」的动词的过去分词，源头为拉丁语中同样表示「欠」的动词，由表示「离开」的前缀与表示「持有」的词根构成。因果义正是从「应归到某个原因」这一想法长出来的。

items.en: Habere meant to hold or have; with the prefix of removal it produced the verb meaning to owe, literally to hold something away from someone.
items.cn: 这个词意为持有、拥有；加上表示「拿走」的前缀后，构成表示「欠」的动词，字面是「把东西拿离某人」。

items.en: Debere meant to owe, and its participle described a sum that is owed.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「欠」，其分词用来形容一笔应付款项。

items.en: The Old French past participle carried the sense of owed into English, where it became the adjective due.
items.cn: 古法语的过去分词把「被欠的」这一意思带进英语，成为形容词。

items.en: English due first described what is owed, then what is owed by a timetable, as in a train due at six.
items.cn: 英语中这个词先指「应支付的」，再指「按时刻表应到的」，例如六点应到的列车。

items.en: The combination began to serve as a preposition of cause in the nineteenth century; its first attestation in that role is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 这一组合在十九世纪开始充当表示原因的介词；它进入这一角色的确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Traditional guides insisted that the phrase follow the verb be, while modern usage allows it at the start of a sentence.
items.cn: 传统指南坚持它必须跟在系动词之后，现代用法则允许它出现在句首。

note.en: The first group shares the phrase frame or the same root; the second group names other ways of stating a cause.
note.cn: 第一组与本短语共享短语框架或同一词根；第二组是其他表示原因的说法。

entries.definition: Scheduled to receive or undergo something soon.
entries.definitionCN: 指预定不久将得到或经历某事。

entries.definition: In accounting, an amount owed by a debtor to the firm.
entries.definitionCN: 会计中指债务人欠本企业的款项，方向与「应付」相反。

entries.definition: The date by which a payment or task must be finished.
entries.definitionCN: 指付款或任务必须完成的日期。

entries.definition: Regular payments required for membership.
entries.definitionCN: 指会员须定期缴纳的费用。

entries.definition: A verb phrase meaning to perform an action on something, which sounds almost the same.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物施加动作的动词短语，读音几乎相同，结构却完全不同。

entries.definition: Because of; the phrase moves more freely in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 由于；在句中的位置更自由。

entries.definition: The most neutral causal preposition, followed by a noun or pronoun.
entries.definitionCN: 最中性的因果介词，后接名词或代词。

entries.definition: Because of, often in formal or explanatory writing.
entries.definitionCN: 由于，多用于正式或解释性文字。

entries.definition: Following from a cause, with the result brought into focus.
entries.definitionCN: 由于……的结果，把结果放在焦点上。

entries.definition: Because of, usually with a fortunate or welcome result.
entries.definitionCN: 多亏，通常引出积极结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the debt word behind the phrase and its two grammar positions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着短语背后的「欠」义，串起固定搭配与两种语法位置。

normal.en: The adjective came from a word meaning owed, so the phrase points to what a result owes its existence to.
normal.cn: 这个形容词本义是「欠」，所以短语指出结果欠了谁才得以发生。

normal.en: After the verb be is the safe position; at the start of a sentence is the looser modern move.
normal.cn: 跟在系动词之后最稳妥；放在句首则是较宽松的现代用法。

normal.en: Amounts owed to suppliers is the accounting sense, where the phrase still means owed.
normal.cn: 「应付给供应商的款项」是会计用法，短语仍保留「欠」的意思。

normal.en: A train due at six keeps the timetable sense of a scheduled obligation.
normal.cn: 六点应到的列车保留的是时刻表上的「应到」义务。

normal.en: The padded connector is the version editors tell writers to replace with a single conjunction.
normal.cn: 「由于……这一事实」是被编辑要求改写成单个连词的累赘版本。

abstract.en: Debt and cause have the same shape: something is owed, and the cause is the creditor.
abstract.cn: 债务与因果是同一个形状：有东西被欠着，而原因就是债主。

abstract.en: A sentence may move the cause to the front, but the grammar of attribution stays behind.
abstract.cn: 句子可以把原因挪到最前面，但归因的语法始终留在原处。

abstract.en: Every explanatory phrase is a small accounting of why things happened.
abstract.cn: 每个解释性短语都是对「事情为何发生」所做的一笔小账。

examples.en: The flight was cancelled due to a technical fault.
examples.cn: 航班因技术故障取消。

examples.en: Due to heavy snow, the pass remained closed for three days.
examples.cn: 由于大雪，山口封闭了三天。

examples.en: She is due to present the findings next Friday.
examples.cn: 她预定下周五报告研究结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「丢图」——图纸丢了，工期延误，追查原因就是「由于」：由于、因为

root: 形容词经古法语的过去分词形式来自拉丁语 debere「欠」，由表示「离开、向下」的前缀与表示「持有」的词根构成；这条短语的介词用法自十九世纪起流行，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses fall into four places: the cause itself, three grammatical positions, the money owed, and the timetable obligation.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项落在四处：原因本身、三种语法位置、应付的款项、时刻表上的应到。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fog-bound airport board, every cancelled flight tied back to the weather.
core.cn: 核心意象：雾锁机场的航班屏，每条被划掉的航班都系回天气。

branches.en: THE PLAIN CAUSE: the phrase opens or closes a clause and names why something happened.
branches.cn: 单纯原因：短语在句首或句末点明事情为何发生。

branches.en: THE ATTRIBUTIVE POSITION: after the verb be or after a noun, the phrase explains the subject.
branches.cn: 归属性位置：跟在系动词或名词之后，解释主语。

branches.en: THE SUM OWED: in accounts the phrase still points to a creditor.
branches.cn: 应付之款：在账目里，短语仍指向收款方。

branches.en: THE TIMETABLE: the same adjective marks what is expected at a fixed hour.
branches.cn: 时刻表：同一个形容词标记按固定时刻应到之事。

branches.en: THE PADDED AND ATTRIBUTED CAUSE: the heavy connector, the official excuse, and the stylistic variant.
branches.cn: 累赘与归因：冗长连接语、机构式交代、以及文体变体。

intro.en: The phrase rests on a Latin verb of owing, so its parts are small pieces of a debt.
intro.cn: 这条短语立在一个表示「欠」的拉丁动词上，各部件都是债务的一小块。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb of owing, the verb of holding and the prefix of removal; Old French supplied the participle that became the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「欠」的动词、「持有」的词根与表示「拿走」的前缀；古法语提供了变成形容词的分词。

items.example: A debt is literally what is held away from a person.
items.exampleCN: 债务字面上就是被拿离某人的东西。

items.example: It turns holding into owing.
items.exampleCN: 它把「持有」变成「欠」。

items.example: The root carries the idea of having something in hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「手中有物」的意思。

items.example: It entered English as the adjective due.
items.exampleCN: 它作为形容词进入英语。

items.example: The adjective carries both the debt and the timetable sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时背着债务与时刻表两种意思。

items.example: It links the adjective to the cause or the creditor.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词挂到原因或收款方上。

items.example: It forms the adverb meaning on time or properly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示按时或适当的副词。

items.example: It forms the adjective meaning excessive or improper.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示过度或不当的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective meaning past the due date.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示逾期的形容词。

items.example: The whole phrase works as a causal preposition.
items.exampleCN: 整条短语充当因果介词。

由形容词转作名词并加复数词尾，义为「会费；应缴费用」

definition_zh: 星际的；恒星之间的；穿越恒星之间的
definition_en: located between or travelling between the stars
core_image: 两枚亮星之间是一段几乎空无一物、却漂着细尘与气体的黑色长路
scene: 看着两枚亮星之间那片看不见尽头的黑，你说 Interstellar space is not entirely empty.
sceneCN: 这里 interstellar 指「位于恒星之间的」（第 1 个义项：两星之间的空间区域）；句意为星际空间并非完全空无一物。图中可辨识物件：两枚亮星、中间的黑色空间、漂着的细尘、远处的微光。

pos.zh: 星际的；恒星之间的

senses.title: Between the stars
senses.definition: located in the space between stars
senses.definitionCN: 位于恒星之间的空间
senses.example: Interstellar space is not entirely empty.
senses.exampleCN: 星际空间并非完全空无一物。
senses.why: the adjective is literal: inter- 'between' plus stellar 'of stars', so it marks the region that belongs to no single star.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词是字面组合：inter-「在……之间」加 stellar「恒星的」，标出不属于任何单颗恒星的那片区域。

senses.title: The matter between stars
senses.titleCN: 恒星之间的物质：星际介质
senses.definition: the gas, dust, radiation and magnetic fields filling the space between stars
senses.definitionCN: 填满恒星之间空间的气体、尘埃、辐射与磁场
senses.example: The interstellar medium is thinner than any laboratory vacuum.
senses.exampleCN: 星际介质比任何实验室真空都稀薄。
senses.why: once the space was found not to be empty, a noun was needed for its contents, and medium supplied that neutral word.
senses.whyCN: 在发现空间并不空之后，需要给其中的内容一个名词，medium 提供了这个中性的词。

senses.title: Travel from star to star
senses.definition: relating to journeys or missions that cross the space between stars
senses.definitionCN: 与穿越恒星之间空间的航行或任务有关
senses.example: Interstellar travel remains far beyond current engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 星际旅行仍远超现有工程能力。
senses.why: the adjective extends from place to motion: what lies between stars also describes the trip across them.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从「地点」扩展到「运动」：位于恒星之间的空间也用来描述穿越它的旅程。

senses.title: An object from another star system
senses.titleCN: 来自另一个恒星系统的天体
senses.definition: describing a comet or asteroid that entered our system from another star
senses.definitionCN: 描述从另一颗恒星系统进入我们系统的彗星或小行星
senses.example: The first known interstellar object passed through in 2017.
senses.exampleCN: 已知的第一个星际天体在 2017 年穿过太阳系。
senses.why: if an object came from between the stars, the adjective marks its origin rather than its position.
senses.whyCN: 若某天体来自恒星之间，这个形容词标的是它的来源，而非当前位置。

senses.title: Dust that dims starlight
senses.titleCN: 使星光变暗的星际尘埃
senses.definition: describing the absorption and reddening of starlight by dust between stars
senses.definitionCN: 描述星光被恒星之间的尘埃吸收与变红
senses.example: Interstellar extinction makes distant stars look redder.
senses.exampleCN: 星际消光让遥远的恒星看起来更红。
senses.why: the dust is in the way, so the adjective names the medium that interferes with the light rather than the light itself.
senses.whyCN: 尘埃挡在光路上，因此这个形容词指的是干扰光的介质，而非光本身。

senses.title: Chemistry in the space between stars
senses.titleCN: 星际空间中的分子与化学
senses.definition: describing molecules, reactions or chemistry occurring in interstellar clouds
senses.definitionCN: 描述发生在星际云中的分子、反应或化学过程
senses.example: Astronomers have found interstellar molecules in cold clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家在冷云中发现了星际分子。
senses.why: chemistry needs a vessel, and the cold clouds between stars turned out to be that vessel.
senses.whyCN: 化学反应需要一个容器，而恒星之间的冷云正是这个容器。

senses.title: Signals across the gap
senses.definition: relating to radio or other signals sent across interstellar distances
senses.definitionCN: 与跨越星际距离发送的无线电或其他信号有关
senses.example: Interstellar communication raises questions no treaty answers.
senses.exampleCN: 星际通讯提出了一些条约无法回答的问题。
senses.why: communication is the human use of the same gap, so the adjective also qualifies the messages sent across it.
senses.whyCN: 通讯是人类对同一段空隙的利用，因此这个形容词也修饰跨越其间的讯息。

senses.title: Figurative: a gap too wide to cross
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：宽到跨不过去的间隔
senses.definition: a figurative use for a distance or difference so large that it seems to separate two worlds
senses.definitionCN: 比喻过大、几乎像隔开两个世界的距离或差异
senses.example: An interstellar gap opened between the two departments.
senses.exampleCN: 两个部门之间裂开了一道星际般的鸿沟。
senses.why: the metaphor borrows the scale of the sky: a gap measured in light-years is beyond ordinary reach.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了天空的尺度：以光年计的空隙，超出日常可达的范围。

intro.en: Interstellar is Latin inter 'between' plus stellar 'of stars', a scientific compound formed in English rather than inherited whole. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: interstellar 是拉丁 inter「在……之间」加 stellar「恒星的」，属英语中形成的科学复合词，而非整体承继而来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Inter is the Latin preposition 'between, among'; it survives in many English compounds such as international and interval.
items.cn: inter 是拉丁介词「在……之间、在……之中」；它活在许多英语复合词中，如 international 与 interval。

items.en: Stella 'star' and its adjective stellaris 'of stars' supply the second half; stellar entered English through scientific Latin.
items.cn: stella「星」及其形容词 stellaris「恒星的」提供后半；stellar 经科学拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Interstellar is generally believed to have been formed in English scientific writing in the seventeenth century, once the space between stars became an object of study.
items.cn: 一般认为，interstellar 在 17 世纪的英语科学写作中形成，当时恒星之间的空间开始成为研究对象。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective attached itself to medium, dust, travel and communication as those fields developed.
items.cn: 20 世纪，随着相关领域的发展，这个形容词依次附着在 medium、dust、travel、communication 之前。

items.en: Root uncertainty: the Indo-European form behind stella is a reconstruction. First-date uncertainty only: the earliest printed use of interstellar is not exactly dated and is usually placed in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 词根存疑：stella 背后的印欧形式属重构。仅首见年代存疑：interstellar 的最早印刷用例没有确切年代，通常定在 17 世纪。

note.en: Group one holds compounds built on the same inter- prefix; group two holds the near adjectives that describe neighbouring kinds of space.
note.cn: 第一组是同用 inter- 前缀的复合词；第二组是描述相邻空间类别的近义形容词。

entries.definition: Inter- plus planetary: it covers the space inside a solar system, a much smaller scale than interstellar.
entries.definitionCN: inter- 加 planetary：指太阳系内的空间，尺度远小于星际。

entries.definition: Inter- plus galactic: it covers the space between whole galaxies, one scale larger than interstellar.
entries.definitionCN: inter- 加 galactic：指整个星系之间的空间，比星际大一个尺度。

entries.definition: Without the prefix it describes a single star's properties; interstellar is about the space that belongs to no star.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉前缀后它描述单颗恒星的性质；interstellar 说的是不属于任何恒星的空间。

entries.definition: The gas and dust within a planetary system; the interstellar medium begins where the solar wind stops.
entries.definitionCN: 行星系统内部的气体与尘埃；星际介质从太阳风终止之处开始。

entries.definition: An informal term for space far from earth; it is not a precise scale and does not name what lies between stars.
entries.definitionCN: 指远离地球的太空的非正式说法；它不是精确尺度，也不特指恒星之间。

entries.definition: The general term for space beyond the atmosphere, including but not limited to interstellar regions.
entries.definitionCN: 指大气层外太空的通用词，包含但不限于星际区域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: inter- 'between' + stellar 'of stars': between stars.
normal.cn: inter-「之间」+ stellar「恒星的」：恒星之间的。

normal.en: Three scales: interplanetary, interstellar, intergalactic.
normal.cn: 三个尺度：行星际、星际、星系际。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: interstellar medium, dust, travel.
normal.cn: 固定短语：星际介质、星际尘埃、星际旅行。

normal.en: The base adjective is stellar.
normal.cn: 基础形容词是 stellar。

normal.en: The prefix inter- also builds international and interval.
normal.cn: 前缀 inter- 还构成 international 与 interval。

abstract.en: Picture two lamps at opposite ends of a dark hall with dust in the air between them.
abstract.cn: 想象暗厅两端各有一盏灯，中间空气里浮着尘。

abstract.en: Picture a message that must cross a void no rope can span.
abstract.cn: 想象一条必须穿过无绳可系的虚空才能送达的消息。

abstract.en: Picture two neighbours so far apart that they never hear each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个邻居相隔太远，永远听不见对方。

examples.en: Interstellar dust reddens the light of distant stars.
examples.cn: 星际尘埃使遥远星光变红。

examples.en: No spacecraft has yet achieved interstellar travel.
examples.cn: 尚无航天器实现星际旅行。

examples.en: The interstellar medium is mostly hydrogen and helium.
examples.cn: 星际介质主要是氢与氦。

root: 拉丁 inter「在……之间」+ 拉丁 stella「星」的形容词 stellaris→stellar；17 世纪英语科学复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gap: the space between stars, the matter in it, the journey across it, an object arriving from it, the dust that dims light, the chemistry inside it, the signals sent through it and finally any gap too wide to cross.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一段空隙展开：恒星之间的空间；其中的物质、穿越它的航行、从它而来的天体、使光变暗的尘埃、其中的化学、穿它而过的讯号，最后是任何宽到跨不过的间隔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long dark road between two lamps, with fine dust drifting along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：两盏灯之间一条很长的暗路，细尘沿路飘着。

branches.en: PLACE AND CONTENTS: the region, and the gas and dust that fill it.
branches.cn: 地点与内容：那片区域，以及填满它的气体与尘埃。

branches.en: MOVEMENT AND MESSAGES: journeys and signals that cross the gap.
branches.cn: 运动与讯息：穿越空隙的航行与信号。

branches.en: FOREIGN ORIGIN: an object whose address is another star system.
branches.cn: 外来来源：地址在另一个恒星系统的天体。

branches.en: WHAT LIES IN THE WAY: dust that dims light and clouds where molecules form.
branches.cn: 挡在路上的东西：使光变暗的尘埃，以及形成分子的云。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any distance that separates two worlds.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何把两个世界隔开的距离。

intro.en: Interstellar is prefix plus adjective, and both halves belong to Latin; the prefix is highly productive in English.
intro.cn: interstellar 是前缀加形容词，两半都属拉丁语；这个前缀在英语中构词力很强。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter 'between' gives interplanetary and intergalactic; Latin stella gives stellar, constellation and stellate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 inter「之间」给出 interplanetary 与 intergalactic；拉丁 stella 给出 stellar、constellation、stellate。

items.example: The prefix marks position between two things.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出位于两物之间。

items.example: The root supplies the second half.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供后半。

items.example: Stellar is the free adjective used here.
items.exampleCN: stellar 是此处使用的自由形容词。

items.example: The compound is formed in English from Latin parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词由拉丁部件在英语中构成。

items.example: Medium is the Latin word for the middle or a substance.
items.exampleCN: medium 是拉丁语中「中间」或「物质」的词。

items.example: Space is a native English noun.
items.exampleCN: space 是英语本族名词。

items.example: The same prefix at a smaller scale.
items.exampleCN: 同一前缀，较小尺度。

items.exampleCN: 同一前缀，较大尺度。

items.example: The prefix also appears in older Latin compounds.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也出现在更早的拉丁复合词中。

definition_en: to have something as one's source, whether a word, a substance, a conclusion, a species or a set of data
core_image: 一条河从远处的山脚出发，分成许多支流，最后每一股细流都能沿着水痕倒着追回同一个源头
scene: 词源课上，老师把一张写满古代写本的幻灯片推到学生面前，说明黑板上那个词并非本地自造。 The term can be derived from an older trade word recorded in port ledgers of the fifteenth century.

senses.title: Traced back in language
senses.definition: to have an earlier word or form as one's linguistic source
senses.definitionCN: 以某个更早的词或词形作为语言上的来源
senses.example: The technical term algebra can be derived from an Arabic word for reunion.
senses.exampleCN: 术语「代数」可以追溯到阿拉伯语中表示「重新结合」的词。
senses.why: The core verb meant to draw off water from a channel, and a word drawn from an older word follows the same course.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「从水道引水」，一个词从更早的词引出来，走的是同一条路。

senses.title: Extracted chemically
senses.definition: to be obtained from a substance by a physical or chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 通过物理或化学过程从某种物质中取得
senses.example: The yellow dye can be derived from the roots of a common roadside plant.
senses.exampleCN: 这种黄色染料可以从一种常见路边植物的根中提取。
senses.why: The stream image is literal here: a substance is drawn out of a larger body, as water is led off from a channel.
senses.whyCN: 这里用的是字面的引水意象：物质从更大的主体中被引出，如水从水道被引开。

senses.title: Inferred from premises
senses.definition: to be reached by logical steps from stated assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 由已陈述的假设经逻辑步骤得出
senses.example: The final theorem must be derived from the three axioms stated at the beginning.
senses.exampleCN: 最终的定理必须由开头陈述的三条公理推导出来。
senses.why: A conclusion is drawn out of premises the way water is drawn from a channel: the result was already implicit in the source.
senses.whyCN: 结论从前提中被引出，正如水从水道被引开：结果本已隐含在来源之中。

senses.title: Evolved from an ancestor
senses.definition: to have descended from an earlier species or population
senses.definitionCN: 由更早的物种或种群演化而来
senses.example: Modern maize is believed to be derived from a wild grass of Central America.
senses.exampleCN: 现代玉米被认为源自中美洲的一种野生禾草。
senses.why: A species is a later branch of an older line, so the modern form can be traced back along the same channel.
senses.whyCN: 物种是旧谱系较晚的分支，现代形态因此能沿同一条水道回溯。

senses.title: Produced from raw material
senses.definition: to be manufactured from a particular starting material
senses.definitionCN: 由某种起始材料加工制成
senses.example: Most of the paper in the archive can be derived from cotton rags rather than wood pulp.
senses.exampleCN: 档案里的大部分纸张原料取自棉布碎料，而非木浆。
senses.why: Paper is drawn out of rags the way a product is drawn out of its raw material.
senses.whyCN: 纸从碎布中被造出，正如产品从原料中被造出。

senses.title: Taken from a data source
senses.definition: to come from a stated survey, sample or record
senses.definitionCN: 来自明确交代的调查、样本或记录
senses.example: The figures in the table should be derived from the same survey sample.
senses.exampleCN: 表中的数字应取自同一份调查样本。
senses.why: Numbers are drawn from one survey, and the survey is the channel they all flow from.
senses.whyCN: 数字从同一份调查中取出，那份调查就是它们共同的渠道。

senses.title: Inherited from an earlier system
senses.definition: to be inherited from rules or arrangements established earlier
senses.definitionCN: 承袭自更早确立的规则或安排
senses.example: The court's procedure may be derived from rules laid down in the previous century.
senses.exampleCN: 该法院的程序可能承袭自上个世纪定下的规则。
senses.why: A rule inherited from an older code follows the same stream backwards to its source.
senses.whyCN: 从旧法典承袭的规则，沿同一条水流回溯到它的源头。

senses.title: Adapted from an earlier work
senses.definition: to be taken and reworked from an existing text, tune or design
senses.definitionCN: 取自既有文本、曲调或设计并加以改写
senses.example: The opening theme can be derived from a folk song collected in the highlands.
senses.exampleCN: 开场的主题可以追溯到高地采集来的一首民歌。
senses.why: A theme taken from a folk song is a branch diverted from an older channel.
senses.whyCN: 取自民歌的主题，是从更早水道分流出来的一支。

senses.title: Caused by a deeper feeling
senses.definition: to arise as an effect of an underlying condition or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 由某种潜在状况或情感所引出
senses.example: Much of the resentment may be derived from a sense that the promises were never kept.
senses.exampleCN: 许多怨气可能来自一种「承诺从未兑现」的感受。
senses.why: A feeling can have a source as concrete as a stream, even when that source is an old wound.
senses.whyCN: 情感也可以有像溪流一样具体的来源，哪怕那个来源是一道旧伤。

intro.en: The phrase rests on the verb derive, which Latin built from de- 'off, away' and rivus 'a stream'. The image is water drawn off from a channel, and every later sense keeps the direction of tracing back to a source.
intro.cn: 这个短语的核心是表示「取得、引水」的动词，拉丁语用表示「离开」的前缀加表示「溪流」的名词构成。意象是从水道中把水引出，后来每个义项都保留「回溯到源头」的方向。

items.en: Rivus meant a brook or a channel, and it also gave English river and rival.
items.cn: 这个词意为小溪或水道，英语的「河流」与「对手」也由它而来。

items.en: De- 'away from' plus rivus produced derivare, to lead water away from its channel, hence to divert or to trace an origin.
items.cn: 表示「离开」的前缀加「溪流」，构成「把水从水道引开」的动词，进而指「转移」与「追溯来源」。

items.en: The noun first named the act of diverting a stream, then the act of showing where a word or thing came from.
items.cn: 相应的名词先指「引开水流」的动作，后指「说明词或物的来源」这一动作。

items.en: English took the verb through French, using it for both water and words; the academic sense of logical derivation came later.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入这个动词，既用于水也用于词语；表示逻辑推导的学术义后来才出现。

items.en: The passive frame became the standard way to state a source without naming who did the tracing. The exact first citation of the frame is uncertain.
items.cn: 由系动词、过去分词加介词构成的被动框架，成为不点明追溯者、只陈述来源的标准说法。该框架最早的书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin stream root or looks close to it; the second group holds other ways of naming a source.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「溪流」词根或形近；第二组是其他交代来源的说法。

entries.definition: The active verb needs a subject: a researcher derives a formula, while the phrase describes the formula, not the researcher.
entries.definitionCN: 主动动词需要主语：研究者推导公式，而本短语描述的是公式，不是研究者。

entries.definition: The noun names the act or the recorded lineage; it does not itself take the source as its object.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「推导」这一动作或记录下来的谱系，本身不直接带出来源对象。

entries.definition: A derivative is the thing produced, as a derived word or compound; the phrase names the relation, not the product.
entries.definitionCN: 派生词或衍生物是被产生出来的东西；短语说的是关系，而不是产物。

entries.tag: same latin root no shared meaning
entries.definition: River comes from the same stream word but has nothing to do with derivation; the resemblance is etymological only.
entries.definitionCN: 「河流」出自同一个「溪流」词，但与「派生」无关，相似只在词源层面。

entries.definition: It points to the first appearance or birthplace of a thing, not to the steps by which it was obtained.
entries.definitionCN: 强调某物最初出现的地点或起点，而非取得它的步骤。

entries.definition: A vivid phrase for a result that grows out of a cause, often used for problems and feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 形象地表示结果由某原因长出，常用于问题与情绪。

entries.definition: The ordinary phrase for a source; it carries no implication of method or logical steps.
entries.definitionCN: 最普通的来源说法，不含方法或逻辑步骤之意。

entries.definition: It says what something rests on, such as data or a model, rather than where it came from.
entries.definitionCN: 说的是某物建立在什么之上，如数据或模型，而不是它从何而来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the branching stream, the dye bath, the axiom list and the port ledger.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用分叉的溪流、染缸、公理清单与港口账簿四个场景。

normal.en: A stream splits into channels: follow any channel backwards and you reach one spring.
normal.cn: 一条溪分成多股水道：顺着任一股往回走，都能到同一个泉眼。

normal.en: Dye boiled out of roots leaves the roots pale and the cloth yellow.
normal.cn: 从根里煮出染料，根变白了，布变黄了。

normal.en: Three axioms at the top of the page, one theorem at the bottom.
normal.cn: 页面顶端三条公理，底端一条定理。

normal.en: A word in a modern dictionary traced to a line in a fifteenth-century ledger.
normal.cn: 现代词典里的一个词，追到十五世纪账簿上的一行字。

normal.en: A table whose every number can be traced back to one survey sheet.
normal.cn: 表中每个数字都能追回同一张调查表。

abstract.en: To name a source is to shorten a history into one arrow.
abstract.cn: 指出一个来源，就是把一段历史压缩成一支箭头。

abstract.en: Nothing is derived from nothing: every lineage has at least one earlier line.
abstract.cn: 无中不能生有：每条谱系至少还有上一条线。

abstract.en: A word and a river share a root because both are things that flow away from a beginning.
abstract.cn: 词与河共享一个词根，因为两者都是从某个起点流走的东西。

examples.en: Many modern drugs can be derived from compounds first found in soil bacteria.
examples.cn: 许多现代药物可以追溯到最初在土壤细菌中发现的化合物。

examples.en: The estimate should be derived from the same sample used in the earlier study.
examples.cn: 这一估计应取自早先研究使用的同一份样本。

examples.en: A conclusion that can be derived from faulty premises may still be false.
examples.cn: 由错误前提推导出的结论，仍可能是错的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 迪莱夫德 弗若姆」：把「引水离渠」记成一条河从源头分出去，凡是支流都能倒着追回泉眼——这就叫源自

root: 核心动词出自拉丁语，由表示「离开」的前缀加表示「溪流」的名词构成，本义是「把水从水道引开」，引申为「追溯来源、推导」。该短语为被动固定框架，由系动词、过去分词与介词构成，来源一方置于介词之后。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one direction, backwards to a source: a word, a substance, a proof, a species, a material, a data set, an institution, a work of art, and a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都朝同一个方向回溯到源头：词语、物质、证明、物种、材料、数据、制度、作品与情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water led off from a channel, with every diverted stream still able to be traced back to the same headwater.
core.cn: 核心意象：水从水道被引开，每一股分流仍能倒着追回同一个源头。

branches.en: THE TRACED LINE: a word or a tune is followed back to an older text.
branches.cn: 回溯的线：词语或曲调被追回到更早的文本。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL CHAIN: a substance or a product is drawn out of a starting material.
branches.cn: 材料链：物质或产品从起始材料中被引出。

branches.en: THE PROOF LADDER: a conclusion is reached step by step from stated premises.
branches.cn: 证明的梯子：结论由已陈述的前提一步步达到。

branches.en: THE FAMILY TREE: a living form descends from an earlier population.
branches.cn: 家系树：现存的生物形态由更早的种群传下。

branches.en: THE RECORD AND THE FEELING: numbers come from one survey, rules from an older code, resentment from an old wound.
branches.cn: 记录与感受：数字来自同一份调查，规则来自旧法典，怨气来自旧伤口。

intro.en: The family is built on a Latin stream word; the prefix points away from the channel and the endings build the acts and the products of tracing.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语「溪流」一词上；前缀指「离开水道」，词尾则构成追溯的动作与产物。

latinIntro.en: Latin rivus and derivare passed through French into English, where the noun and adjective endings were added.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「溪流」与「引出」经法语进入英语，英语又加上名词与形容词词尾。

items.example: It marks the water as led away from its channel.
items.exampleCN: 它标出水流被从水道引开。

items.example: The source image of flowing water.
items.exampleCN: 这是「流动之水」的源意象。

items.meaning: to lead water off, to divert
items.example: The verb behind the whole English family.
items.exampleCN: 整个英语词族背后的动词。

items.example: The stem of the noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 表示过程的名词所用词干。

items.example: It forms the noun of the act of deriving.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「推导动作」的名词。

items.example: It forms the word for the produced item.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「被产出之物」的词。

items.example: It forms the adjective for what can be derived.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「可被推导」的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成与过程相关的形容词。

derivatives.zh: 核心动词，义为「取得；推导；起源」
由动词加过程名词尾构成，义为「推导；词源」
由动词加表示产物的词尾构成，义为「派生词；衍生物」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可推导的」

definition_zh: 安全；保障措施；保安；证券
definition_en: the state of being safe from harm; measures that protect people or property; a financial document that proves ownership
core_image: 门口站岗的保安与上锁的保险库，一切都被守护着
scene: 演唱会前场馆加强了人员检查，观众都感到踏实。 The airport raised its security before the holiday rush.
sceneCN: 这里 security 是「安保措施」（第 2 个义项：为防危险而采取的行动）；句意是机场在假期高峰前提升了安保级别。

pos.zh: 安全；安保；证券

derivatives.zh: security 的动词与形容词同根形式，义为「使安全；牢固的」
加 -ize 动词后缀，义为「把资产证券化」
加否定前缀 in-，义为「不安全感」

senses.title: The state of being safe
senses.definition: the condition of not being in danger or of not being attacked
senses.definitionCN: 没有危险、不被攻击的处境
senses.example: The treaty promised security for both nations.
senses.exampleCN: 条约承诺保障两国的安全。
senses.why: The locked vault means nothing inside gets hurt — the calm state after protection.
senses.whyCN: 上锁的金库意味着里面的东西毫发无损——被保护后的安稳状态。

senses.title: Measures that protect people or things
senses.definition: actions and systems designed to prevent crime, attack, or loss
senses.definitionCN: 为防犯罪、袭击或损失而设计的行动与制度
senses.example: Show your passport at the security check.
senses.exampleCN: 在安检处出示护照。
senses.why: The guards, locks and cameras are the active version of the locked door.
senses.whyCN: 保安、门锁与摄像头就是「那扇锁着的门」的动态版本。

senses.title: People who guard a place
senses.definition: people employed to watch over a building or event
senses.definitionCN: 受雇看守建筑或活动的人员
senses.example: Security stopped him at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 保安在入口处拦住了他。
senses.why: The protectors themselves take the name of what they provide.
senses.whyCN: 守护者以他们所提供的东西为名。

senses.title: Money or property pledged for a loan
senses.definition: assets promised to a lender in case the debt is not repaid
senses.definitionCN: 为贷款提供的资产，若不还债即被收走
senses.example: He offered his house as security for the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿房子为贷款作抵押。
senses.why: What is locked in the vault can be claimed if promises break.
senses.whyCN: 金库里锁着的东西，一旦承诺落空便可被取走。

senses.title: Financial instruments that prove ownership
senses.definition: documents such as stocks and bonds that show investment or debt
senses.definitionCN: 股票、债券等表明投资或债权关系的凭证
senses.example: Government securities are considered very safe investments.
senses.exampleCN: 政府证券被视为非常安全的投资。
senses.why: A pledged promise in writing becomes a tradable object — safety turned into paper.
senses.whyCN: 被抵押的书面承诺变成可交易的对象——安全感被写成了纸。

intro.en: From Latin securitas, the noun form of securus (free from care).
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 securitas，即 securus（无忧的）的名词形式。

items.en: The root behind Latin cura again means to care or pay attention.
items.cn: 与拉丁语 cura 同源的重构词根，仍表「留意、操心」。

items.en: Securitas means freedom from care and danger, formed from securus with the noun ending -tas.
items.cn: 拉丁语 securitas 由 securus 加名词后缀 -tas 构成，意为「无忧无险」。

items.en: Old French seurte carried the meaning of safety and certainty.
items.cn: 古法语 seurte 承载了安全与确定之义。

items.en: Forms like seurete reached England through law and commerce.
items.cn: seurete 等形式经法律与商业渠道传入英格兰。

items.en: English security first meant freedom from care, then protection and legal pledge.
items.cn: 英语 security 先表「无忧」，后发展出保护与法律担保义。

items.en: Modern use spans safety, guarding services, collateral, and financial securities.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖安全、安保服务、抵押品与金融证券。

note.en: Look-alikes around the -urity spelling, and nearby words in the protection field.
note.cn: -urity 拼写附近的形近词，以及保护义场的近义词。

entries.definition: the desire to learn or know
entries.definitionCN: 好奇心——与 security 拼写相近且同含 cura 词源，但语义相反方向：一个向外探，一个向内守

entries.definition: the state of being unknown or unclear
entries.definitionCN: 晦涩；无名——拼写与 security 相近，但词根不同，注意区分

entries.definition: a person or thing that guarantees a promise
entries.definitionCN: 保证人；担保——与 security 的抵押义项直接同源

entries.definition: the condition of being safe from harm
entries.definitionCN: 安全——泛指无危险，security 更强调主动的防护体系

entries.definition: the act of keeping someone or something safe
entries.definitionCN: 保护——强调动作，security 既指状态也指制度

entries.definition: a formal promise that something will happen
entries.definitionCN: 担保——与抵押义项相近，但 guarantee 偏承诺，security 偏实物

normalIntro.en: Hooks anchored in the -ity noun ending and the guard-at-the-door picture.
normalIntro.cn: 锚定在 -ity 名词后缀与门口保安画面上的记忆钩子。

normal.en: secure + -ity: the noun form of secure
normal.cn: secure 加 -ity 就是它的名词形式

normal.en: curiosity and security share the cura root but pull opposite ways
normal.cn: curiosity 与 security 同源却方向相反：一个好奇外探，一个守成

normal.en: the airport guard is the human face of this word
normal.cn: 机场保安就是这个词的人格化形象

normal.en: securities in finance are assets locked in as guarantees
normal.cn: 金融里的 securities 是被锁进来作担保的资产

normal.en: in- flips it: insecurity is the feeling of no protection
normal.cn: 加 in- 就反转：insecurity 是失去保护的感觉

abstract.en: Picture a guard with a clipboard standing at every door
abstract.cn: 想象每个门口都站着拿登记板的保安

abstract.en: See camera lights blinking quietly over a sleeping city
abstract.cn: 看见摄像头在沉睡的城市上空静静闪烁

abstract.en: Feel the weight of the key chain in the night watchman's pocket
abstract.cn: 体会守夜人口袋里钥匙串沉甸甸的分量

examples.en: Tight security kept the ceremony running smoothly.
examples.cn: 严密的安保让典礼顺利进行。

examples.en: She sold her securities to fund the new clinic.
examples.cn: 她卖掉证券为新诊所筹资。

examples.en: A steady job gave him a sense of security.
examples.cn: 稳定的工作给了他安全感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「色库里提」——从色库（仓库）里提东西？不行，得先过保安这一关，安保与证券的意思全在里面。

root: 拉丁语 securus（无忧的）+ 名词后缀 -tas 构成 securitas「无忧无险的状态」；经古法语 seurte 进入英语。抵押与证券义由「被锁住作担保的财产」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: One picture, four uses: the calm state, the guarding system, the pledged asset, the paper claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个画面，四种用法：安稳状态、守护体系、抵押资产与纸面凭证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a guard at the vault door, everything watched and safe
core.cn: 核心意象：金库门口的保安，一切被看守、被守护

branches.en: the quiet that comes when danger is kept out
branches.cn: 危险被挡在外面后的安宁

branches.en: the guards, cameras and checks that make the calm
branches.cn: 保安、摄像头与安检共同造就这份安宁

branches.en: the vault contents promised to a lender
branches.cn: 金库里的东西被许诺给债主

branches.en: the promise turned into tradable paper
branches.cn: 承诺变成了可交易的纸

branches.en: protection and peace are two sides of one door
branches.cn: 保护与安宁是同一扇门的两面

intro.en: Nouns and verbs built from the secure family and the -ity ending.
intro.cn: 由 secure 词族与 -ity 后缀构成的名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nouns in the cura family.
latinIntro.cn: cura 词族里的拉丁名词。

items.example: Purity means the state of being pure.
items.exampleCN: purity 表示「纯净」这一状态。

items.example: Securitas was also a Roman goddess.
items.exampleCN: Securitas 还是罗马的安全女神。

items.example: Security was tight at the summit.
items.exampleCN: 峰会安保森严。

items.example: He acted as surety for his brother.
items.exampleCN: 他为兄弟作保。

items.example: Curiosity drives every scientist.
items.exampleCN: 好奇心驱动每位科学家。

items.example: His insecurity showed in his silence.
items.exampleCN: 他的不安写在沉默里。

items.example: Banks securitize their mortgage loans.
items.exampleCN: 银行把房贷证券化。

items.meaningCN: 无名；晦涩——形近但词源不同，来自 obscurus（黑暗的）
items.example: The poet lived in obscurity for years.
items.exampleCN: 这位诗人默默无闻多年。

definition_zh: 为……出力；捐资；促成；加剧；向……投稿；为……提供材料
definition_en: to give money, effort, material or a cause toward something, whether to help it or to make it worse
core_image: 一只募捐盘在门口传了一圈，回来时压着硬币、纸条与一张写满数据的卡片，盘子本身却没变重多少
scene: 社区公告栏上贴着一张修缮老桥的筹款表，往来的人在上面写下各自能出的份额。 Anyone who uses the bridge may contribute to its upkeep.
sceneCN: 这里指出钱出力帮助某项公共事务（第 1 个义项：为共同目标提供资金或资源）；句意为任何使用这座桥的人都可以为它的维护出钱出力。图中可辨识物件：筹款表、硬币、修缮中的桥、签名笔。

pos.zh: 为……出力；捐资；促成（不及物动词短语加介词，后接受益对象或结果）
向……投稿；为……撰稿（后接刊物、讨论或文集）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示行为的名词尾构成，义为「贡献；捐款；投稿」
由动词加表示施事者的词尾构成，义为「贡献者；投稿人」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「促成的；有责任的」
由分词转作形容词，义为「有所贡献的」

senses.title: Give money to a shared aim
senses.definition: to give money toward a fund, a project or a public good
senses.definitionCN: 为基金、项目或公共事业提供资金
senses.example: Each member may contribute to the repair fund according to income.
senses.exampleCN: 每位成员可以按收入情况向修缮基金捐资。
senses.why: The verb meant to allot a share alongside others; money given into a common pot is a share assigned to the whole.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「与他人一起分派份额」；放进公家的钱，就是分给整体的一份。

senses.title: Help cause a result
senses.definition: to be one of the causes that help produce an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 作为帮助产生某一结果的成因之一
senses.example: Better street lighting can contribute to a fall in night accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的路灯照明可以促成夜间事故下降。
senses.why: A share added to a total can turn the total; a street lamp adds its bit to the night's safety.
senses.whyCN: 加进总量的一份可以改变总量；路灯为夜间安全添上自己那一份。

senses.title: Add effort to a team
senses.definition: to give work or skill to a joint undertaking
senses.definitionCN: 为共同的事业提供劳动或技能
senses.example: Every student should contribute to the group's field notes.
senses.exampleCN: 每位学生都应为小组的野外记录出力。
senses.why: Field notes are a share given to a joint page.
senses.whyCN: 野外记录是交到共同页面上的一份。

senses.title: Submit writing to a publication
senses.definition: to send an article or a piece of writing for publication
senses.definitionCN: 把文章或文字作品投给刊物发表
senses.example: She may contribute to the journal only after the embargo ends.
senses.exampleCN: 她只有在禁发期结束后才能向该刊投稿。
senses.why: An article is a share handed in to an editor's common fund of pages.
senses.whyCN: 文章是交到编辑那一份公共版面里的份额。

senses.title: Supply data for research
senses.definition: to provide records or measurements that others will analyse
senses.definitionCN: 提供可供他人分析的记录或测量
senses.example: Farmers can contribute to the climate record by sending daily readings.
senses.exampleCN: 农民可以通过寄送每日读数，为气候记录提供数据。
senses.why: Daily readings are shares handed to a collective record.
senses.whyCN: 每日读数是交到集体记录里的一份份份额。

senses.title: Make a problem worse
senses.definition: to be one of the factors that intensifies an unwanted condition
senses.definitionCN: 作为使某种不良状况加剧的因素之一
senses.example: Idling engines may contribute to the smog that covers the basin.
senses.exampleCN: 空转的发动机可能加剧笼罩盆地的烟雾。
senses.why: The same frame serves help and harm: a share can be added to a good total or to a bad one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个框架既可用于帮助也可用于损害：份额可以加进好的总量，也可以加进坏的总量。

senses.title: Advance knowledge or culture
senses.definition: to add something of lasting value to a field or an art
senses.definitionCN: 为一个领域或一门艺术增添有持久价值的东西
senses.example: Translators can contribute to the survival of a minority literature.
senses.exampleCN: 译者可以为少数族裔文学的存续作出贡献。
senses.why: A translated book is a share added to a literature's common stock.
senses.whyCN: 一部译作是加进文学公共库存的一份。

senses.title: Join a discussion with views
senses.definition: to add one's views or findings to an ongoing debate
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的看法或发现加进正在进行的讨论
senses.example: Observers may contribute to the debate without voting.
senses.exampleCN: 观察员可以参与讨论而不参加表决。
senses.why: A view offered in debate is a share put into a common pot of argument.
senses.whyCN: 讨论中提出的看法，是放进公共论证锅里的一份。

senses.title: Pay into a fund over time
senses.definition: to make regular payments into a pension or insurance fund
senses.definitionCN: 定期向养老金或保险基金缴款
senses.example: Employees should contribute to the pension plan from their first month.
senses.exampleCN: 雇员应从第一个月起向养老金计划缴存。
senses.why: A monthly payment into a pension is a share handed over before it is needed.
senses.whyCN: 每月缴进养老金的钱，是在需要之前就交出去的一份。

intro.en: The phrase rests on a Latin verb built from together plus allot. Its root sense is a share assigned alongside others, which is why the same phrase can help a project, feed a debate or worsen a problem.
intro.cn: 这个短语的核心是拉丁语中由「一起」加「分派」构成的动词。其本义是「与他人一起分得的一份份额」，因此同一短语既能帮助项目，也能喂给讨论，或加剧一个问题。

items.en: Tribus named a division of the Roman people, and the word is usually explained as a threefold division, a reconstructed form rather than a recorded one.
items.cn: 这个词指罗马人民的一个分部，通常被解释为「三分之划分」，但那是重构形式，并非有记录的原形。

items.en: From the noun came tribuere, to allot, to assign a share, to grant.
items.cn: 由该名词产生「分派、分配一份、给予」的动词。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus tribuere produced contribuere, to bring shares together into one common fund.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的前缀加「分派」，构成「把各份汇到一起」的动词。

items.en: French contribuer and English contribute both carried the sense of joining one's share to a common sum.
items.cn: 法语与英语的形式都保留了「把自己的份额加进公共总额」的意思。

items.en: With to, the phrase points either at the recipient or at the result, which is how helping and worsening share one form. The exact first citation is uncertain, and the deeper origin of the division word is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 带介词时，这个短语或指接受者，或指结果，帮助与加剧因此共用一种形式。最早书证年代不确定；表示「分部」的那个词更早的来源属重构形式。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin allotting root, including a word that looks similar but distributes rather than gathers; the second group holds other ways of adding to something.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「分派」词根，其中还包括一个形近却表示「分发」而非「汇集」的词；第二组是其他表示「增添」的说法。

entries.definition: It names the share given; the phrase names the act of giving it toward something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「所给出的那份」；短语指「把它给向某物」这一动作。

entries.definition: It names the giver, including a writer who sends an article; the phrase has no person in it.
entries.definitionCN: 指给予者，也包括投稿的作者；短语本身不含「人」。

entries.definition: From dis- 'apart' plus the same allotting verb: it sends shares outward instead of gathering them in.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「分开」的前缀加同一个「分派」动词：它把份额分发出去，而不是汇拢进来。

entries.definition: From ad- 'to' plus the same verb: it assigns a cause or a quality to someone, without any gift.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「朝向」的前缀加同一个动词：把原因或性质归到某人身上，不涉及给予。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for making something larger; it can help or worsen but carries no sense of a share.
entries.definitionCN: 日常表示「使增大」的说法，可好可坏，但不含「份额」之意。

entries.definition: It marks a step in a causal chain; it does not imply that other factors are also at work.
entries.definitionCN: 标出因果链中的一步，不暗示还有其他因素在起作用。

entries.definition: It is limited to giving money or goods, usually to a charity, and cannot mean to worsen a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 限于捐钱捐物，通常给慈善机构，不能表示「加剧问题」。

entries.definition: It is the usual verb for sending an article to an editor; it says nothing about the wider effect of the work.
entries.definitionCN: 是把文章送交编辑的常用说法，不涉及作品更广泛的作用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the collection plate, the street lamp, the embargoed journal and the idling engine.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用募捐盘、路灯、禁发期的期刊与空转的发动机四个场景。

normal.en: A collection plate passed around the room, each person dropping in a share.
normal.cn: 募捐盘在屋里传一圈，每人放进自己的一份。

normal.en: A new street lamp over a crossing where cars used to meet.
normal.cn: 旧日车祸频发的路口，新装了一盏路灯。

normal.en: A farmer mailing a sheet of daily readings to a climate office.
normal.cn: 农民把一张每日读数寄给气候机构。

normal.en: An idling engine outside a school gate, adding to the haze.
normal.cn: 校门外空转的发动机，给雾霾又添一份。

normal.en: A translator keeping an old literature alive one book at a time.
normal.cn: 译者一本一本地让旧文学活下去。

abstract.en: A contribution is a share that becomes part of a sum larger than itself.
abstract.cn: 贡献是一份份额，它并入一个比自己更大的总额。

abstract.en: The same gesture that helps can harm, because the frame asks only where the share goes.
abstract.cn: 帮助与损害可以是同一个动作，因为这个框架只问份额去了哪里。

abstract.en: Giving is not losing: the share leaves the hand and stays in the result.
abstract.cn: 给予不是失去：份额离开手，却留在结果里。

examples.en: Every household can contribute to the village well fund in small amounts.
examples.cn: 每家每户都可以小额向村井基金捐资。

examples.en: Poor ventilation may contribute to the spread of the infection indoors.
examples.cn: 通风不良可能加剧感染在室内的传播。

examples.en: Outside scholars may contribute to the volume after peer review.
examples.cn: 外部学者可以在同行评审之后向该文集投稿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「肯吹比尤特 图」：把「分一份进去」记成募捐盘传一圈，每人都放一份——份额汇进去，就有了贡献

root: 核心动词出自拉丁语，由表示「一起」的前缀加表示「分派份额」的动词构成，本义是「把各份汇到一起」，引申为「贡献、促成、投稿、缴存」。表示「份额」的那一名词更早的来源属重构形式，未有定论。该短语后接介词，既可指接受者，也可指结果。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses give a share toward something: money, a cause, team effort, an article, data, a worse problem, culture, a debate, and a pension fund.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把一份东西给向某处：钱、成因、团队劳动、文章、数据、更糟的问题、文化、讨论与养老基金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a collection plate passed around, returning loaded with coins, notes and a data card while the plate itself is barely heavier.
core.cn: 核心意象：募捐盘传了一圈，回来时压着硬币、纸条与数据卡，盘子本身却几乎没变重。

branches.en: THE COMMON PURSE: a repair fund and a pension plan both collect regular shares.
branches.cn: 公共钱袋：修缮基金与养老金都收集定期份额。

branches.en: THE CAUSAL SHARE: a street lamp lowers accidents, an idling engine raises smog.
branches.cn: 因果份额：路灯减少事故，空转发动机增加雾霾。

branches.en: THE WORK GIVEN: field notes and translated books are labour added to a lasting whole.
branches.cn: 给出的劳动：野外记录与译作都是加进持久整体的劳动。

branches.en: THE PAGE AND THE PODIUM: an article sent to a journal, a view added to a debate.
branches.cn: 版面与讲台：投给期刊的文章，加进讨论的看法。

branches.en: THE DATA GIFT: daily readings handed over for others to analyse.
branches.cn: 数据之赠：交出每日读数，供他人分析。

intro.en: The family is built on a Latin allotting verb; the prefix gathers shares, while other prefixes scatter or assign them.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语「分派」动词上；前缀把份额汇拢，别的前缀则把份额散开或归到某处。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribuere and contribuere reached French and then English, which added its own noun and agent endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「分派」与「汇合」动词进入法语，再进入英语，英语又加上自己的名词与施事词尾。

items.example: It gathers the shares into one fund.
items.exampleCN: 它把各份汇进同一个基金。

items.example: The noun behind the allotting verb.
items.exampleCN: 「分派」动词背后的名词。

items.example: The giving verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: 词族中的「给予」动词。

items.example: The direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms the noun of the share given.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「所给份额」的名词。

items.example: It forms the word for the giver.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「给予者」的词。

items.example: It forms the adjective for what helps cause a result.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「起促成作用」的形容词。

items.example: It points the share at its recipient or result.
items.exampleCN: 它把份额指向接受者或结果。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加行为名词尾构成，义为「贡献；捐款」
由动词加施事词尾构成，义为「贡献者；投稿人」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「促成的」
由分词转作形容词，义为「有贡献的」

definition_zh: 根除；消灭；杜绝；连根拔除
definition_en: to remove something harmful completely, including its source or roots
core_image: 田里一株病草被连根拔出，根须完整地带出土，地面上只留下一个干净的坑
scene: 防疫队把最后一批病例追踪到位，之后三年没有再出现新发。 The campaign aims to eradicate the disease from the whole region.
sceneCN: 这里指把疾病从源头彻底清除（第 1 个义项：根除疾病）；句意为这场运动的目标是在全区根除这种病。图中可辨识物件：连根拔起的病草、拔出的根须、干净的土坑。

pos.zh: 根除；消灭；杜绝

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「根除；消灭」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「根除者；消灭者」
由该动词加「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可根除的」
由否定前缀加「可根除的」构成，义为「无法根除的」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已被根除的」

senses.title: To wipe out a disease
senses.definition: to bring a disease down to zero new cases over a wide area and keep it there
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病在大范围内降到零新增并保持下去
senses.example: Vaccination helped eradicate smallpox worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗接种帮助在全世界根除了天花。
senses.why: The image is a plant pulled out by the root, and a disease is treated as something growing in a population.
senses.whyCN: 画面是被连根拔起的植物，而疾病被当作在人群中生长之物。

senses.title: To destroy a pest
senses.definition: to remove an insect, weed or other pest completely from an area
senses.definitionCN: 把一个地区的昆虫、杂草或其他有害生物彻底清除
senses.example: The programme eradicated the beetle from the island.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目把这个岛上的甲虫彻底消灭了。
senses.why: This is the literal agricultural scene: pull the weed out, root and all.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的农事画面：连根把草拔掉。

senses.title: To eliminate poverty
senses.definition: to reduce material deprivation to a level defined as zero by a policy target
senses.definitionCN: 把物质匮乏降到政策目标所定义的零水平
senses.example: No single programme can eradicate poverty in a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 没有任何一个项目能在十年内消除贫困。
senses.why: Policy borrows the strong verb because it promises to remove the root, not just the visible part.
senses.whyCN: 政策借用了这个强动词，因为它承诺拔掉根，而不只是割掉露出地面的部分。

senses.title: To stamp out corruption
senses.definition: to remove dishonest practices from an institution so that they no longer recur
senses.definitionCN: 从机构中清除不诚实做法，使其不再反复出现
senses.example: The commission was set up to eradicate bribery in licensing.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会成立的目的是杜绝发证环节的贿赂。
senses.why: Corruption is pictured as a weed with deep roots in procedure, hence the word for rooting it out.
senses.whyCN: 腐败被想象成在程序里扎根的杂草，于是用了「连根拔」这个词。

senses.title: To abolish a practice
senses.definition: to end a custom or method completely so that it is no longer taught or used
senses.definitionCN: 彻底终止某种习俗或方法，使其不再被传授或使用
senses.example: The reform eradicated the practice of paying for referrals.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革废除了付费转介的做法。
senses.why: Practices spread like plants, and ending them fully means removing the conditions that reproduce them.
senses.whyCN: 做法像植物一样蔓延，彻底终止意味着拆掉让它繁殖的条件。

senses.title: To remove a hidden risk
senses.definition: to find and remove the underlying cause of a danger rather than its symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 找到并移除危险的深层原因，而不只是处理表象
senses.example: Inspectors eradicated the fault before the line reopened.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员在生产线重开前消除了这个隐患。
senses.why: The root is hidden underground, which is exactly why the word suits hidden causes.
senses.whyCN: 根藏在地下，这正是这个词适合「隐藏原因」的原因。

senses.title: To uproot a plant
senses.definition: to pull a plant out of the ground with its roots intact
senses.definitionCN: 把植物连根从土里拔出
senses.example: Workers eradicated the invasive reed along the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 工人沿运河连根清除了入侵的芦苇。
senses.why: This is the etymological sense in the open: e-radix means out of the root.
senses.whyCN: 这是词源义的明面：前缀加「根」就是「从根里出来」。

senses.title: To solve a problem at its root
senses.definition: to deal with the cause of a problem so that it cannot return
senses.definitionCN: 处理问题的成因，使它无法再回来
senses.example: The redesign eradicated the vibration instead of damping it.
senses.exampleCN: 重新设计从根本上消除了振动，而不是把它压住。
senses.why: Damping treats the symptom, uprooting treats the cause, and the verb belongs to the second.
senses.whyCN: 阻尼处理症状，拔根处理病因，这个词属于后者。

intro.en: Eradicate comes from Latin eradicare, to root out, from e-, out of, and radix, root. English took it in the sixteenth century for both plants and evils.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 eradicare「连根拔除」，由 e-「出」与 radix「根」构成；英语十六世纪引入，既用于植物，也用于祸害。

items.en: Radix meant root, and it also gave English radical, radish and the mathematical root.
items.cn: 这个词意为「根」，还给出「根本的」「萝卜」以及数学上的根等词。

items.en: The prefix e- is a form of ex, meaning out of, and it marks removal from the inside.
items.cn: 前缀 e- 是 ex 的一种形式，意为「出」，标出从内部取走。

items.en: The verb meant to pull up by the roots, and farmers used it of vines and trees before writers used it of vices.
items.cn: 这个动词意为连根拔起，农人先用它说藤与树，文人后来才用它说恶习。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain and is usually given only as that century.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪采用这个动词，确切首见年代不确定，通常只给「十六世纪」。

items.en: Public health and reform movements extended the verb to disease, poverty and corruption.
items.cn: 公共卫生与改革运动把这个动词扩展到疾病、贫困与腐败。

items.en: Radical, radish and eradicate all point back to the same Latin word for root, though each took a different road.
items.cn: 「根本的」「萝卜」与本词都回到同一个表示「根」的拉丁词，只是各走一条路。

note.en: The first group shares the root word or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of complete removal.
note.cn: 第一组与「eradicate」共享「根」这个词或只是形近；第二组是与「彻底清除」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of removing something completely.
entries.definitionCN: 指彻底清除这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: An adjective for something that cannot be rooted out.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指无法根除的。

entries.definition: Going to the root, from the same Latin word for root.
entries.definitionCN: 指根本的、激进的，同出「根」这个词。

entries.definition: The vegetable named from the same root word.
entries.definitionCN: 这种蔬菜的名字同出「根」这个词。

entries.definition: To send out rays, from radius, a spoke; it looks close but is a different stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指放射，出自「辐条」；形近但词干不同。

entries.definition: To remove something completely, often by taking it out of a set.
entries.definitionCN: 指彻底去除，常指从一组中剔除。

entries.definition: To destroy a group of living things entirely, usually pests.
entries.definitionCN: 指彻底消灭一群生物，多指害虫。

entries.definition: To end a law, system or practice officially.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式废除法律、制度或做法。

entries.definition: To destroy something completely, in plainer speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指彻底摧毁，口语色彩更强。

entries.definition: To end something bad by firm action, as if stepping on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指以坚决行动扑灭坏事，像用脚踩灭。

entries.definition: To take something away, without promising that it cannot return.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物拿走，不保证不会再来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the root word inside the verb, its plant family and the public campaigns that made it famous.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用动词内部那个「根」词、它的植物同族词，以及让它出名的公共卫生运动。

normal.en: Radix is root, so eradicate is literally to take something out by the root.
normal.cn: radix 是「根」，所以这个词字面就是连根取出。

normal.en: Radical, radish and eradicate all trace back to the same root word.
normal.cn: radical、radish、eradicate 都回到同一个「根」词。

normal.en: Public health speaks of eradicating a disease, never of merely controlling it.
normal.cn: 公共卫生说根除疾病，而不只是控制它。

normal.en: Ineradicable is the negative adjective: a habit that cannot be rooted out.
normal.cn: 「无法根除的」是否定形容词：拔不掉的习惯。

normal.en: A weed is eradicated, a symptom is treated, and the word insists on the difference.
normal.cn: 杂草被根除，症状被治疗，这个词坚持这个区别。

abstract.en: To eradicate is to refuse the compromise of cutting the stem and leaving the root.
abstract.cn: 根除，就是拒绝「割茎留根」这种妥协。

abstract.en: What grows back was never eradicated, only trimmed.
abstract.cn: 会再长出来的东西从来没有被根除，只是被修剪过。

abstract.en: The deepest causes are the ones no one can see, which is why the word begins underground.
abstract.cn: 最深的成因没人看得见，所以这个词从地下开始。

examples.en: The region eradicated malaria within a single generation.
examples.cn: 该地区在一代人之内根除了疟疾。

examples.en: Gardeners eradicated the knotweed before it reached the river.
examples.cn: 园丁在节节草到达河边之前就把它连根清除了。

examples.en: The reform did not eradicate the practice, but it made it rare.
examples.cn: 改革没有杜绝这种做法，但让它变得少见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「伊拉德凯特」——手一拽，根须完整出土：根除、消灭

root: 拉丁语 radix「根」→ eradicare「连根拔除」（e-「出」+ radicare「扎根」）；英语十六世纪引入。与 radius「辐条」不同源（radiate 属另一词干）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all pull something up by the root: disease, pests, poverty, corruption, a practice, a hidden fault, a plant and a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把某物连根拔起：疾病、害虫、贫困、腐败、做法、隐患、植物与成因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a diseased weed comes out with its full root, leaving a clean hole in the soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：病草带着完整的根被拔出，土里留下一个干净的坑。

branches.en: THE EPIDEMIC ENDS: new cases fall to zero and stay there.
branches.cn: 流行病终结：新增病例降到零并保持。

branches.en: THE PLANT IS PULLED: a pest or a weed leaves the ground with its roots intact.
branches.cn: 植物被拔起：害虫或杂草带着完整的根离开土地。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN ROOT: poverty and unseen faults are attacked below the surface.
branches.cn: 隐藏的根：贫困与看不见的隐患在地表之下被处理。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION IS CLEANED: bribery stops reproducing itself inside procedure.
branches.cn: 机构被清理：贿赂不再在程序内部自我繁殖。

branches.en: THE SOURCE IS REMOVED: a custom or a problem loses the conditions that kept it alive.
branches.cn: 源头被移除：习俗或问题失去让它存活的那些条件。

intro.en: Eradicate is a Latin verb built on the word for root, and the same root appears in radical and radish.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在「根」这个词上的拉丁动词，同一词根也出现在 radical 与 radish 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies radix, radicari and eradicare; the family is well recorded, so no part of the word is marked uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 radix、radicari、eradicare；这一族有清楚记录，这个词没有哪一部分标为存疑。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词指植物的地下部分。

items.example: The verb named the plant's settling into soil.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指植物在土里安身。

items.example: It marks removal from within.
items.exampleCN: 它标出从内部取出。

items.example: The verb combined removal with the root.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「取出」与「根」合在一起。

items.example: It marks the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它标明英语动词。

items.example: It forms eradication.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 eradicator。

definition_zh: 激怒；挑衅；引发；引起；煽动
definition_en: to stir someone into anger or action, or to cause a reaction or an event
core_image: 有人把一根长杆伸进静止的水面，圈圈波纹从杆尖向外荡开
scene: 这份提案把两边的旧账都翻了出来，会上争了两个小时。 The proposal provoked a long debate in the council.
sceneCN: 这里指引起一场争论（第 3 个义项：引发反应或讨论）；句意为这份提案在议会引发了长时间辩论。图中可辨识物件：伸进水面的长杆、向外荡开的波纹、静止的水；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 激怒；挑衅；引发；引起

由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「挑衅的；煽动的；引人深思的」
